summary.en: King Jangsu of Goguryeo raised a 6-metre stone stele near the capital Gungnae (modern Ji'an) to commemorate his father Gwanggaeto. Its roughly 1,800 characters record the dynasty's origins and Gwanggaeto's campaigns and are a key source for early relations between Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla and Wa.
summary.zh: 高句丽长寿王在国内城（今集安）附近立起高约六米的石碑，纪念其父广开土王。碑文约一千八百字，记述王室起源与广开土王的征战，是研究高句丽、百济、新罗与倭早期关系的重要史料。

sources.title: Gwanggaeto Stele inscription (414)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Capital Cities and Tombs of the Ancient Koguryo Kingdom
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Gwanggaeto Stele

summary.en: Goguryeo general Eulji Mundeok lured a large Sui expeditionary force deep into the peninsula and destroyed it as it retreated across the Salsu (probably the Cheongcheon River). The disaster crippled Emperor Yang's campaigns against Goguryeo.
summary.zh: 高句丽将领乙支文德诱使隋朝远征大军深入，并在其撤退渡过萨水（一般认为即清川江）时予以重创。此役使隋炀帝征讨高句丽的战争严重受挫。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Suishu (Book of Sui, 636), annals of Emperor Yang
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Battle of Salsu

note: Wikidata gives no coordinates; the Salsu is usually identified with the Cheongcheon River near Anju, and Sui troop numbers in the sources are probably exaggerated.

summary.en: A set of moral and political injunctions for officials, drawing on Confucian and Buddhist ideals, which the Nihon Shoki attributes to Prince Shōtoku in 604. It stresses harmony, reverence for Buddhism and obedience to the sovereign.
summary.zh: 据《日本书纪》记载，圣德太子于604年制定了这一针对官员的道德与政治训诫，融合儒家与佛教思想，强调“以和为贵”、崇敬佛法、服从君主。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Seventeen-article constitution
Nihon Shoki (720), trans. W. G. Aston, Nihongi (1896)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Seventeen-article constitution

note: Known only from the Nihon Shoki (720); its date and Shōtoku's authorship are debated by historians.

summary.en: After the overthrow of the Soga clan in 645, Prince Naka no Ōe and Nakatomi no Kamatari launched reforms under Emperor Kōtoku modelled on Tang China: land and people were declared the sovereign's, and a centralised bureaucracy and tax system were planned from the new palace at Naniwa.
summary.zh: 645年苏我氏被推翻后，中大兄皇子与中臣镰足在孝德天皇治下仿效唐朝推行改革，宣布土地与人民归于天皇，并以难波新宫为中心筹划中央集权的官僚与税制。

sources.title: Nihon Shoki (720), trans. W. G. Aston, Nihongi (1896)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Taika Reform

note: The wording of the 646 reform edict in the Nihon Shoki was probably revised later; the real pace of reform is debated.

story.en:
On a summer day in 645, during a ceremony at the Itabuki palace in Asuka where envoys from the Korean kingdoms were supposedly being received, Prince Naka no Ōe and his ally Nakatomi no Kamatari cut down Soga no Iruka in front of the empress. The Soga had dominated the court for three generations. The next day Iruka's father Emishi set fire to his own house and died; according to the chronicle a court history burned with it, though one chronicle was saved from the flames.

The new emperor Kōtoku moved the court to Naniwa and adopted Japan's first era name, Taika, "great change". The reform edict issued on New Year's Day 646 declared that all land and people belonged to the sovereign, and called for household registers, the allotment of rice fields and uniform taxes on the Tang model.

Historians now think the Nihon shoki's compilers polished the edict's wording with later laws, and the system was built over the next half-century. Kamatari was granted the surname Fujiwara on his deathbed in 669; his descendants would rule the court for centuries.
story.zh:
645年夏天的一日，在飞鸟板盖宫举行的仪式上，据称是在接见朝鲜诸国的使者，中大兄皇子与盟友中臣镰足当着女皇的面砍杀了苏我入鹿。苏我氏已经把持朝政三代。次日，入鹿之父苏我虾夷焚宅自尽；据史书记载，一部国史随之被焚，只有一部国记从火中抢出。

新即位的孝德天皇把朝廷迁到难波，并采用日本第一个年号“大化”，意为“大变革”。646年元旦颁布的改新之诏宣布天下土地和人民均归天皇所有，并要求仿照唐制编制户籍、班给田地、统一赋税。

现代史学家认为，《日本书纪》的编者曾用后来的律令润色了诏书文字，这套制度实际上是在此后半个世纪中逐步建立的。669年，镰足临终时获赐“藤原”之姓；他的子孙此后数百年间主宰着朝廷。

name.en: Battle of Hwangsanbeol and fall of Baekje
name.zh: 黄山伐之战与百济灭亡

summary.en: Baekje general Gyebaek made a last stand against the Silla army of Kim Yu-sin at Hwangsanbeol while a Tang fleet landed in the west. The Baekje capital Sabi fell soon after and King Uija surrendered.
summary.zh: 百济将领阶伯在黄山伐迎战金庾信率领的新罗军，最终战死，同时唐朝水军在西海岸登陆。不久百济都城泗沘陷落，义慈王投降。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Battle of Hwangsanbeol

note: Battlefield location near Nonsan is approximate (Wikidata gives none).

summary.en: A Yamato fleet sent to restore Baekje was destroyed by Tang and Silla naval forces at the mouth of the Baekgang (Geum River). The defeat ended Baekje restoration hopes and led Japan to fortify its western coasts.
summary.zh: 倭国派遣水军援助百济复国，在白江口（今锦江入海口）被唐朝与新罗联军击败。此役终结了百济复国的希望，也促使日本在西部沿海修筑防御工事。

sources.title: Nihon Shoki (720), trans. W. G. Aston, Nihongi (1896)
Jiu Tangshu (Old Book of Tang, 945), "Biography of Liu Rengui" and "Account of Baekje"
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Battle of Baekgang

story.en:
When Tang and Silla destroyed Baekje in 660, Baekje loyalists asked Yamato to send home Prince Buyeo Pung, who had lived at the Japanese court for decades, and to help restore the kingdom. Empress Saimei, nearly seventy, travelled to Kyushu to direct the expedition and died there in 661; her son, the future Emperor Tenji, carried it on.

In late August 663 the Yamato fleet reached the mouth of the Baekgang, the lower Geum River, where a Tang squadron lay waiting. The Chinese histories say the Japanese attacked four times in disordered waves and lost four hundred ships, and that the smoke and flames rose to the sky and the sea turned red. Prince Pung fled to Goguryeo; the Baekje fortress of Juryu surrendered soon after.

The defeat frightened Yamato into building defences: a great earth dike at Mizuki in front of Dazaifu, Korean-style mountain forts and beacons from Tsushima to the Inland Sea. Baekje refugees brought skills and learning to Japan, and in 667 Tenji moved his capital inland to Ōmi.
story.zh:
660年唐与新罗灭百济后，百济的复国势力请求大和送回在日本朝廷生活了数十年的王子扶余丰，并出兵助其复国。年近七十的齐明天皇亲赴九州指挥远征，661年死于当地；其子、后来的天智天皇继续推进这一事业。

663年8月下旬，大和船队抵达白江口，即锦江下游，唐朝水军早已严阵以待。据中国史书记载，倭军队形混乱地四次进攻，损失船只四百艘，烟焰涨天，海水皆赤。王子扶余丰逃往高句丽，百济的周留城不久投降。

这场惨败使大和惊恐不已，开始大修防御工事：在大宰府前修筑巨大的水城土堤，建造朝鲜式山城，并从对马到濑户内海设置烽火台。百济遗民把技艺和学问带到日本；667年，天智天皇把都城迁到内陆的近江。

name.en: Goguryeo–Tang War and fall of Pyongyang
name.zh: 唐与高句丽战争及平壤陷落

summary.en: After repeated Tang invasions from 645, an allied Tang–Silla army besieged Pyongyang in 668 and captured King Bojang, ending Goguryeo after some seven centuries. Tang set up the Protectorate General to Pacify the East in its former capital.
summary.zh: 唐朝自645年起多次进攻高句丽，668年唐与新罗联军围攻平壤，俘获宝藏王，高句丽灭亡。唐朝随后在平壤设立安东都护府。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Goguryeo–Tang War

story.en:
Goguryeo had already destroyed the armies of the Sui. In 642 the general Yeon Gaesomun murdered King Yeongnyu and some hundred officials and ruled as military dictator through the puppet King Bojang. Emperor Taizong of Tang invaded in 645, took several fortresses in Liaodong and besieged Ansi for about two months, but autumn came, supplies ran low, and he withdrew, reportedly regretting the campaign. Korean tradition later named Ansi's defender as Yang Manchun.

Tang raids continued for twenty years without success. Then Yeon Gaesomun died in 666 and his sons quarrelled: the eldest, Namsaeng, driven from Pyongyang by his brothers, went over to the Tang and showed them the way. In 668 the Tang general Li Ji and Silla's army converged on Pyongyang, which fell after a month's siege when a monk opened the gates.

King Bojang was taken to Chang'an, and large numbers of Goguryeo families were deported into China. Within thirty years, a former Goguryeo officer, Dae Jo-yeong, would found Balhae in the old northern lands.
story.zh:
高句丽曾经击溃隋朝的大军。642年，将军渊盖苏文杀死荣留王及百余名大臣，以傀儡宝藏王为名实行军事独裁。645年唐太宗亲征，攻下辽东数城，围攻安市城约两个月；然而秋天来临、粮草不继，他只得撤军，据说对此役深感懊悔。后来的朝鲜传说称安市城主为杨万春。

此后二十年间，唐军屡次进犯均未成功。666年渊盖苏文去世，其子之间发生内讧：长子渊男生被弟弟们逐出平壤，投降唐朝并为唐军引路。668年，唐将李勣与新罗军会攻平壤，围城一月后，一名僧人打开城门，平壤陷落。

宝藏王被押往长安，大批高句丽家族被迁入中国内地。不到三十年，原高句丽将领大祚荣就在北方故地建立了渤海国。

summary.en: Having helped Tang destroy Baekje and Goguryeo, Silla turned on its ally when Tang tried to rule the peninsula directly. Victories at Maeso fortress (675) and Gibeolpo (676) forced Tang to withdraw, leaving Silla master of the peninsula south of the Taedong River.
summary.zh: 新罗协助唐朝灭百济与高句丽后，因唐欲直接统治半岛而与之反目。675年买肖城之战与676年伎伐浦海战获胜后，唐军撤退，新罗控制了大同江以南的半岛。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Silla–Tang War

story.en:
Silla had invited the Tang into the peninsula to destroy its rivals, but the Tang had its own plans. It set up protectorates in the former lands of Baekje and Goguryeo and even named King Munmu of Silla governor of a Tang "area command", as if Silla were a province.

From 670 Munmu fought back. Silla backed Goguryeo restoration rebels, seized the Baekje territories, and at the Maeso fortress north of the Han River in 675 routed a Tang army; the Samguk sagi says Silla captured some 30,000 horses. In 676 Silla ships won a series of battles at Gibeolpo at the mouth of the Geum, and the Tang moved its Protectorate General to Pacify the East back to Liaodong.

Silla now ruled the peninsula south of the Taedong River. Munmu, worried about the Japanese, asked to be cremated and buried in the sea so that he could become a dragon guarding the coast; a rock islet off Gyeongju, Daewangam, is traditionally his tomb.
story.zh:
新罗请唐军进入半岛消灭对手，但唐朝另有打算。它在百济和高句丽故地设立都督府和都护府，甚至任命新罗文武王为唐朝“鸡林州大都督”，仿佛新罗只是唐的一个州。

670年起，文武王展开反击。新罗支持高句丽复国势力，夺取百济故地，675年在汉江以北的买肖城大败唐军；据《三国史记》记载，新罗缴获战马约三万匹。676年，新罗水军在锦江口的伎伐浦连战连胜，唐朝把安东都护府撤回辽东。

此后新罗统治了大同江以南的半岛。文武王担心倭人来犯，遗命火葬后葬于海中，以化为护国之龙守卫海岸；庆州外海的礁石大王岩，相传就是他的陵墓。

summary.en: Empress Genmei moved the court to Heijō-kyō (Nara), a grid-planned capital modelled on Tang Chang'an. It gave its name to the Nara period and, apart from 740–745, remained the capital until 784.
summary.zh: 元明天皇将都城迁至仿照唐长安城棋盘式规划的平城京（今奈良）。奈良时代因此得名，除740至745年外，此地一直为都城，直至784年。

sources.title: Shoku Nihongi (797)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Heijō-kyō

story.en:
Empress Genmei moved the court in 710 to a new city on the northern edge of the Nara basin, laid out like a scaled-down Chang'an. A broad avenue, the Suzaku-ōji, about 70 metres wide, ran south from the palace gate between a grid of blocks covering roughly 4 by 5 kilometres, with an eastern extension where Kōfuku-ji and later Tōdai-ji rose. Perhaps 50,000 to 100,000 people lived there, officials, monks, labourers and the households serving them.

Archaeologists have recovered hundreds of thousands of mokkan, wooden tags and memos, from the palace ditches: labels on tribute of salt, seaweed and abalone from distant provinces, and notes ordering rice for workers. They show the new bureaucracy at work.

The capital was not stable. Amid rebellion and epidemic, Emperor Shōmu moved the court between Kuni, Naniwa and Shigaraki from 740 to 745 before returning. In 784 Emperor Kanmu left for Nagaoka, and the palace became rice fields. Its site, with the reconstructed Suzaku Gate and Former Audience Hall, is part of a World Heritage property.
story.zh:
710年，元明天皇把朝廷迁到奈良盆地北缘的新都城，其布局仿佛缩小版的长安。宽约70米的朱雀大路从宫城正门向南延伸，两侧是约4公里乘5公里的棋盘式街区，东侧还有外京，兴福寺以及后来的东大寺就建在那里。城中大约居住着五万至十万人，包括官员、僧侣、劳役和为他们服务的家人。

考古学家从宫城的沟渠中出土了数十万枚木简，即木制的标签和便条：有远方诸国进贡的盐、海藻和鲍鱼的货签，也有为劳工支取口粮的文书。它们展现了新官僚体制的实际运作。

这座都城并不安稳。740年至745年间，因叛乱和瘟疫，圣武天皇先后迁都恭仁、难波和紫香乐，然后才回到平城。784年桓武天皇迁往长冈京，宫城旧址变为稻田。如今遗址上复原的朱雀门和第一次大极殿，是世界遗产的组成部分。

summary.en: Ō no Yasumaro presented the Kojiki, Japan's oldest surviving chronicle, to Empress Genmei. It narrates the creation myths and the genealogy of the imperial line up to Empress Suiko.
summary.zh: 太安万侣向元明天皇献上《古事记》，这是现存最古老的日本史书，记述了创世神话及至推古天皇为止的皇室谱系。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kojiki
Donald L. Philippi (trans.), Kojiki (University of Tokyo Press, 1968)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Kojiki

summary.en: Emperor Shōmu's colossal bronze Vairocana Buddha at Tōdai-ji, the head temple of the provincial temple network, was ceremonially "eye-opened" in 752 before monks from across Asia.
summary.zh: 圣武天皇下令铸造的东大寺卢舍那大佛于752年举行开眼供养法会，来自亚洲各地的僧侣参加。东大寺是全国国分寺体系的总寺。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tōdai Temple
Shoku Nihongi (797)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara
Wikipedia: Tōdai-ji

summary.en: According to the Samguk yusa, the Silla minister Kim Dae-seong began the artificial granite grotto of Seokguram on Mount Toham in 751, together with Bulguksa temple below. Its seated Buddha is a masterpiece of East Asian Buddhist sculpture.
summary.zh: 据《三国遗事》记载，新罗宰相金大城于751年在吐含山开始营建人工花岗岩石窟石窟庵，并同时修建山下的佛国寺。窟内本尊坐佛是东亚佛教雕塑的杰作。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sokkuram
Iryeon, Samguk yusa (Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms, c. 1281)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Seokguram Grotto and Bulguksa Temple
Wikipedia: Seokguram

note: The 751 start and 774 completion follow the Samguk yusa.

summary.en: Emperor Kanmu moved the court from Nagaoka to the new grid-planned capital of Heian-kyō, modern Kyoto. It remained the imperial capital until 1869 and gave its name to the Heian period.
summary.zh: 桓武天皇将朝廷从长冈京迁至新建的棋盘式都城平安京，即今京都。此后直到1869年这里一直是天皇所在的都城，平安时代亦由此得名。

sources.title: The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 2: Heian Japan (1999)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto (Kyoto, Uji and Otsu Cities)
Wikipedia: Heian-kyō

story.en:
Emperor Kanmu wanted to escape Nara, where the great monasteries meddled in politics. His first new capital, Nagaoka, begun in 784, was cursed by misfortune: its builder Fujiwara no Tanetsugu was assassinated in 785, the emperor's brother Prince Sawara, accused of the plot, died on his way to exile, and floods and deaths in the imperial family followed. Diviners blamed Sawara's angry spirit.

In 794 Kanmu moved again, a few kilometres northeast, to a site between two rivers with mountains on three sides, and named it Heian-kyō, "capital of peace and tranquillity". It was laid out on a grid of about 4.5 by 5.2 kilometres, with the Rashōmon gate at the south. Only two official temples, Tō-ji and Sai-ji, were allowed inside.

The western half was marshy and soon emptied, and the city grew eastward toward the Kamo River. For more than a thousand years, through fires, wars and the rise of shoguns in Kamakura and Edo, Kyoto remained the emperor's home until Emperor Meiji left for Tokyo in 1869.
story.zh:
桓武天皇想要摆脱奈良，那里的大寺院干预朝政。784年他开始营建的第一座新都长冈京却厄运连连：负责营建的藤原种继于785年遇刺，被指控参与此事的天皇之弟早良亲王在流放途中死去，此后洪水泛滥、皇室成员接连亡故。占卜者把这些归咎于早良亲王的怨灵。

794年，桓武再次迁都，迁往东北方向几公里外一处两河之间、三面环山的地方，并命名为“平安京”，意为和平安宁之都。都城按约4.5公里乘5.2公里的棋盘格布局，南端是罗城门。城内只允许建造东寺和西寺两座官寺。

西半部地势低湿，很快衰落，城市向东朝鸭川方向发展。此后一千多年间，历经火灾、战乱以及镰仓和江户幕府的兴起，京都一直是天皇的居所，直到1869年明治天皇移居东京。

name.en: Later Three Kingdoms and Goryeo reunification
name.zh: 后三国时代与高丽统一

summary.en: As Silla weakened, rebel states Later Baekje and Taebong (Later Goguryeo) arose. Wang Geon, who founded Goryeo in 918, accepted Silla's surrender in 935 and defeated Later Baekje at Illicheon in 936, reuniting the peninsula.
summary.zh: 新罗衰落后，后百济与泰封（后高句丽）相继崛起。918年建立高丽的王建于935年接受新罗归降，936年在一利川击败后百济，重新统一朝鲜半岛。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Later Three Kingdoms
Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Goryeosa (History of Goryeo, 1451)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Later Three Kingdoms

story.en:
By the late 9th century Silla's court in Gyeongju had lost control of the provinces. When the government of Queen Jinseong pressed for overdue taxes in 889, peasants rose across the country, and local strongmen built their own armies. Gyeon Hwon, a Silla officer, proclaimed Later Baekje in the southwest; the one-eyed monk Gung Ye founded Later Goguryeo in the north. In 918 Gung Ye's generals overthrew him and made Wang Geon king of a new state, Goryeo.

The three-way war was brutal. In 927 Gyeon Hwon stormed Gyeongju and forced King Gyeongae to kill himself. Wang Geon rushed to help and was nearly killed at Mount Gong near Daegu; according to tradition his general Shin Sung-gyeom put on the king's armour and died in his place so that Wang Geon could escape.

The end came through family quarrels. In 935 Gyeon Hwon's son Singeom imprisoned his father in a temple; the old king escaped to Goryeo. The last Silla king surrendered to Wang Geon the same year, and in 936, with Gyeon Hwon riding at his side, Wang Geon destroyed Later Baekje at Illicheon.
story.zh:
到9世纪末，庆州的新罗朝廷已经失去对地方的控制。889年真圣女王的朝廷催缴拖欠的赋税，农民在全国各地起事，地方豪强纷纷建立私人武装。新罗军官甄萱在西南部建立后百济；独眼僧人弓裔在北方建立后高句丽。918年，弓裔的部将推翻了他，拥立王建为新国家高丽的国王。

三方之间的战争十分残酷。927年，甄萱攻入庆州，逼迫景哀王自尽。王建赶去救援，在大邱附近的公山险些丧命；相传他的将领申崇谦换上国王的铠甲，替他战死，王建才得以脱身。

结局来自家族内讧。935年，甄萱之子神剑把父亲囚禁在寺院里，老国王逃往高丽。同年新罗末代国王向王建投降；936年，王建在甄萱的陪同下于一利川消灭了后百济。

summary.en: Murasaki Shikibu, a lady-in-waiting at the Heian court, wrote this long prose narrative of the life and loves of the "Shining Prince" Genji. It was circulating by 1008 and is often called the world's first novel.
summary.zh: 平安宫廷女官紫式部创作了这部描写“光源氏”一生与情爱的长篇物语。至1008年该书已在宫中流传，常被誉为世界上第一部长篇小说。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: The Tale of Genji
Murasaki Shikibu, Murasaki Shikibu nikki (Diary, c. 1010)
Richard Bowring, Murasaki Shikibu: The Tale of Genji (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2004)
Wikipedia: The Tale of Genji

note: Wikidata gives 1010 as inception; the earliest datable reference to the work, in Murasaki's diary, is from 1008. Composition dates are not known precisely.

story.en:
Murasaki Shikibu was the widowed daughter of a provincial governor and scholar of Chinese when, around 1005, she entered the service of Empress Shōshi, daughter of the regent Fujiwara no Michinaga. She had probably begun the Genji before that, and court ladies copied the chapters as she wrote them. Her own diary records that in 1008 the poet Fujiwara no Kintō came looking for her at a party and asked whether "our young Murasaki" was there, the jest of a reader who knew her heroine.

The Tale of Genji runs to fifty-four chapters and several hundred characters over some seventy years. It follows Genji, a son of the emperor removed from the succession, through love affairs, exile and return to power, then turns darker in the last chapters set at Uji after his death. Its attention to feeling, memory and the passing of things made it the model for Japanese literature.

Within a century it was illustrated in the Genji scrolls; it was translated into modern Japanese by Yosano Akiko and Tanizaki Jun'ichirō, and into English by Arthur Waley from 1925.
story.zh:
大约1005年，紫式部入宫侍奉摄政藤原道长之女中宫彰子。她是一位地方官兼汉学家的女儿，当时已经守寡。她很可能在入宫前就已开始写作《源氏物语》，宫中女官们随写随抄。据她本人的日记记载，1008年一次宴会上，歌人藤原公任前来找她，问“我们的小紫在吗？”，这是熟悉书中女主角的读者开的玩笑。

《源氏物语》共五十四帖，历时约七十年，出场人物数百。它讲述被排除在皇位继承之外的皇子光源氏的恋情、流放与重返权力中心，在他死后以宇治为舞台的最后数帖则转向更加阴郁的基调。作品对情感、回忆和世事无常的关注，使它成为日本文学的典范。

不到一百年，它就被绘成《源氏物语绘卷》；后来与谢野晶子和谷崎润一郎将其译成现代日语，1925年起阿瑟·韦利将其译成英文。

summary.en: From 1231 the Mongols invaded Goryeo repeatedly. The military regime moved the court to Ganghwa Island and resisted for decades while the mainland was ravaged, until Goryeo accepted vassal status in 1259.
summary.zh: 自1231年起蒙古多次入侵高丽。武臣政权将朝廷迁往江华岛，坚持抵抗数十年，本土则惨遭蹂躏，直至1259年高丽接受藩属地位。

sources.title: Goryeosa (History of Goryeo, 1451)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Mongol invasions of Korea

summary.en: During the Mongol invasions Goryeo carved the entire Buddhist canon onto more than 81,000 woodblocks, hoping for divine protection. Carved under the court in exile on Ganghwa Island and completed in 1251, the blocks were moved to Haeinsa temple in 1398, where they remain.
summary.zh: 蒙古入侵期间，高丽为祈求佛法护国，将整部大藏经刻于八万一千余块木板之上，由江华岛流亡朝廷主持，1251年完成，1398年移藏海印寺至今。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tripitaka Koreana
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Haeinsa Temple Janggyeong Panjeon, the Depositories for the Tripitaka Koreana Woodblocks
Goryeosa (History of Goryeo, 1451)
Wikipedia: Tripitaka Koreana

note: Wikidata gives an inception of 1300; standard accounts date the carving to 1236/37–1251.

summary.en: A civil war between the Taira and Minamoto warrior clans. It ended with the destruction of the Taira fleet at Dan-no-ura in 1185 and left Minamoto no Yoritomo the dominant power in Japan.
summary.zh: 平氏与源氏两大武士集团之间的内战。1185年平氏水军在坛之浦覆灭，源赖朝由此成为日本最有权势的人物。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Genpei War
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)
Azuma kagami (Mirror of the East, late 13th c.)
Wikipedia: Genpei War

story.en:
The Taira clan under Kiyomori had made itself master of the court, marrying his daughter to the emperor and placing his infant grandson Antoku on the throne in 1180. That year Prince Mochihito called on the Minamoto to rise; he was killed within weeks, but in Izu the exiled Minamoto no Yoritomo raised his banner. Defeated at Ishibashiyama, he escaped by boat and rebuilt his army among the warriors of the east, settling in Kamakura.

The Taira were weakened by famine in the west and by Kiyomori's death from fever in 1181. In 1183 Yoritomo's cousin Kiso Yoshinaka drove them from Kyoto, taking the child emperor with them; Yoritomo then sent his brothers to destroy Yoshinaka in 1184 and pursue the Taira west. Minamoto no Yoshitsune won at Ichi-no-Tani, at Yashima and finally at Dan-no-ura in 1185.

The war became the great epic of Japan. The Tale of the Heike, chanted by blind lute players, begins by reminding its listeners that the proud do not endure, and tells the fall of the Taira as a Buddhist lesson in impermanence.
story.zh:
以平清盛为首的平氏已经掌握朝廷，他把女儿嫁给天皇，并于1180年让年幼的外孙安德天皇即位。同年，以仁王号召源氏起兵；他在几周内就被杀，但流放在伊豆的源赖朝举起了旗帜。赖朝在石桥山战败，乘船逃脱，在东国武士中重建军队，并以镰仓为据点。

西国的饥荒和1181年平清盛因高热病死，削弱了平氏。1183年，赖朝的堂弟木曾义仲把平氏逐出京都，平氏带着幼帝一同西逃；1184年，赖朝派弟弟们消灭义仲，并西追平氏。源义经先后在一之谷、屋岛取胜，最终于1185年在坛之浦获得决定性胜利。

这场战争成为日本的伟大史诗。由盲眼琵琶法师吟唱的《平家物语》开篇便提醒听众，骄者必不长久，并把平氏的覆灭讲述为一则关于诸行无常的佛教寓言。

summary.en: Minamoto no Yoritomo, already ruling the warrior class from Kamakura, was appointed sei-i taishōgun in 1192. His government created a dual system in which the shogunate controlled military affairs alongside the imperial court in Kyoto.
summary.zh: 已在镰仓统领武士阶层的源赖朝于1192年被任命为征夷大将军。幕府掌握军事与地方治安，与京都朝廷并存，形成公武二元体制。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kamakura shogunate
Azuma kagami (Mirror of the East, late 13th c.)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)
Wikipedia: Kamakura shogunate

note: Historians date the regime variously from 1180, 1185 or 1192; Wikidata gives 1200. No Wikidata item exists for this event itself; Q736839 denotes the state and is linked from polity-kamakura, so no qid is set here.

story.en:
Yoritomo never moved to Kyoto. From 1180 he governed the eastern warriors from Kamakura, a small seaside town protected by hills, setting up a board of retainers, an administrative office and a court of appeals. In 1185, after the Taira fell, the retired emperor Go-Shirakawa allowed him to appoint military governors (shugo) and estate stewards (jitō) across the country, giving his vassals a share of land revenues everywhere.

In 1189 Yoritomo destroyed the Northern Fujiwara of Hiraizumi, who had sheltered his brother Yoshitsune. Only after Go-Shirakawa's death did the court grant him, in 1192, the title sei-i taishōgun, "great general who subdues the barbarians".

Yoritomo died in 1199 after a fall from his horse. His sons were weak; his widow Hōjō Masako and her family took control as regents, and after his last son Sanetomo was murdered by a nephew on the steps of the Tsurugaoka Hachiman shrine in 1219, the shoguns became figureheads. The warrior government he created, alongside the imperial court, lasted in one form or another until 1868.
story.zh:
源赖朝从未迁居京都。自1180年起，他就在三面环山、临海的小镇镰仓统治东国武士，设立了侍所、公文所（政所）和问注所。1185年平氏灭亡后，后白河法皇允许他在全国任命守护和地头，使他的家臣在各地都能分享庄园收益。

1189年，赖朝消灭了曾庇护其弟义经的平泉奥州藤原氏。直到后白河法皇去世后，朝廷才在1192年授予他“征夷大将军”的称号。

1199年赖朝坠马后去世。他的儿子们软弱无能；遗孀北条政子及其家族以执权身份掌握大权。1219年，赖朝最后一个儿子源实朝在鹤冈八幡宫的石阶上被侄子刺杀，此后将军沦为傀儡。他所开创的、与朝廷并存的武家政权，以各种形式一直延续到1868年。

summary.en: Kublai Khan's Yuan dynasty, with Goryeo ships and troops, twice invaded northern Kyushu. Both attacks at Hakata Bay were contained by samurai defenders (in 1281 also by the new coastal wall), and storms—later called kamikaze—wrecked much of the 1281 fleet.
summary.zh: 忽必烈的元朝联合高丽船只与兵力两次进攻九州北部。两次在博多湾的登陆都被武士阻挡（1281年另有新筑的石垒），1281年的庞大舰队更多被台风（后称“神风”）摧毁。

label.en: Battle of Bun'ei at Hakata Bay

label.zh: 江南军自庆元（宁波）出发

label.en: Battle of Kōan at Hakata Bay

label.zh: 台风在鹰岛海域摧毁舰队

sources.title: Thomas D. Conlan, In Little Need of Divine Intervention: Takezaki Suenaga's Scrolls of the Mongol Invasions of Japan (Cornell, 2001)
Yuanshi (History of Yuan, 1370), "Account of Japan" (Riben zhuan)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)
Wikipedia: Mongol invasions of Japan

story.en:
Kublai Khan sent letters from 1268 inviting Japan to submit. The young regent Hōjō Tokimune did not reply, and later had envoys beheaded. In November 1274 a Mongol, Chinese and Korean force of perhaps 25,000 to 30,000 men in some 900 Goryeo-built ships ravaged Tsushima and Iki and landed at Hakata Bay. The samurai, used to single combat, faced massed archers and exploding iron bombs, both shown in the scroll painted for the warrior Takezaki Suenaga. After a day of fighting the invaders re-embarked and sailed home, losing many ships to bad weather.

Japan built a stone wall some 20 kilometres long around Hakata Bay. In 1281 two fleets came, one from Korea and a far larger one from southern China, perhaps 140,000 men in all. Kept off the beaches by the wall and harried by night raids on their ships, they were still at anchor off Takashima when a typhoon struck in August and destroyed much of the fleet.

The storms were later called kamikaze, "divine winds". Since 2011 archaeologists have found wrecks of the 1281 fleet in Imari Bay.
story.zh:
自1268年起，忽必烈多次致书日本，要求其臣服。年轻的执权北条时宗不予答复，后来还斩杀了元朝使节。1274年11月，一支由蒙古人、汉人和高丽人组成、约二万五千至三万人的军队，乘坐约九百艘高丽建造的船只，蹂躏对马和壹岐后在博多湾登陆。习惯一骑讨的武士面对的是密集的弓箭手和会爆炸的铁炮，这两者都见于为武士竹崎季长绘制的《蒙古袭来绘词》。激战一日后，入侵者登船返航，途中因恶劣天气损失了许多船只。

日本在博多湾沿岸修筑了长约20公里的石墙。1281年，两支舰队来犯，一支从朝鲜出发，另一支规模大得多的从中国江南出发，总兵力或达十四万。被石墙挡在滩头之外，又在夜间屡遭袭击，元军舰队8月仍停泊在鹰岛海面时，一场台风袭来，摧毁了大部分船只。

这些风暴后来被称为“神风”。2011年以来，考古学家在伊万里湾发现了1281年元军舰队的沉船。

name.zh: 《直指心体要节》金属活字印刷

summary.en: Monks at Heungdeok temple in Cheongju printed this anthology of Seon (Zen) teachings with movable metal type. The surviving volume, held in the Bibliothèque nationale de France, is the oldest extant book printed this way.
summary.zh: 清州兴德寺僧人用金属活字印行这部禅宗语录选集。现存的一卷藏于法国国家图书馆，是世界上现存最早的金属活字印本。

sources.title: UNESCO Memory of the World Register: Baegun hwasang chorok buljo jikji simche yojeol (vol. II)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Jikji

summary.en: General Yi Seong-gye, who had turned his army back at Wihwa Island in 1388 and taken power, deposed the last Goryeo king and was enthroned as King Taejo in Gaegyeong. He renamed the state Joseon and moved the capital to Hanseong (Seoul) in 1394.
summary.zh: 1388年威化岛回军后掌握大权的将军李成桂，于1392年废黜高丽末代国王，在开京即位为太祖。他改国号为朝鲜，并于1394年迁都汉城（今首尔）。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Chosŏn dynasty
Annals of the Joseon Dynasty (Joseon wangjo sillok), National Institute of Korean History
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Joseon

note: No Wikidata item exists for this event itself; Q28179 denotes the state and is linked from polity-joseon, so no qid is set here.

story.en:
After the Wihwado retreat in 1388, Yi Seong-gye and the reformers around him held power in Kaesong, but the respected scholar-official Jeong Mong-ju remained loyal to Goryeo. Tradition says that Yi's son Bang-won tested him with a poem asking why they should not intertwine like vines; Jeong answered with a poem saying that even if he died a hundred times, his heart would not change. In 1392 Bang-won's men killed him on the Seonjuk Bridge in Kaesong.

Three months later the last Goryeo king, Gongyang, was deposed, and Yi was enthroned. He asked the Ming emperor to choose a name for the new state; Hongwu picked Joseon, the name of the ancient kingdom of Gija and Dangun legend. In 1394 the court moved to Hanyang, where Jeong Do-jeon planned the palace, shrines and walls of the new capital.

The new state rested on Neo-Confucianism: Buddhist monasteries lost land, and the examination-educated yangban became the ruling class. The dynasty Yi founded lasted 518 years, one of the longest in world history.
story.zh:
1388年威化岛回军之后，李成桂及其周围的改革派在开京掌握了大权，但德高望重的儒臣郑梦周仍然效忠高丽。相传李成桂之子李芳远曾以一首诗试探他，问何不像藤蔓一样彼此缠绕；郑梦周以一首诗作答，说纵然死一百次，丹心也不会改变。1392年，李芳远的手下在开京善竹桥上将他杀害。

三个月后，高丽末代国王恭让王被废，李成桂即位。他请明朝皇帝为新国家选定国号；洪武帝选中了“朝鲜”，这是传说中檀君和箕子古国的名称。1394年朝廷迁到汉阳，郑道传规划了新都的宫殿、宗庙、社稷和城墙。

新王朝以性理学立国：佛教寺院失去土地，经科举培养的两班成为统治阶层。李成桂开创的这个王朝延续了518年，是世界历史上最长久的王朝之一。

summary.en: King Sejong completed a new phonetic alphabet in 1443 and promulgated it in 1446 in the document Hunminjeongeum, "the correct sounds for instructing the people", so that commoners could read and write Korean.
summary.zh: 世宗大王于1443年创制了一套新的表音文字，并于1446年以《训民正音》（意为“教百姓以正确的字音”）颁布，使平民也能读写朝鲜语。

sources.title: Annals of the Joseon Dynasty (Joseon wangjo sillok), National Institute of Korean History
UNESCO Memory of the World Register: Hunmin Chongum Manuscript
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Hunminjeongeum

story.en:
Fifteenth-century Koreans wrote in classical Chinese, which took years to learn; most people could not read at all. In the winter of 1443 King Sejong announced a script of twenty-eight letters. Its consonants were drawn from the shape of the mouth, tongue and throat as they make each sound, and its vowels from three symbols for heaven, earth and humankind, combined into syllable blocks.

The king's preface says he pitied the people who had something to say but could not write it down. Not everyone agreed: in 1444 the scholar Choe Man-ri petitioned that abandoning Chinese characters would make Korea a barbarian country. Sejong had him briefly jailed and went ahead. The script was promulgated in 1446 in the Hunminjeongeum, with an explanatory volume by scholars of the Hall of Worthies.

The elite kept writing in Chinese for centuries, and King Yeonsan banned the script in 1504 after anonymous posters criticised him in it. Women, commoners and popular novels kept it alive. An original copy of the 1446 explanatory edition was found in Andong in 1940; it is now a UNESCO Memory of the World document, and 9 October is Hangul Day.
story.zh:
15世纪的朝鲜人用文言汉文书写，学习需要多年，绝大多数人根本不识字。1443年冬，世宗宣布创制了一套二十八个字母的文字。辅音字母仿照发音时口、舌、喉的形状，元音字母则由象征天、地、人的三个符号构成，再组合成音节方块。

世宗在序言中说，他怜悯那些有话要说却无法写下来的百姓。并非人人都赞同：1444年，学者崔万理上疏称，舍弃汉字会使朝鲜沦为夷狄之邦。世宗把他短暂下狱，坚持推行。1446年，这套文字以《训民正音》之名颁布，集贤殿学士们还为其撰写了解说本。

此后几百年间，士大夫仍用汉文写作；1504年，有人用谚文写匿名告示批评燕山君，他随即禁用此文字。是女性、平民和通俗小说使它得以流传。1940年，在安东发现了1446年解例本的原本，如今已列入联合国教科文组织《世界记忆名录》，10月9日被定为韩文日。

summary.en: A succession dispute in the Ashikaga shogunate drew the Hosokawa and Yamana coalitions into a decade of fighting that burned much of Kyoto. The shogunate never recovered its authority, opening the Sengoku (Warring States) era.
summary.zh: 足利将军家的继嗣纷争使细川与山名两大阵营在京都激战十年，城市大半焚毁。幕府权威一蹶不振，日本由此进入战国时代。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ōnin War
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Ōnin War

note: Coordinates set on Kyoto, where the fighting took place; the Wikidata point lies about 17 km to the south.

story.en:
The eighth Ashikaga shogun, Yoshimasa, preferred tea, gardens and painting to government. Childless, he named his brother Yoshimi as heir in 1464, and the next year his wife Hino Tomiko bore a son. Each claimant found a patron among the great lords: Hosokawa Katsumoto, leading the Eastern Army, and his father-in-law Yamana Sōzen, leading the Western Army. Succession disputes in the Hatakeyama and Shiba houses added fuel.

Fighting broke out in Kyoto in 1467 and turned the capital into a battlefield of trenches and burned temples. Light infantry called ashigaru, recruited from the urban poor, looted at will. Both commanders died in 1473, yet the armies fought on until 1477, when the lords simply went home with nothing decided.

Much of Kyoto lay in ashes, and the shogun's authority over the provinces was gone. Yoshimasa retired to build his Silver Pavilion in the eastern hills, where tea ceremony, ink painting and rock gardens flourished, while across Japan provincial warlords fought for a century in the age of Warring States.
story.zh:
室町幕府第八代将军足利义政更喜欢茶道、庭园和绘画，而非政务。他膝下无子，于1464年立弟弟义视为继承人，次年其妻日野富子却生下一子。两位继承人各自在大名中找到了靠山：率领东军的细川胜元，以及他的岳父、率领西军的山名宗全。畠山氏和斯波氏的家督之争更是火上浇油。

1467年战火在京都燃起，把都城变成了到处是壕沟和焚毁寺院的战场。从城市贫民中招募的轻装步兵“足轨”肆意劫掠。1473年两位主帅相继去世，双方却仍然打到1477年，最后大名们各自回国，什么也没有解决。

京都大半化为灰烬，将军对地方的统治权丧失殆尽。义政隐退到东山营建银阁，茶道、水墨画和枯山水庭园在那里兴盛起来；而在日本各地，地方豪强进入了长达一个世纪的战国时代。

summary.en: Oda Nobunaga, with a small force, surprised and killed the daimyō Imagawa Yoshimoto, whose much larger army was marching through Owari. The victory launched Nobunaga's rise as a unifier of Japan.
summary.zh: 织田信长以少量兵力奇袭行军经过尾张的今川义元大军，并斩杀义元。此役使信长崛起，开始统一日本的进程。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Okehazama
Jeroen P. Lamers, Japonius Tyrannus: The Japanese Warlord Oda Nobunaga Reconsidered (Hotei, 2000)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Wikipedia: Battle of Okehazama

name.zh: 壬辰倭乱（万历朝鲜战争）

summary.en: Toyotomi Hideyoshi sent some 150,000 troops into Joseon in 1592, aiming ultimately at Ming China. After rapid Japanese advances, Ming intervention, guerrilla resistance and Yi Sun-sin's navy stalled the campaign; a second invasion in 1597 ended with Hideyoshi's death and withdrawal in 1598.
summary.zh: 1592年丰臣秀吉派遣约十五万大军入侵朝鲜，最终目标是明朝。日军初期推进迅速，但明军援朝、义兵抗击与李舜臣水军使战事陷入僵局；1597年再度入侵，1598年秀吉死后日军撤退。

label.zh: 肥前名护屋城：出兵基地

label.en: Yi Sun-sin wins at Hansan Island

sources.title: Kenneth M. Swope, A Dragon's Head and a Serpent's Tail: Ming China and the First Great East Asian War, 1592–1598 (University of Oklahoma Press, 2009)
Stephen Turnbull, Samurai Invasion: Japan's Korean War 1592–98 (Cassell, 2002)
Yu Seong-ryong, Jingbirok (Book of Corrections, c. 1604)
Wikipedia: Imjin War

story.en:
On 23 May 1592 the first Japanese division under Konishi Yukinaga landed at Busan; the fortress fell the next day and Dongnae the day after. Armed with matchlocks and hardened by a century of civil war, the invaders reached Seoul within three weeks. King Seonjo fled north to Uiju on the Chinese border, and angry crowds burned palace buildings and the slave registers behind him.

The tide turned in three ways. At sea, Yi Sun-sin's fleet, including his armoured turtle ships, cut the Japanese supply route along the south coast. On land, righteous armies of local gentry, peasants and monks, among them the "Red-Robed General" Gwak Jae-u and the monk Hyujeong, harried the occupiers. And in early 1593 a Ming army under Li Rusong retook Pyongyang. The Japanese withdrew to forts on the south coast while years of negotiations failed.

Hideyoshi invaded again in 1597, but his death in September 1598 ended the war; at Noryang, covering the Japanese retreat, Yi Sun-sin was killed. Korea had lost perhaps a million or more people. Thousands of Koreans, among them the potters who founded Arita ware, were taken to Japan, and the Mimizuka mound in Kyoto holds noses cut from Korean dead.
story.zh:
1592年5月23日，小西行长率领的日军第一军在釜山登陆，次日釜山镇陷落，再一日东莱失守。手持火绳枪、历经百年内战磨炼的入侵者三周内就攻到汉城。宣祖北逃至中朝边境的义州，愤怒的民众在他身后焚烧宫殿和奴婢文书。

战局从三个方面发生逆转。在海上，李舜臣的舰队，包括他的装甲龟船，切断了日军沿南海岸的补给线。在陆上，由地方士绅、农民和僧侣组成的义兵，如“红衣将军”郭再祐和僧人休静，不断袭扰占领军。1593年初，李如松率领的明军收复平壤。日军退守南海岸的倭城，多年的和谈始终未果。

1597年丰臣秀吉再度出兵，但他于1598年9月去世，战争随之结束；在掩护日军撤退的露梁海战中，李舜臣战死。朝鲜大约损失了一百万甚至更多人口。数以千计的朝鲜人被掳往日本，其中包括开创有田烧的陶工；京都的耳冢中埋着从朝鲜死者身上割下的鼻子。

summary.en: Admiral Yi Sun-sin lured a Japanese fleet into open water near Hansan Island and enveloped it in a "crane-wing" formation, sinking or capturing most of the ships. The victory cut Japanese sea supply along Korea's southern coast.
summary.zh: 李舜臣将日本舰队诱至闲山岛附近的开阔海域，以“鹤翼阵”合围，击沉或俘获大部分敌船。此役切断了日军沿朝鲜南海岸的海上补给线。

sources.title: Yi Sun-sin, Nanjung ilgi (War Diary, 1592–1598)
Stephen Turnbull, Samurai Invasion: Japan's Korean War 1592–98 (Cassell, 2002)
Wikipedia: Battle of Hansan Island

summary.en: With only 13 warships left after the Joseon navy's disaster at Chilcheollyang, Yi Sun-sin used the fierce tidal currents of the Myeongnyang Strait to repel a Japanese fleet many times larger, halting the Japanese advance by sea.
summary.zh: 朝鲜水军在漆川梁惨败后，李舜臣仅余十三艘战船，他利用鸣梁海峡湍急的潮流，击退数倍于己的日本舰队，阻止了日军的海上推进。

sources.title: Yi Sun-sin, Nanjung ilgi (War Diary, 1592–1598)
Kenneth M. Swope, A Dragon's Head and a Serpent's Tail: Ming China and the First Great East Asian War, 1592–1598 (University of Oklahoma Press, 2009)
Wikipedia: Battle of Myeongnyang

story.en:
In the summer of 1597 Yi Sun-sin was in disgrace, stripped of command after court intrigues and made to serve as a common soldier, while his successor Won Gyun led the Joseon fleet to destruction at Chilcheollyang. Restored to command, Yi gathered the few surviving ships. When the court suggested he give up the sea and fight on land, he replied, in a famous memorial, that he still had twelve warships, and that as long as he lived the enemy would not dare to despise Joseon.

On 26 October 1597 he waited at the Myeongnyang Strait between Jindo and the mainland, where the tide runs at up to ten knots. More than a hundred Japanese warships entered on the flood. For an hour his flagship fought almost alone while his captains hung back; then the tide turned, the Japanese ships jammed together in the narrows, and the Korean ships closed in. Yi's war diary says 31 enemy ships were destroyed; the body of the Japanese commander Kurushima Michifusa was hauled from the water and hung from the mast.

The Japanese gave up their plan to sail up the west coast. The battle became Korea's great story of defiance and, in 2014, its most-watched film.
story.zh:
1597年夏，李舜臣因朝廷倾轧被革职，以白衣从军；继任者元均率领的朝鲜水军在漆川梁全军覆没。李舜臣复职后收拢残存的几艘战船。朝廷建议他放弃水战、改在陆上作战，他在一篇著名的奏疏中答道：臣尚有十二艘战船，只要臣一息尚存，敌人就不敢轻视朝鲜。

1597年10月26日，他在珍岛与陆地之间的鸣梁海峡等候敌军，那里的潮流速度可达每小时十节。一百多艘日本战船乘涨潮驶入。一个小时里，他的旗舰几乎孤军奋战，其他将领踌躇不前；随后潮流转向，日本战船在狭窄的水道中挤作一团，朝鲜战船纷纷围上来。据李舜臣的《乱中日记》记载，击毁敌船三十一艘；日本将领来岛通总的尸体被从水中捞起，悬挂在桅杆上。

日军放弃了沿西海岸北上的计划。这场战斗成为朝鲜最伟大的抗争故事，2014年拍成的电影是韩国史上观影人次最多的影片。

summary.en: Tokugawa Ieyasu's Eastern Army defeated the Western Army led by Ishida Mitsunari, helped by defections during the battle. The victory made Ieyasu master of Japan; he became shogun in 1603.
summary.zh: 德川家康率领的东军在战场倒戈的帮助下击败石田三成为首的西军。此役使家康成为日本实际的统治者，并于1603年就任征夷大将军。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Sekigahara
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Battle of Sekigahara

story.en:
Hideyoshi died in 1598 leaving a five-year-old heir, Hideyori, and a council of five great lords to govern for him. The greatest of them, Tokugawa Ieyasu, began acting as ruler; the administrator Ishida Mitsunari organised a coalition against him. In the autumn of 1600 the two armies, about 75,000 in the East and over 80,000 in the West, met in the narrow valley of Sekigahara, where the Nakasendō highway crosses the mountains between Mino and Ōmi.

The battle began in fog on the morning of 21 October. The Western Army held strong positions on the hills, but many of its lords had already been in secret contact with Ieyasu. Kobayakawa Hideaki, commanding 15,000 men on Mount Matsuo, waited until midday before attacking the Western flank; tradition says Ieyasu's guns fired at his position to force a decision. Other lords followed his lead, and the Western line collapsed. The Shimazu cut their way out straight through the enemy.

Mitsunari was captured and beheaded in Kyoto. Ieyasu's son Hidetada arrived too late, delayed by the Sanada at Ueda Castle. Ieyasu redistributed a third of Japan's lands and became shogun in 1603.
story.zh:
1598年丰臣秀吉去世，留下五岁的继承人丰臣秀赖和五大老辅政。五大老中实力最强的德川家康开始以天下人自居；奉行石田三成则组织联军与之对抗。1600年秋，东军约七万五千人与西军八万余人在关原相遇。关原是一条狭窄的山谷，中山道在此穿越美浓与近江之间的山地。

10月21日清晨，战斗在浓雾中打响。西军占据山上的有利阵地，但其中许多大名早已与家康暗中往来。在松尾山上统率一万五千人的小早川秀秋一直观望到正午，才转而攻击西军侧翼；传说是家康命令铁炮队向他的阵地射击，逼他表态。其他大名纷纷效仿，西军阵线崩溃。岛津军则从敌阵正中突围而出。

石田三成被俘，在京都被斩首。家康之子德川秀忠在上田城被真田氏拖住，未能赶上决战。家康重新分配了全国三分之一的领地，并于1603年就任征夷大将军。

summary.en: In two winter and summer campaigns the Tokugawa besieged Osaka Castle, the last stronghold of Toyotomi Hideyori. Its fall in 1615 destroyed the Toyotomi line and secured Tokugawa rule for two and a half centuries.
summary.zh: 德川方分冬、夏两阵围攻丰臣秀赖的最后据点大坂城。1615年城陷，丰臣氏灭亡，德川统治由此稳固了两个半世纪。

sources.title: The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Siege of Osaka

summary.en: Overtaxed peasants and masterless samurai of Shimabara and Amakusa, many of them Christian, rose and held Hara Castle until it fell to a shogunal army in 1638. The revolt hardened the ban on Christianity and the exclusion of the Portuguese.
summary.zh: 岛原与天草地区不堪重税的农民和浪人（多为天主教徒）起事，据守原城，1638年被幕府大军攻陷。此后幕府更加严厉地禁教，并驱逐葡萄牙人。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Shimabara Rebellion
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Ronald P. Toby, State and Diplomacy in Early Modern Japan (Princeton University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Shimabara Rebellion

summary.en: A series of Tokugawa edicts in the 1630s banned Japanese from travelling abroad, expelled the Portuguese and confined Dutch trade to Dejima in Nagasaki. Controlled contacts continued with China, Korea, the Ryukyus and the Ainu until the 1850s.
summary.zh: 17世纪30年代德川幕府颁布一系列法令，禁止日本人出海、驱逐葡萄牙人，并将荷兰贸易限制在长崎出岛。与中国、朝鲜、琉球及阿伊努的有限往来则一直持续到19世纪50年代。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: sakoku
Ronald P. Toby, State and Diplomacy in Early Modern Japan (Princeton University Press, 1984)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Wikipedia: Sakoku

note: The term sakoku was coined only in 1801; historians debate how closed Japan really was.

story.en:
The policy took shape in stages. The Tokugawa feared Christianity as a foreign loyalty and the Spanish and Portuguese as possible invaders. From 1633 a series of edicts forbade Japanese ships to sail abroad and, from 1635, any Japanese who had lived overseas to return on pain of death. After the Shimabara rebellion of 1637–38, which the shogunate blamed on Christians, the Portuguese were expelled in 1639. When a Portuguese embassy came from Macao in 1640 to plead for trade, most of its members were executed.

Japan was not sealed. Contacts ran through four gates: the Dutch and Chinese at Nagasaki, Korea through the Tsushima domain, the Ryukyu kingdom through Satsuma, and the Ainu through Matsumae. Silver, copper, silk, sugar, medicines and books kept arriving, and suspected Christians were made to tread on holy images.

The word sakoku, "closed country", was coined only in 1801 by the interpreter Shizuki Tadao, translating an essay by Engelbert Kaempfer. Many historians now prefer to speak of maritime restrictions, a system of controlled foreign relations that lasted until Perry.
story.zh:
这一政策是分阶段形成的。德川幕府把天主教视为对外国的效忠，又担心西班牙和葡萄牙会入侵日本。从1633年起，一系列禁令禁止日本船只出海；1635年起，凡在海外居住过的日本人回国一律处死。1637至1638年的岛原之乱被幕府归咎于天主教徒，此后葡萄牙人于1639年被驱逐。1640年，一个葡萄牙使团从澳门前来请求恢复贸易，大部分成员遭到处决。

日本并未完全封闭。对外联系通过“四口”进行：长崎的荷兰人和中国人、经对马藩往来的朝鲜、经萨摩藩往来的琉球王国，以及经松前藩往来的阿伊努人。白银、铜、生丝、砂糖、药材和书籍源源不断地进出，被怀疑信奉天主教的人则被强迫踩踏圣像（踏绘）。

“锁国”一词直到1801年才由通词志筑忠雄在翻译坎普弗尔的一篇文章时创造出来。如今许多史学家更愿意称之为“海禁”，即一套延续到佩里来航为止的受控对外关系体系。

summary.en: US Commodore Matthew Perry anchored his "black ships" off Uraga in 1853 and returned in 1854 to obtain the Convention of Kanagawa, which opened two ports to American ships and ended Japan's policy of seclusion.
summary.zh: 1853年美国海军准将佩里率“黑船”驶抵浦贺，1854年再次来航，迫使幕府签订《神奈川条约》，开放两个港口供美国船只停靠，日本锁国政策就此终结。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Perry Expedition
Francis L. Hawks, Narrative of the Expedition of an American Squadron to the China Seas and Japan (1856)
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)
Wikipedia: Perry Expedition

story.en:
On 8 July 1853 four American warships, two of them steam frigates belching smoke, anchored off Uraga at the mouth of Edo Bay. Commodore Matthew Perry refused to go to Nagasaki, the only port where foreigners were received, and threatened to force his way to Edo if no one accepted President Fillmore's letter asking for coal, provisions, protection of shipwrecked sailors and trade. Officials accepted it at Kurihama and Perry left, promising to return.

The senior councillor Abe Masahiro took the unprecedented step of asking the daimyo, and even commoners, for their opinions. A popular comic poem punned on jōkisen, a premium tea and "steamship", saying that four cups had made it impossible to sleep. When Perry returned in February 1854 with a larger squadron, the shogunate signed the Convention of Kanagawa on 31 March, opening Shimoda and Hakodate.

Perry's gifts included a quarter-size steam locomotive and a telegraph, which officials rode and tested on the beach. The 1858 Harris treaty that followed opened trade ports on unequal terms and set off the crisis that destroyed the shogunate within fifteen years.
story.zh:
1853年7月8日，四艘美国军舰在江户湾口的浦贺海面下锚，其中两艘是冒着黑烟的蒸汽巡洋舰。马修·佩里准将拒绝前往唯一接待外国人的长崎，并扬言如果无人接受菲尔莫尔总统的国书，他就强行驶向江户。国书要求日本提供煤炭和补给、保护遇难船员并开展贸易。幕府官员在久里滨接受了国书，佩里承诺来年再来，随即离去。

老中阿部正弘破天荒地征询大名乃至平民的意见。当时一首流行的狂歌用双关语“上喜撰”（一种名茶，与“蒸汽船”同音）调侃说，只喝了四杯便彻夜难眠。1854年2月佩里率领更大的舰队返回，幕府于3月31日签订《神奈川条约》，开放下田和箱馆两港。

佩里带来的礼物中有一台四分之一比例的蒸汽机车模型和一套电报机，官员们在海滩上试乘、试验。随后1858年的《哈里斯条约》以不平等条件开放通商口岸，引发了一场在十五年内摧毁幕府的危机。

summary.en: Samurai from Satsuma and Chōshū proclaimed the restoration of imperial rule in Kyoto on 3 January 1868 and defeated the shogunate in the Boshin War. The new government abolished the domains and samurai privileges and set Japan on a course of rapid modernisation.
summary.zh: 1868年1月3日，萨摩、长州等藩的武士在京都宣布“王政复古”，并在戊辰战争中击败幕府。新政府废藩置县、废除武士特权，使日本走上迅速现代化的道路。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Meiji Restoration
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 5: The Nineteenth Century (1989)
Wikipedia: Meiji Restoration

story.en:
On 3 January 1868 troops of Satsuma and allied domains seized the gates of the Kyoto palace, and the fifteen-year-old Emperor Meiji proclaimed the restoration of imperial rule. The young samurai behind the coup, among them Ōkubo Toshimichi, Saigō Takamori and Kido Takayoshi, won the Boshin War against the shogunate and then set out to remake the country.

In April 1868 the emperor swore the Charter Oath, promising that deliberative assemblies would be established and that knowledge would be sought throughout the world. In the autumn Edo became Tokyo, the "eastern capital", and the emperor moved into the shogun's castle. In 1871, in a single day, the 260-odd domains were abolished and replaced by prefectures run by appointed governors. Conscription in 1873 ended the samurai monopoly of arms, and in 1876 they lost the right to wear swords and their stipends.

The slogan "rich country, strong army" guided railways, telegraphs, factories, schools and a new army and navy. Within a generation Japan had a constitution and was fighting China; by 1905 it had defeated Russia.
story.zh:
1868年1月3日，萨摩及其同盟诸藩的军队控制了京都皇宫各门，十五岁的明治天皇宣布王政复古。策划这次政变的年轻武士包括大久保利通、西乡隆盛和木户孝允，他们在戊辰战争中击败幕府，随即着手改造国家。

1868年4月，天皇颁布《五条誓文》，承诺“广兴会议”，并“求知识于世界”。同年秋天江户改称东京，天皇迁入将军的城堡。1871年，全国二百六十多个藩在一天之内被废除，代之以由中央任命知事的县。1873年的征兵令打破了武士对武力的垄断，1876年武士又失去了佩刀权和俸禄。

“富国强兵”的口号指引着铁路、电报、工厂、学校以及新式陆海军的建设。不到一代人时间，日本就有了宪法，并与中国开战；到1905年，它已经打败了俄国。

summary.en: After a gunboat confrontation off Ganghwa Island, Japan forced Joseon to sign its first modern, unequal treaty, opening three ports and granting Japanese extraterritoriality. It ended Korea's seclusion and its exclusive tributary ties to Qing China.
summary.zh: 在江华岛炮舰冲突之后，日本迫使朝鲜签订第一个近代不平等条约，开放三处港口并给予日本领事裁判权。条约打破了朝鲜的闭关状态及其与清朝的宗藩关系。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Treaty of Ganghwa
Peter Duus, The Abacus and the Sword: The Japanese Penetration of Korea, 1895–1910 (University of California Press, 1995)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Japan–Korea Treaty of 1876

name.zh: 东学农民运动（甲午农民战争）

summary.en: Peasants led by followers of the Donghak religion rose against corrupt officials in Jeolla province in 1894. The Joseon court's appeal for Qing troops prompted Japan to send its own, triggering the First Sino-Japanese War; the rebels were crushed by early 1895.
summary.zh: 1894年，东学道信徒领导全罗道农民反抗贪官污吏。朝鲜朝廷请求清军援助，日本亦借机出兵，引发甲午中日战争；起义军于1895年初被镇压。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Donghak Peasant Revolution
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Tonghak Peasant Revolution

summary.en: Rivalry over Manchuria and Korea led Japan to attack the Russian fleet at Port Arthur in 1904. Japanese victories on land at Mukden and at sea at Tsushima produced the Treaty of Portsmouth, the first defeat of a European great power by an Asian state in modern times.
summary.zh: 日俄两国因争夺中国东北与朝鲜而交恶，1904年日本突袭旅顺口的俄国舰队。日本在奉天陆战与对马海战中获胜，双方签订《朴次茅斯条约》，这是近代亚洲国家首次击败欧洲列强。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Russo-Japanese War
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 6: The Twentieth Century (1988)
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)
Wikipedia: Russo-Japanese War

story.en:
Japan had won Korea's allegiance from China in 1895 but was forced by Russia, France and Germany to give back the Liaodong peninsula, which Russia then leased for itself, building a naval base at Port Arthur and a railway across Manchuria. Talks over spheres in Korea and Manchuria failed, and on the night of 8 February 1904 Japanese torpedo boats attacked the Russian squadron at Port Arthur before war was formally declared.

The siege of Port Arthur became a foretaste of the First World War: machine guns, barbed wire and mass assaults. General Nogi Maresuke, who lost both his sons, finally took 203-Metre Hill in December, and the fortress surrendered on 2 January 1905. At Mukden in February and March more than half a million men fought for three weeks. In May the Japanese navy destroyed Russia's Baltic Fleet at Tsushima.

Both sides were exhausted, and Russia was shaken by revolution. President Theodore Roosevelt brokered the Treaty of Portsmouth in September 1905: Japan gained a free hand in Korea, the Liaodong lease, the South Manchuria railway and southern Sakhalin, but no indemnity, which set off riots in Tokyo. Across Asia, nationalists from Sun Yat-sen to the young Nehru took heart that a European empire could be beaten.
story.zh:
1895年日本从中国手中夺得了对朝鲜的控制权，却被俄、法、德三国逼迫归还辽东半岛，随后俄国自己租借了辽东，在旅顺修建海军基地，并修筑横贯中国东北的铁路。关于朝鲜和满洲势力范围的谈判破裂后，1904年2月8日夜，日本鱼雷艇在正式宣战之前就袭击了旅顺的俄国舰队。

旅顺围攻战预演了第一次世界大战的样貌：机枪、铁丝网和大规模冲锋。失去两个儿子的乃木希典将军终于在12月攻下二〇三高地，要塞于1905年1月2日投降。2月至3月的奉天会战中，五十多万人激战三周。5月，日本海军在对马海峡歼灭了俄国波罗的海舰队。

双方都已精疲力竭，俄国又因革命而动荡。1905年9月，美国总统西奥多·罗斯福促成《朴次茅斯条约》：日本获得在朝鲜的行动自由、辽东租借地、南满铁路和库页岛南部，但没有得到赔款，因而在东京引发骚乱。在整个亚洲，从孙中山到青年尼赫鲁，民族主义者都因看到欧洲帝国可以被打败而深受鼓舞。

summary.en: Admiral Tōgō Heihachirō's fleet annihilated the Russian Baltic Fleet, which had sailed halfway around the world, in the Tsushima Strait. The battle decided the Russo-Japanese War.
summary.zh: 东乡平八郎率领的日本联合舰队在对马海峡全歼远航半个地球而来的俄国波罗的海舰队，决定了日俄战争的结局。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Tsushima
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 6: The Twentieth Century (1988)
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)
Wikipedia: Battle of Tsushima

story.en:
Russia's Second Pacific Squadron left the Baltic in October 1904 for a voyage of some 18,000 nautical miles around Africa. In the North Sea its nervous gunners fired on British fishing boats, mistaking them for Japanese torpedo craft, and nearly started a war with Britain. Coaling was difficult, as few ports would receive it; by the time it reached Asia in May 1905, Port Arthur had already fallen.

Admiral Rozhestvensky tried to slip through the Tsushima Strait to Vladivostok. Admiral Tōgō Heihachirō was waiting with a faster, better-trained fleet. On 27 May he hoisted the Z flag with a signal that the fate of the empire depended on this battle, turned his line across the head of the Russian column, and concentrated fire on its leading battleships. By the next day the Russian fleet had ceased to exist: most of its 38 ships were sunk, captured or interned, and Rozhestvensky was taken prisoner, while Japan lost only three torpedo boats.

Tōgō became a national hero, and navies everywhere studied the battle. His flagship Mikasa is preserved at Yokosuka.
story.zh:
1904年10月，俄国第二太平洋舰队从波罗的海出发，绕道非洲航行约一万八千海里。在北海，紧张的炮手把英国渔船误认为日本鱼雷艇而开炮，几乎引发英俄战争。由于很少有港口愿意接待，舰队加煤十分困难；到1905年5月驶抵亚洲时，旅顺早已陷落。

罗热斯特文斯基司令试图穿过对马海峡驶往海参崴。东乡平八郎率领速度更快、训练更精良的舰队在此等候。5月27日，他升起Z字旗，信号称皇国兴废在此一战，随即率舰队横切俄国纵队的前方，集中火力攻击其先头战列舰。到次日，俄国舰队已不复存在：38艘舰船中绝大多数被击沉、俘获或被中立国扣留，罗热斯特文斯基本人被俘，而日本仅损失三艘鱼雷艇。

东乡成为国民英雄，各国海军都研究这场海战。他的旗舰“三笠”号至今保存在横须贺。

summary.en: Under military pressure, Korean ministers signed a treaty making the Korean Empire a Japanese protectorate and handing its diplomacy to a Japanese Resident-General, Itō Hirobumi. Emperor Gojong never ratified it.
summary.zh: 在日本军事压力下，大韩帝国大臣签订条约，使韩国沦为日本保护国，外交权交由日本统监伊藤博文掌管。高宗皇帝始终未予批准。

sources.title: Peter Duus, The Abacus and the Sword: The Japanese Penetration of Korea, 1895–1910 (University of California Press, 1995)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Japan–Korea Treaty of 1905

summary.en: Prime Minister Yi Wan-yong and Resident-General Terauchi Masatake signed the annexation treaty on 22 August 1910; it was proclaimed a week later, ending the Korean Empire and beginning 35 years of Japanese colonial rule.
summary.zh: 1910年8月22日，总理大臣李完用与统监寺内正毅签订合并条约，一周后公布。大韩帝国就此灭亡，朝鲜开始了长达三十五年的日本殖民统治。

sources.title: Peter Duus, The Abacus and the Sword: The Japanese Penetration of Korea, 1895–1910 (University of California Press, 1995)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Japan–Korea Treaty of 1910

story.en:
Annexation came in steps. The protectorate treaty of 1905 took over Korea's foreign relations. In 1907, when Emperor Gojong sent secret envoys to the Hague peace conference to protest, Japan forced him to abdicate in favour of his son Sunjong and disbanded the Korean army, many of whose soldiers joined the righteous armies fighting in the hills. Tens of thousands of guerrillas were killed in the following years.

After An Jung-geun killed Itō Hirobumi in 1909, the hardliners in Tokyo pressed ahead. General Terauchi Masatake arrived as Resident-General with orders to finish the matter. On 22 August 1910 he and Prime Minister Yi Wan-yong signed a treaty by which the Korean emperor ceded "all rights of sovereignty" to the Japanese emperor, and on 29 August it was announced. Koreans remember the day as national humiliation day.

The scholar Hwang Hyeon took poison, leaving a poem lamenting that it had become hard to be an educated man in the world. A Government-General ruled Korea by military police, and a land survey from 1910 to 1918 transferred much land to the colonial state and Japanese companies.
story.zh:
吞并是一步步完成的。1905年的保护条约夺走了朝鲜的外交权。1907年，高宗秘密派遣使者前往海牙和平会议抗议，日本便逼他让位于儿子纯宗，并解散了朝鲜军队，许多士兵转入山中加入义兵作战。此后几年间，数以万计的义兵被杀。

1909年安重根刺杀伊藤博文后，东京的强硬派加快了步伐。寺内正毅大将奉命出任统监，要把此事了结。1910年8月22日，他与总理大臣李完用签署条约，规定韩国皇帝把“一切统治权”让与日本天皇，8月29日公布。朝鲜人把这一天称为“国耻日”。

学者黄玹服毒自尽，留下诗句感叹如今世上做一个读书人实在太难。朝鲜总督府以宪兵警察实行统治，1910年至1918年的土地调查把大量土地转入殖民政府和日本公司手中。

summary.en: A Declaration of Independence was read in Seoul on 1 March 1919, sparking nationwide peaceful demonstrations against Japanese rule. Their violent suppression killed thousands, but the movement led to the Korean Provisional Government in Shanghai.
summary.zh: 1919年3月1日，《独立宣言》在汉城宣读，引发全国性反对日本统治的和平示威。运动遭血腥镇压，数千人遇难，但随后促成了上海大韩民国临时政府的成立。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: March First Movement
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: March First Movement

story.en:
The former emperor Gojong died suddenly on 21 January 1919, amid rumours that the Japanese had poisoned him, and his funeral was set for 3 March. Inspired by Woodrow Wilson's talk of national self-determination and by a declaration of Korean students in Tokyo in February, thirty-three religious leaders, Cheondoist, Christian and Buddhist, signed a declaration of independence drafted by the writer Choe Nam-seon.

On 1 March the signatories read it at a Seoul restaurant and then called the police to arrest them. At nearby Tapgol Park students read it to a crowd, which marched through the streets shouting "Manse!" (Long live Korean independence). Over the following weeks demonstrations spread to almost every county, involving perhaps a million or more people.

The suppression was harsh. At Jeamni in April soldiers locked villagers in a church and set it on fire. Korean nationalists counted about 7,500 killed; Japanese official figures were far lower. Japan replaced military police rule with a more conciliatory "cultural policy" under Governor-General Saitō Makoto, and exiles founded the Provisional Government in Shanghai. 1 March is a national holiday in South Korea.
story.zh:
1919年1月21日，前皇帝高宗突然去世，民间传言是被日本人毒死的，葬礼定在3月3日。受到威尔逊“民族自决”言论以及2月朝鲜留日学生独立宣言的鼓舞，天道教、基督教和佛教的三十三位宗教领袖在作家崔南善起草的独立宣言上签名。

3月1日，签名者在汉城一家饭馆宣读宣言，然后自己打电话叫警察来逮捕他们。在附近的塔洞公园，学生们向人群宣读宣言，人群走上街头高呼“万岁”（朝鲜独立万岁）。此后数周，示威蔓延到几乎每一个郡，参与者或达一百万人以上。

镇压十分残酷。4月在堤岩里，日本士兵把村民锁在教堂里纵火焚烧。朝鲜民族主义者统计约有七千五百人被杀，日本官方数字则低得多。日本以斋藤实总督的较温和的“文化政治”取代了宪兵警察统治，流亡者则在上海成立了临时政府。3月1日如今是韩国的国家节日。

summary.en: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake beneath Sagami Bay struck at midday, and the fires that followed destroyed much of Tokyo and Yokohama. More than 100,000 people died, and in the chaos vigilantes massacred thousands of Koreans.
summary.zh: 一场约7.9级地震在相模湾下方于正午发生，随后的大火焚毁了东京和横滨的大部分地区，死亡逾十万人。混乱中，自警团屠杀了数千名朝鲜人。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Great Kantō earthquake
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 6: The Twentieth Century (1988)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Great Kantō Earthquake

summary.en: The US B-29 Enola Gay dropped the uranium bomb "Little Boy" on Hiroshima, the first use of a nuclear weapon in war. Around 70,000–80,000 people died instantly and many more by the end of 1945.
summary.zh: 美国B-29轰炸机“艾诺拉·盖”号在广岛投下铀弹“小男孩”，这是核武器首次用于战争。约七万至八万人当场死亡，至1945年底死亡人数大幅增加。

sources.title: U.S. Strategic Bombing Survey, The Effects of Atomic Bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki (1946)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome)
Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum
Wikipedia: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima

story.en:
At 8.15 a.m. on 6 August 1945 the B-29 Enola Gay, flying from Tinian, dropped a uranium bomb aimed at the T-shaped Aioi Bridge in the centre of Hiroshima, a city of some 350,000 people and an army headquarters. It exploded about 600 metres above the Shima hospital with a force equal to some 15,000 tonnes of TNT. The fireball and blast destroyed almost everything within two kilometres, and fires burned for hours; many survivors remember black rain falling in the afternoon.

About 70,000 to 80,000 people died that day, including thousands of mobilised schoolchildren clearing firebreaks and Korean forced labourers. By the end of the year about 140,000 were dead from burns, injuries and radiation sickness. The domed Industrial Promotion Hall, almost directly beneath the blast, was left standing as the Atomic Bomb Dome, a World Heritage site since 1996.

Sadako Sasaki, two years old in 1945, developed leukaemia and died in 1955 after folding paper cranes; children's cranes now hang at the Peace Memorial Park. The survivors' organisation Nihon Hidankyo received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2024.
story.zh:
1945年8月6日上午8时15分，从提尼安岛起飞的B-29轰炸机“艾诺拉·盖伊”号投下一枚铀弹，瞄准点是广岛市中心呈T字形的相生桥。广岛当时约有三十五万人，并驻有陆军司令部。原子弹在岛医院上空约600米处爆炸，威力约相当于一万五千吨TNT炸药。火球和冲击波几乎摧毁了两公里内的一切，大火燃烧了数小时；许多幸存者记得午后下起了黑雨。

当天约有七万至八万人死亡，其中有数千名被动员拆房开辟防火带的学生，以及被强征来的朝鲜劳工。到年底，死于烧伤、外伤和放射病的人数约达十四万。几乎位于爆心正下方的圆顶建筑“产业奖励馆”残存下来，成为原爆圆顶，1996年列入世界遗产。

1945年时年仅两岁的佐佐木祯子后来患上白血病，在折纸鹤中于1955年去世；如今和平纪念公园里挂满了孩子们折的纸鹤。原子弹受害者团体“日本原水爆被害者团体协议会”于2024年获得诺贝尔和平奖。

summary.en: Three days after Hiroshima, the plutonium bomb "Fat Man" exploded over the Urakami district of Nagasaki, killing some 40,000 people immediately. Japan announced its surrender on 15 August.
summary.zh: 广岛原爆三天后，钚弹“胖子”在长崎浦上地区上空爆炸，约四万人当场死亡。8月15日日本宣布投降。

sources.title: U.S. Strategic Bombing Survey, The Effects of Atomic Bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki (1946)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 6: The Twentieth Century (1988)
Wikipedia: Atomic bombing of Nagasaki

story.en:
The second bomb was meant for Kokura. On the morning of 9 August 1945 the B-29 Bockscar found the city hidden by haze and smoke from a fire raid on a neighbouring town, made three passes, and, short of fuel, turned to its secondary target. Through a gap in the clouds over Nagasaki the bombardier released the plutonium bomb at 11.02 a.m. It exploded over the Urakami valley, about three kilometres north of the planned aiming point.

Urakami was the home of Nagasaki's Catholic community, descendants of the hidden Christians who had kept their faith in secret through two and a half centuries of persecution. The cathedral, the largest in East Asia, was destroyed with worshippers inside; the Mitsubishi arms works and the medical college were also flattened. The hills around the valley shielded the old harbour city from the worst, but about 74,000 people were dead by the end of the year.

The radiologist Nagai Takashi, who lost his wife and himself died of radiation-related leukaemia in 1951, wrote The Bells of Nagasaki among the ruins. Nagasaki has campaigned since to be the last city ever destroyed by a nuclear weapon.
story.zh:
第二枚原子弹的原定目标是小仓。1945年8月9日上午，B-29轰炸机“博克之车”号发现小仓被雾霭和邻近城市空袭的烟尘遮蔽，盘旋三次后，燃料不足，只得转向第二目标。在长崎上空的云层缝隙中，投弹手于上午11时02分投下钚弹。它在浦上山谷上空爆炸，比预定瞄准点偏北约三公里。

浦上是长崎天主教徒聚居之地，他们是在两个半世纪的迫害中秘密守护信仰的“潜伏切支丹”的后代。当时东亚最大的浦上天主堂连同正在祈祷的信徒一起被毁；三菱兵器工厂和医科大学也被夷为平地。山谷周围的山丘使旧港区免遭最严重的破坏，但到年底仍有约七万四千人死亡。

失去妻子、自己也于1951年死于辐射相关白血病的放射科医生永井隆，在废墟中写下了《长崎的钟》。此后，长崎一直呼吁要成为最后一个被核武器摧毁的城市。

summary.en: North Korea invaded the South in June 1950. A US-led UN force, after holding the Pusan Perimeter and landing at Incheon, advanced to the Yalu; Chinese intervention drove it back, and the front settled near the 38th parallel until the 1953 armistice.
summary.zh: 1950年6月朝鲜人民军南下。以美国为首的联合国军守住釜山防御圈并在仁川登陆后推进至鸭绿江；中国人民志愿军参战后将其击退，战线最终稳定在三八线附近，直至1953年签订停战协定。

label.en: North Korean forces cross the 38th parallel (25 June)
label.zh: 朝鲜人民军越过三八线（6月25日）
联合国军推进至鸭绿江

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Korean War
Bruce Cumings, The Korean War: A History (Modern Library, 2010)
Roy E. Appleman, South to the Naktong, North to the Yalu (U.S. Army Center of Military History, 1961)
Wikipedia: Korean War

story.en:
At dawn on 25 June 1950 the North Korean army, with Soviet tanks and Stalin's approval, crossed the 38th parallel. Seoul fell in three days; the South Korean army blew up the Han River bridge while it was crowded with refugees. With the Soviet delegate boycotting, the UN Security Council called on members to help the South, and US troops were rushed from Japan. By August the defenders held only the Pusan Perimeter in the southeast.

On 15 September MacArthur landed at Incheon behind the North Korean lines; Seoul was retaken and UN forces drove north, taking Pyongyang in October and approaching the Yalu. China then sent hundreds of thousands of "volunteers". After the battles at the Chosin Reservoir, UN forces evacuated Hungnam by sea in December, taking some 100,000 refugees with them; Seoul changed hands for the third and fourth times in early 1951.

The front then stabilised near the 38th parallel, and for two years men died over hills while negotiators argued at Kaesong and Panmunjom, above all over whether prisoners could refuse repatriation. Perhaps three million people, most of them Korean civilians, were killed, and millions of families were divided.
story.zh:
1950年6月25日黎明，朝鲜人民军在苏联坦克的支援和斯大林的同意下越过三八线。三天后汉城陷落；韩国军队在汉江大桥上挤满难民时将其炸断。由于苏联代表抵制会议，联合国安理会呼吁会员国援助南方，美军从日本紧急调往朝鲜。到8月，守军只剩下东南部的釜山防御圈。

9月15日，麦克阿瑟在人民军后方的仁川登陆；汉城被收复，联合国军向北推进，10月攻占平壤，逼近鸭绿江。随后中国派出数十万“志愿军”。长津湖战役之后，联合国军于12月从兴南由海路撤退，同时带走约十万难民；1951年初，汉城第三次、第四次易手。

此后战线稳定在三八线附近。两年间，士兵们为争夺一座座山头而死，谈判代表则在开城和板门店争论不休，焦点是战俘能否拒绝遣返。大约三百万人死于这场战争，其中大多数是朝鲜半岛的平民，数百万家庭从此离散。

summary.en: General Douglas MacArthur's amphibious landing at Incheon, behind North Korean lines, led to the recapture of Seoul and the collapse of the North Korean army in the South.
summary.zh: 麦克阿瑟将军指挥联合国军在朝鲜人民军后方的仁川实施两栖登陆，随后收复汉城，使南下的朝鲜人民军全面溃退。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Incheon landing
Roy E. Appleman, South to the Naktong, North to the Yalu (U.S. Army Center of Military History, 1961)
Bruce Cumings, The Korean War: A History (Modern Library, 2010)
Wikipedia: Battle of Inchon

summary.en: Signed at Panmunjom by the UN Command, the Korean People's Army and the Chinese People's Volunteers, the armistice ended fighting and created the Demilitarized Zone. No peace treaty has followed.
summary.zh: 联合国军司令部与朝鲜人民军、中国人民志愿军在板门店签署停战协定，停止敌对行动并设立非军事区。此后双方至今未签订和平条约。

sources.title: Bruce Cumings, The Korean War: A History (Modern Library, 2010)
Roy E. Appleman, South to the Naktong, North to the Yalu (U.S. Army Center of Military History, 1961)
Wikipedia: Korean Armistice Agreement

story.en:
Armistice talks began in July 1951 and lasted two years. The hardest issue was the prisoners of war: tens of thousands of Chinese and North Korean prisoners did not want to go home, and the United States refused to force them. Stalin's death in March 1953 helped break the deadlock. South Korea's president Syngman Rhee, who wanted to fight on to unification, tried to wreck the deal in June by releasing some 27,000 anti-communist prisoners.

At 10 a.m. on 27 July 1953, in a hall built for the purpose at Panmunjom, the American general William Harrison and the North Korean general Nam Il signed the copies in silence and left without a word. The commanders, Mark Clark, Kim Il-sung and Peng Dehuai, countersigned separately. South Korea never signed. The guns fell silent at 10 that night.

The armistice drew a Military Demarcation Line with a Demilitarized Zone about four kilometres wide across the peninsula. It was meant to be temporary until a political settlement, but the 1954 Geneva conference failed, and more than seventy years later no peace treaty has been signed.
story.zh:
停战谈判始于1951年7月，持续了两年。最棘手的问题是战俘：数以万计的中国和朝鲜战俘不愿回国，美国拒绝强制遣返。1953年3月斯大林去世，有助于打破僵局。主张继续打到统一的韩国总统李承晚，于6月擅自释放约两万七千名反共战俘，企图破坏协议。

1953年7月27日上午10时，在板门店专门搭建的会场里，美国将军威廉·哈里森与朝鲜将军南日一言不发地签署文本，然后不辞而别。双方司令官克拉克、金日成和彭德怀分别在别处补签。韩国始终没有签字。当晚10时，枪炮声停止了。

停战协定在半岛上划出一条军事分界线，以及一条约四公里宽的非军事区。它本应只是政治解决之前的临时安排，但1954年日内瓦会议无果而终；七十多年过去了，和平条约至今仍未签订。

summary.en: The 24th Summer Olympics, held in Seoul shortly after South Korea's transition to democracy, showcased the country's rapid industrialisation and brought together athletes from both Cold War blocs after two boycotted Games.
summary.zh: 第24届夏季奥运会在韩国民主化转型后不久于汉城举行，展示了韩国迅速工业化的成就，也是在两届遭抵制的奥运会之后东西方阵营运动员再度同场竞技。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Seoul Summer Olympics
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
International Olympic Committee: Seoul 1988
Wikipedia: 1988 Summer Olympics

summary.en: A magnitude 9.0–9.1 megathrust earthquake off northeastern Honshu generated a tsunami that killed about 18,000 people and caused meltdowns at the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant.
summary.zh: 本州东北近海发生9.0至9.1级逆冲型大地震，引发海啸，约一万八千人罹难，并导致福岛第一核电站发生堆芯熔毁。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami
Japan Meteorological Agency, The 2011 off the Pacific coast of Tohoku Earthquake (report, 2011)
USGS: M 9.1 – 2011 Great Tohoku Earthquake, Japan
Wikipedia: 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami

story.en:
At 2.46 p.m. on 11 March 2011 the Pacific plate slipped beneath northeastern Japan along a fault some 500 kilometres long, producing an earthquake of magnitude 9.0–9.1, the largest ever recorded in Japan. It moved the Oshika peninsula about five metres to the east. Within half an hour the first tsunami waves reached the Sanriku coast; in places they ran up hillsides to nearly 40 metres.

Towns such as Rikuzentakata, Minamisanriku and Ōtsuchi were largely swept away, and many people died in buildings designated as evacuation centres. At Ōkawa Elementary School, 74 pupils and 10 teachers were killed while waiting on the playground. Meanwhile, at the Fukushima Daiichi plant the flooding knocked out cooling and three reactors melted down.

About 15,900 people died and some 2,500 remain missing. Of the 70,000 pines of Rikuzentakata's coastal forest, one survived, and is preserved as the "miracle pine". Japan rebuilt with higher seawalls and raised ground, and the disaster reshaped its debates about nuclear power and coastal life.
story.zh:
2011年3月11日下午2时46分，太平洋板块沿着一条长约500公里的断层俯冲到日本东北地区之下，引发9.0至9.1级地震，这是日本有记录以来最强的地震。牡鹿半岛向东移动了约五米。不到半小时，第一波海啸就抵达三陆海岸，有的地方海浪沿山坡上涌近40米高。

陆前高田、南三陆、大槌等城镇大部分被冲毁，许多人死于被指定为避难所的建筑中。在大川小学，74名学生和10名教师在操场上等待时遇难。与此同时，福岛第一核电站因浸水失去冷却能力，三座反应堆发生堆芯熔毁。

约一万五千九百人死亡，约两千五百人至今下落不明。陆前高田海岸七万株松树中只有一棵幸存，被作为“奇迹之松”保存下来。日本以更高的防潮堤和垫高的地基重建家园，这场灾难也重塑了日本有关核电和沿海生活的讨论。

summary.en: King Seong of Baekje sent a gilt-bronze Buddha image and sutras to the Yamato court of Emperor Kinmei. The Soga clan championed the new faith against the Mononobe and Nakatomi; after the Soga victory in 587, Buddhism became a pillar of the Asuka state.
summary.zh: 百济圣王向钦明天皇的大和朝廷献上金铜佛像和经论。苏我氏支持这一新信仰，与物部氏和中臣氏对立；587年苏我氏获胜后，佛教成为飞鸟时代国家的支柱。

sources.title: 《日本书纪》卷第十九 钦明天皇十三年（维基文库）
Wikipedia: Buddhism in Japan
William E. Deal & Brian Ruppert, A Cultural History of Japanese Buddhism (2015)

note: The Nihon shoki dates the gift to 552; the Gangōji engi and Jōgū Shōtoku hōō teisetsu give 538, which many historians prefer. Marker near Kinmei's palace at Shikishima (Sakurai). No Wikidata item exists for the event.

story.en:
The Nihon shoki dates the arrival to 552, though two older temple records give 538. King Seong of Baekje, seeking allies against Silla, sent Emperor Kinmei a gilt-bronze Buddha, banners and sutras with a letter praising the doctrine as the most excellent of all. Kinmei asked his ministers what to do. Soga no Iname urged acceptance, as every country to the west worshipped it; the Mononobe and Nakatomi, keepers of the native kami rites, warned that the gods would be angry.

Kinmei let Iname worship the image privately. When an epidemic followed, the chronicle says, the opponents threw the statue into a canal at Naniwa and burned the temple. The quarrel between the two clans lasted a generation and ended in war: in 587 Soga no Umako, with the young Prince Shōtoku, defeated Mononobe no Moriya.

The next year Baekje craftsmen began Asuka-dera, Japan's first full temple. Within a century Buddhism, with its writing, architecture and art, had become the religion of the court.
story.zh:
《日本书纪》把佛教传入的时间定为552年，但两份更早的寺院记录写作538年。为了寻求盟友对抗新罗，百济圣王送给钦明天皇一尊金铜佛像以及幡盖和经论，并附上书信称赞佛法是诸法中最殊胜的。钦明询问群臣。苏我稻目主张接受，理由是西方诸国都礼拜佛像；而主管本土神祇祭祀的物部氏和中臣氏警告说，这会触怒国神。

钦明允许稻目私下供奉佛像。据史书记载，随后瘟疫流行，反对者便把佛像扔进难波的水渠，并烧毁了寺院。两大氏族的争执持续了一代人，最终演变为战争：587年，苏我马子与年轻的圣德太子一起击败了物部守屋。

次年，百济工匠开始营建日本第一座完整的寺院飞鸟寺。不到一百年，佛教连同它带来的文字、建筑和艺术，已成为朝廷的宗教。

summary.en: Built in the Silla capital Gyeongju during the reign of Queen Seondeok, this bottle-shaped tower of about 360 granite blocks is often called the oldest surviving astronomical observatory in East Asia, though its exact function is still debated.
summary.zh: 瞻星台建于新罗善德女王在位时的都城庆州，由约360块花岗岩砌成瓶形塔身，常被称为东亚现存最古老的天文台，但其确切用途至今仍有争议。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Gyeongju Historic Areas
一然《三国遗事》卷1 善德王知几三事
Wikipedia: Cheomseongdae

note: The Samguk yusa places it in Seondeok's reign (632–647); the Sejong sillok jiriji gives 633 (Zhenguan 7), and 647 is also cited.

summary.en: Japan's oldest poetry anthology gathers about 4,500 poems by emperors, courtiers, frontier guards and commoners, written with Chinese characters used for their sounds (man'yōgana). Its latest datable poem is from 759, and Ōtomo no Yakamochi is thought to have been its main compiler.
summary.zh: 《万叶集》是日本现存最古老的和歌集，收录天皇、贵族、戍边防人和平民的约4500首和歌，以借汉字表音的“万叶假名”书写。其中可确定年代的最晚一首作于759年，一般认为大伴家持是主要编纂者。

sources.title: Britannica: Man'yō-shū
Wikipedia: Man'yōshū
Ian Hideo Levy (trans.), The Ten Thousand Leaves: A Translation of the Man'yōshū (1981)

note: Compiled after 759; the collection probably reached its final form in the 780s.

story.en:
The Man'yōshū, "collection of ten thousand leaves", gathers some 4,500 poems in twenty books, from legendary emperors to the 750s. Its poets include the court poet Kakinomoto no Hitomaro, who mourned princes in long chōka; Yamanoue no Okura, whose dialogue on poverty imagines a starving family in winter; and Princess Nukata. There are also the azuma-uta, songs of the eastern provinces, and the poems of sakimori, conscript frontier guards from the east who left their wives and parents to serve in Kyushu.

Japanese then had no script of its own, so the compilers wrote the poems in Chinese characters, some used for their meaning and many used only for their sound. This man'yōgana was the ancestor of the kana syllabaries.

The last datable poem was written by Ōtomo no Yakamochi on New Year's Day 759 at the provincial office in Inaba, and he is thought to have done much of the compiling. In 2019 the new era name Reiwa was taken from the preface to a group of Man'yōshū poems on plum blossoms, the first era name drawn from a Japanese rather than a Chinese classic.
story.zh:
《万叶集》意为“万叶之集”，共二十卷，收录约四千五百首和歌，时间上自传说中的天皇，下至750年代。其中的歌人有以长歌哀悼皇子的宫廷歌人柿本人麻吕；有写下《贫穷问答歌》、描绘冬日饥寒之家的山上忆良；还有额田王。集中还收有东国地方的“东歌”，以及“防人歌”，作者是被征召到九州戍边、告别妻儿父母的东国士兵。

当时日语还没有自己的文字，编者便用汉字记录和歌，有的取其字义，更多的只借其读音。这种“万叶假名”就是后来假名的祖先。

集中年代可考的最后一首歌，是大伴家持759年元旦在因幡国厅所作，一般认为他是主要编者。2019年，新年号“令和”取自《万叶集》中一组梅花歌的序文，这是第一个出自日本古典而非中国典籍的年号。

summary.en: Commissioned by King Seonjo in 1596 and completed by the royal physician Heo Jun in 1610, this 25-volume compendium organised East Asian medicine for Korean use and was printed in 1613. It was reprinted in China and Japan and is on the UNESCO Memory of the World Register.
summary.zh: 《东医宝鉴》由宣祖于1596年下令编纂，御医许浚于1610年完成，1613年刊行。这部25卷的医学全书将东亚医学系统整理以适合朝鲜之用，曾在中国和日本翻刻，已列入联合国教科文组织《世界记忆名录》。

sources.title: UNESCO Memory of the World: Donguibogam: Principles and Practice of Eastern Medicine
Wikipedia: Donguibogam

summary.en: Over three days a fire driven by strong winds burned most of Edo, including the main keep of Edo Castle, and killed perhaps 100,000 people. The shogunate rebuilt the city with firebreaks, wider streets and relocated temples and daimyo mansions; the keep was never rebuilt.
summary.zh: 强风助长下的大火连烧三日，焚毁江户大半城区，包括江户城天守阁，死者或达10万人。幕府重建时设置防火带、拓宽街道，并迁移寺院和大名宅邸；天守阁此后再未重建。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Great Fire of Meireki
Wikipedia (ja): 明暦の大火
Jeffrey Hanes, "Urban Planning as an Urban Problem", in J. L. McClain et al. (eds.), Edo and Paris (1994)

note: Began on the 18th day of the 1st month of Meireki 3 (2 March 1657, Gregorian). Death estimates range from about 30,000 to over 100,000.

summary.en: Nine days before the Tokyo Olympics opened, Japanese National Railways began services on the world's first high-speed railway, between Tokyo and Shin-Ōsaka, at up to 210 km/h. The 'bullet train' cut the journey from about 6.5 to 4 hours and inspired high-speed rail worldwide.
summary.zh: 东京奥运会开幕前九天，日本国有铁道开通了东京至新大阪之间的世界首条高速铁路，最高时速210公里。“子弹列车”将行程由约6个半小时缩短为4小时，并带动了全球高速铁路的发展。

sources.title: Britannica: Shinkansen
Central Japan Railway Company: About the Shinkansen
Wikipedia: Tokaido Shinkansen

note: Journey time fell to 4 hours at opening and to 3 hours 10 minutes in November 1965.

story.en:
The idea of a new high-speed line between Tokyo and Osaka was championed by Sogō Shinji, president of Japanese National Railways, and his chief engineer Shima Hideo, whose father had planned a prewar "bullet train" to the continent. Japan's old main line was narrow gauge and overloaded; the new one would be standard gauge, without level crossings, with electric multiple units instead of locomotives. Many critics thought railways belonged to the past.

Construction began in 1959 with the help of an 80-million-dollar World Bank loan. Costs nearly doubled, and Sogō resigned in 1963 to take responsibility; he was not invited to the opening. On 1 October 1964, nine days before the Tokyo Olympics, the blue-and-white trains began running at up to 210 km/h, cutting the trip to Shin-Ōsaka to four hours and, a year later, to three hours ten minutes.

The Shinkansen carried its billionth passenger in 1976, and in six decades no passenger has been killed by a derailment or collision. France's TGV, China's high-speed network and many others followed its example.
story.zh:
在东京与大阪之间修建一条新的高速铁路，这一构想由日本国有铁道总裁十河信二及其总工程师岛秀雄大力推动。岛秀雄的父亲曾在战前规划通往大陆的“弹丸列车”。日本原有的干线是窄轨，运力早已饱和；新线将采用标准轨距，没有平交道口，并以动力分散式电动车组取代机车。许多批评者认为铁路已经属于过去。

工程于1959年动工，并获得世界银行8000万美元的贷款。费用几乎翻了一番，十河信二于1963年引咎辞职，甚至没有受邀出席通车典礼。1964年10月1日，东京奥运会开幕前九天，蓝白相间的列车开始以最高210公里的时速运行，使东京到新大阪的旅程缩短到四小时，一年后又缩短到三小时十分钟。

1976年新干线运送了第十亿名乘客；六十年来，从未有乘客因脱轨或碰撞事故死亡。法国的TGV、中国的高铁网等许多系统都效仿了它。

name.en: Queen Himiko sends envoys to Wei

summary.en: The Wei zhi's "Account of the Wa" records that Himiko, ruler of Yamatai, sent envoys through the Daifang commandery to the Wei court, which named her "Queen of Wa, Friend of Wei" and sent a gold seal and bronze mirrors. It is the earliest detailed description of a Japanese polity.
summary.zh: 《三国志·魏书·倭人传》记载，邪马台国女王卑弥呼经带方郡遣使至魏廷，魏帝封其为“亲魏倭王”，赐金印与铜镜。这是关于日本列岛政权最早的详细记载。

sources.title: Chen Shou, Sanguozhi (Records of the Three Kingdoms), Wei shu 30: Account of the Wa
J. Edward Kidder, Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai (University of Hawaii Press, 2007)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Himiko
Wikipedia: Himiko

note: The Wei zhi text reads Jingchu 2 (238); most historians correct it to 239. The location of Yamatai (Kinai, e.g. Makimuku, or northern Kyushu) is debated; the pin marks the Makimuku candidate and the route the Wei itinerary to the Kyushu coast.

story.en:
Japan enters written history through a Chinese report. The Wei zhi, compiled by Chen Shou around 280, describes the Wa as living in many small countries that had fought one another for years until they agreed on a woman as ruler. Himiko, it says, "served the way of demons" and bewitched the people; she was seldom seen, lived in a palace with watchtowers and a stockade, and was served by a thousand women while a younger brother handled affairs.

In 239 her envoys reached the Wei court with slaves and cloth. The emperor answered with the title "Queen of Wa, Friend of Wei", a gold seal and a hundred bronze mirrors. When she died, around 248, a great mound was raised; a man who tried to rule failed, and peace returned only under a thirteen-year-old girl of her family, Iyo (or Toyo).
