Where Yamatai lay is one of Japanese archaeology's longest arguments. Kyushu has the Wei itinerary on its side; the Nara basin has Makimuku and the Hashihaka mound, built about when Himiko died.
story.zh:
日本是通过一份中国记录进入成文历史的。陈寿约在280年编成的《魏志》称，倭人分为许多小国，彼此攻伐多年，后来共立一女子为王。据记载，卑弥呼“事鬼道，能惑众”，很少露面，居于有楼观、城栅的宫室中，有婢女千人侍奉，由其弟辅佐治国。

239年，她的使者携奴婢和布匹抵达魏廷。魏帝回赐“亲魏倭王”称号、金印和铜镜百枚。约248年卑弥呼去世，倭人为她筑起大冢；此后男王继位，国中不服，直到立其宗女、年仅十三岁的壹与（台与）才重新安定。

邪马台国究竟在何处，是日本考古学持续最久的争论之一。九州说依据《魏志》所记的行程；畿内说则以奈良盆地的缠向遗址和箸墓古坟为证，后者的年代恰与卑弥呼去世时间相近。

summary.en: The largest keyhole-shaped burial mound in Japan, about 486 m long, was raised near Sakai in the mid-5th century and is attributed by the Imperial Household Agency to Emperor Nintoku. With the other Mozu and Furuichi tombs it shows the power of the Yamato kings in the Kofun period.
summary.zh: 日本最大的前方后圆坟，全长约486米，约于5世纪中叶修筑于今堺市附近，宫内厅将其定为仁德天皇陵。它与百舌鸟、古市古坟群的其他陵墓一起，显示出古坟时代大和王权的力量。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group: Mounded Tombs of Ancient Japan
Walter Edwards, "Contested Access: The Imperial Tombs in the Postwar Period", Journal of Japanese Studies 26:2 (2000)
Wikipedia: Daisen Kofun

note: Dated by archaeology to the mid-5th century (Wikidata gives c. 500); the attribution to Nintoku is traditional and cannot be tested because excavation is not permitted.

story.en:
Seen from the air, the Daisen Kofun is a vast keyhole of forest ringed by three moats. The mound is about 486 metres long, longer than any pyramid's base, and estimates suggest that building it took thousands of labourers more than a decade. Clay haniwa figures, cylinders, houses and horses once lined its terraces.

The Nihon shoki assigns the tomb to Emperor Nintoku, remembered as a sage who saw no smoke rising from his subjects' kitchens and lifted taxes for three years. Archaeologists date the tomb to the mid-5th century, the age when Yamato kings sent envoys to the Chinese Southern dynasties as the "five kings of Wa".

Because the Imperial Household Agency treats it as an imperial mausoleum, the tomb has never been excavated. In 2019 it was inscribed by UNESCO with 48 other mounds of the Mozu and Furuichi groups.
story.zh:
从空中俯瞰，大仙陵古坟是一个被三重壕沟环绕、覆满森林的巨大“钥匙孔”。坟丘全长约486米，超过任何一座金字塔的底边。据估算，修筑它需要数千名劳工花费十多年。坟丘的台阶上曾排列着圆筒、房屋和马匹等形状的陶质埴轮。

《日本书纪》将此墓归于仁德天皇。传说他登高望见百姓家中不起炊烟，便免除赋役三年。考古学家则把古坟年代定在5世纪中叶，正是大和王以“倭五王”之名向中国南朝遣使的时代。

由于宫内厅将其视为天皇陵墓，此墓从未发掘。2019年，它与百舌鸟、古市古坟群中的其他48座古坟一同列入联合国教科文组织世界遗产名录。

summary.en: Prince Shōtoku and Empress Suiko founded the temple at Ikaruga around 607. After a fire recorded for 670 it was rebuilt; its Golden Hall and five-storey pagoda are among the oldest surviving wooden buildings in the world.
summary.zh: 约607年，圣德太子与推古天皇在斑鸠创建法隆寺。据记载670年寺院遭火灾后重建，其金堂与五重塔是世界现存最古老的木构建筑之一。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Buddhist Monuments in the Hōryū-ji Area
Nihon shoki (Chronicles of Japan, 720)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Hōryū-ji
Wikipedia: Hōryū-ji

note: Founding date from the inscription on the Yakushi image; whether the present buildings are the 607 originals or a late-7th-century rebuild was long debated and is now settled in favour of a rebuild.

summary.en: Compiled under Prince Toneri and presented to the court at Heijō-kyō in 720, the thirty-volume Nihon shoki is Japan's first official history, written in classical Chinese and running from the age of the gods to 697.
summary.zh: 由舍人亲王主持编纂、720年进献于平城京朝廷的《日本书纪》共三十卷，是日本第一部官修正史，以汉文写成，记事从神代一直到697年。

sources.title: W. G. Aston (trans.), Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 (1896)
Shoku Nihongi (797), entry for Yōrō 4 (720)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Nihon shoki
Wikipedia: Nihon Shoki

name.en: Saichō founds Enryaku-ji on Mount Hiei
name.zh: 最澄于比叡山创建延历寺

summary.en: The monk Saichō built a hermitage on Mount Hiei above the future Heian capital in 788. After his study in Tang China it became the headquarters of the Tendai school and the training ground of Hōnen, Shinran, Dōgen and Nichiren, until Oda Nobunaga burned it in 1571.
summary.zh: 788年，僧人最澄在日后平安京上方的比叡山结庵。他入唐求法归来后，这里成为天台宗总本山，法然、亲鸾、道元、日莲都曾在此修行。1571年被织田信长焚毁。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto (Kyoto, Uji and Otsu Cities)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Saichō
Wikipedia: Enryaku-ji

name.en: Kūkai founds the monastery on Mount Kōya

summary.en: In 816 Emperor Saga granted Kūkai, newly returned from Tang Chang'an with Esoteric Buddhist teachings, a remote plateau in the Kii mountains. Kōyasan became the centre of the Shingon school and, after Kūkai's death there in 835, one of Japan's great pilgrimage sites.
summary.zh: 816年，嵯峨天皇将纪伊山地中一处偏远的高原赐给刚从唐朝长安学成密教归来的空海。高野山由此成为真言宗的中心；835年空海在此入寂后，又成为日本最重要的朝圣地之一。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range
Yoshito S. Hakeda, Kūkai: Major Works (Columbia University Press, 1972)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kūkai
Wikipedia: Mount Kōya

story.en:
Kūkai sailed for China in 804 on a mission whose four ships were scattered by storms; his drifted south to Fujian before he could travel on to Chang'an. There the master Huiguo, near the end of his life, gave him in a few months the full initiations of Esoteric Buddhism and told him to carry them east. Kūkai came home in 806 with sutras, mandalas and ritual implements, far ahead of his twenty-year assignment.

In 816 he asked Emperor Saga for land in the mountains where monks could meditate away from the capital. On the Kōya plateau, ringed by eight peaks that he compared to the petals of a lotus, he laid out a monastery. He died there in 835; Shingon tradition holds that he did not die but entered eternal meditation, and monks still bring meals to his mausoleum at Okunoin.

Today more than a hundred temples stand on the plateau, and the cemetery at Okunoin holds the graves of emperors, warlords and companies.
story.zh:
804年，空海随遣唐使渡海，四艘船被风暴吹散，他乘坐的船漂到福建，此后他才辗转抵达长安。在那里，晚年的惠果阿阇梨在短短数月内向他传授了密教的全部灌顶，并嘱咐他把教法传到东方。806年空海携经卷、曼荼罗和法器回国，远远早于原定二十年的留学期限。

816年，他向嵯峨天皇请求一块远离京城、可供僧人修禅的山地。高野山的高原四周有八座山峰环绕，空海把它们比作莲花的花瓣，在此规划寺院。835年他在此入寂；真言宗传统认为他并未死去，而是入定至今，僧人至今仍每天向奥之院的御庙送去斋饭。

如今高原上有一百多座寺院，奥之院墓地里长眠着天皇、武将，甚至还有企业的供养塔。

summary.en: Around 1002 the court lady Sei Shōnagon completed a collection of lists, sketches and opinions drawn from her years serving Empress Teishi. Witty and sharp-eyed, the Pillow Book founded the zuihitsu ("following the brush") essay genre.
summary.zh: 约1002年，女官清少纳言完成了一部由清单、片段和议论组成的作品，取材于她侍奉皇后定子的岁月。《枕草子》机智敏锐，开创了日本“随笔”文体。

sources.title: Ivan Morris (trans.), The Pillow Book of Sei Shōnagon (Columbia University Press, 1967)
Ivan Morris, The World of the Shining Prince: Court Life in Ancient Japan (1964)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: The Pillow Book
Wikipedia: The Pillow Book

note: Completion is usually placed around 1002; parts were circulating earlier and the text survives in several differing recensions.

story.en:
The Pillow Book begins with the seasons: in spring the dawn, in summer the night, in autumn the evening, in winter the early morning. From there Sei Shōnagon moves through lists of "things that make the heart beat faster", "hateful things" and "things that should be large", and through scenes from the household of Empress Teishi, whom she served from about 993.

Teishi's world was fragile. Her father, the regent Fujiwara no Michitaka, died in 995; his brother Michinaga pushed his own daughter Shōshi forward as a second consort, and Teishi died in childbirth in 1000. The book says little of this decline; its brilliance lies in a confident, often merciless eye for elegance and awkwardness.

Murasaki Shikibu, who served the rival empress Shōshi, wrote in her diary that Sei Shōnagon was "dreadfully conceited". Posterity has kept both women: the novelist of the Genji and the founder of the Japanese essay.
story.zh:
《枕草子》以四季开篇：春天是黎明，夏天是夜晚，秋天是黄昏，冬天是清晨。接着，清少纳言列出“令人心跳的事”“可憎的事”“应当大的东西”等种种清单，并描写她约自993年起侍奉的皇后定子身边的生活场景。

定子的世界其实十分脆弱。她的父亲、摄政藤原道隆于995年去世；其弟藤原道长扶植自己的女儿彰子成为另一位后妃，定子于1000年难产而死。书中很少提及这些变故，它的光彩在于作者对风雅与尴尬那种自信而又常常毫不留情的观察。

侍奉彰子的紫式部在日记中批评清少纳言“自以为是得可怕”。后世则把两人都记住了：一位是《源氏物语》的作者，一位是日本随笔的开创者。

summary.en: The regent Fujiwara no Yorimichi turned his father Michinaga's villa at Uji into a temple in 1052 and dedicated the Phoenix Hall to Amida Buddha in 1053, a vision of the Pure Land at the height of Fujiwara power. The hall appears on Japan's 10-yen coin.
summary.zh: 摄政藤原赖通于1052年将其父道长在宇治的别墅改为寺院，1053年建成供奉阿弥陀佛的凤凰堂，在藤原氏权势鼎盛时再现了净土景象。凤凰堂图案见于日本十元硬币。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto (Kyoto, Uji and Otsu Cities)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Byōdō-in
Wikipedia: Byōdō-in

summary.en: In the strait of Shimonoseki the Minamoto fleet under Minamoto no Yoshitsune destroyed the Taira. The child emperor Antoku drowned with his grandmother, and one of the imperial regalia, the sword, was lost; the Genpei War was over.
summary.zh: 在下关海峡，源义经率领的源氏水军歼灭平氏。年幼的安德天皇与外祖母一同投海身亡，三神器之一的宝剑沉入海中，源平合战就此结束。

sources.title: Helen Craig McCullough (trans.), The Tale of the Heike (Stanford University Press, 1988), book 11
Azuma kagami, entries for Genryaku 2 (1185)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Dannoura
Wikipedia: Battle of Dan-no-ura

story.en:
By spring 1185 the Taira had been driven from Kyoto, from Ichi-no-Tani and from Yashima, and their fleet, carrying the six-year-old emperor Antoku and the imperial regalia, was trapped in the narrow strait between Honshu and Kyushu. On 25 April the two fleets met off Dan-no-ura.

The Tale of the Heike says that the Taira had the better of the morning, riding the tide, and that the current turned at midday. A Taira commander, Taguchi Shigeyoshi, defected and showed the Minamoto which ship carried the emperor. As defeat became certain, Antoku's grandmother, the nun Nii-no-ama, took the boy in her arms and told him there was a capital beneath the waves; they leapt together. Many Taira nobles followed, weighed down by armour or anchors.

The sacred mirror and jewel were recovered, but the sword was lost. Local legend says the Heike crabs of the strait, whose shells look like angry faces, carry the spirits of the drowned warriors. Yoshitsune's triumph soon turned his brother Yoritomo against him.
story.zh:
到1185年春，平氏已先后被逐出京都、一之谷和屋岛。他们的船队载着年仅六岁的安德天皇和三神器，被困在本州与九州之间狭窄的海峡里。4月25日，双方船队在坛之浦海面交战。

据《平家物语》记载，上午平氏借着潮水占了上风，正午潮流逆转。平氏将领田口重能倒戈，向源氏指明天皇所在的船只。败局已定时，安德天皇的外祖母二位尼抱起这个孩子，告诉他“浪下也有都城”，两人一同投海。许多平氏公卿也随之跳海，有的身披铠甲，有的抱着船锚。

神镜和神玺后来被找回，宝剑却永远失落了。当地传说，海峡中背壳酷似怒容的“平家蟹”，寄托着溺死武士的亡魂。源义经的大胜，不久却招致了兄长源赖朝的猜忌。

summary.en: Retired Emperor Go-Toba declared the Kamakura regent Hōjō Yoshitoki an outlaw, but eastern warriors rallied to the shogunate and took Kyoto within a month. Go-Toba was exiled to the Oki Islands and the Hōjō set up the Rokuhara office to watch the court.
summary.zh: 后鸟羽上皇下旨讨伐镰仓幕府执权北条义时，但东国武士纷纷支持幕府，不到一个月便攻入京都。后鸟羽被流放到隐岐，北条氏设立六波罗探题监视朝廷。

sources.title: Azuma kagami, entries for Jōkyū 3 (1221)
Jeffrey P. Mass, The Development of Kamakura Rule, 1180–1250 (Stanford University Press, 1979)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Jōkyū Disturbance
Wikipedia: Jōkyū War

summary.en: Emperor Go-Daigo, aided by Ashikaga Takauji, Nitta Yoshisada and Kusunoki Masashige, overthrew the Kamakura shogunate in 1333 and tried to rule directly. Warriors felt cheated of rewards; Takauji rebelled, won at Minatogawa in 1336 and installed a rival emperor, splitting the court into Northern and Southern lines.
summary.zh: 后醍醐天皇在足利尊氏、新田义贞、楠木正成的协助下，于1333年推翻镰仓幕府，试图亲政。武士因恩赏不公而不满；足利尊氏起兵反叛，1336年在凑川获胜并另立天皇，朝廷由此分裂为南北两朝。

label.en: Escapes to Funanoe and Mount Senjō (Hōki)

label.zh: 足利尊氏攻破京都六波罗

sources.title: H. Paul Varley, Imperial Restoration in Medieval Japan (Columbia University Press, 1971)
Taiheiki (late 14th century)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kemmu Restoration
Wikipedia: Kenmu Restoration

story.en:
Go-Daigo meant to be an emperor who ruled, not a figurehead behind a shogun and a Hōjō regent. His first plots were discovered, and in 1332 he was exiled to the Oki Islands. A year later he escaped in a fishing boat, and the shogunate's best general, Ashikaga Takauji, sent to crush the loyalists, changed sides and took the Hōjō headquarters in Kyoto. In the east Nitta Yoshisada stormed Kamakura; the last Hōjō regent, Takatoki, and several hundred followers killed themselves at the Tōshō-ji temple.

The restored court was soon swamped by claims for reward, and Go-Daigo favoured courtiers and his own sons. Takauji broke with him in 1335. At Minatogawa in 1336 the loyal Kusunoki Masashige, ordered to fight against his own advice, was defeated and took his life, later becoming the model of imperial loyalty.

Takauji put a rival prince on the throne in Kyoto, and Go-Daigo carried the regalia to Yoshino in the mountains. Two courts claimed legitimacy until 1392.
story.zh:
后醍醐天皇想做一位真正执政的君主，而不是将军和北条执权背后的傀儡。他最初的密谋败露，1332年被流放到隐岐。一年后他乘渔船逃脱，幕府派去镇压勤王军的名将足利尊氏临阵倒戈，攻下北条氏在京都的据点六波罗。在东国，新田义贞攻入镰仓，末代执权北条高时与数百名部下在东胜寺自尽。

复辟后的朝廷很快被请赏的武士淹没，而后醍醐偏袒公卿和自己的皇子。1335年足利尊氏与他决裂。1336年凑川之战中，忠臣楠木正成奉命出战，此前他的建议未被采纳，最终战败自尽，后来成为“忠君”的楷模。

尊氏在京都另立皇子为天皇，后醍醐则携三神器避走吉野山中。此后两个朝廷各自宣称正统，直到1392年。

name.en: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu builds the Golden Pavilion

summary.en: After stepping down as shogun, Ashikaga Yoshimitsu acquired a Kitayama estate in 1397 and built a gold-leafed pavilion beside a pond. Turned into the Zen temple Rokuon-ji after his death, it was burned by a monk in 1950 and rebuilt in 1955.
summary.zh: 足利义满让出将军职后，于1397年取得北山的一处宅邸，在池畔建起贴金箔的楼阁。他死后此地改为禅寺鹿苑寺。1950年金阁被一名僧人纵火焚毁，1955年重建。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto (Kyoto, Uji and Otsu Cities)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kinkaku-ji
Wikipedia: Kinkaku-ji

story.en:
Ashikaga Yoshimitsu was the most powerful man Japan had seen in a century. He reunited the Northern and Southern courts in 1392, crushed rebellious vassals, and in 1394 handed the title of shogun to his young son while keeping real power. In 1397 he took over the Kitayama villa of the Saionji family and built a retreat whose three storeys mixed palace, samurai and Zen styles, the upper two covered in gold leaf.

There he received Ming envoys. The Yongle Emperor addressed him as "King of Japan", a title that opened official tally trade with China and angered later nationalists. Kitayama culture, the Noh of Zeami, whom Yoshimitsu patronised as a boy actor, and Chinese-style ink painting, flourished around him.

On 2 July 1950 a young acolyte set the pavilion on fire, an act that inspired Mishima Yukio's novel The Temple of the Golden Pavilion. The present building is a 1955 reconstruction, regilded in the 1980s.
story.zh:
足利义满是一个世纪以来日本最有权势的人。1392年他促成南北朝合一，镇压了叛乱的守护大名，1394年把将军职位传给年幼的儿子，自己仍掌实权。1397年，他接收了西园寺家的北山山庄，建起一座三层楼阁，融合了寝殿造、武家造与禅宗佛殿样式，上两层贴满金箔。

他在这里接见明朝使节。永乐帝称他为“日本国王”，这一封号开启了日明勘合贸易，却也令后世的民族主义者不满。以他为中心的北山文化随之繁荣：他少年时便赏识的世阿弥所演的能乐，以及中国风格的水墨画，都在此时兴盛。

1950年7月2日，一名年轻的见习僧人纵火烧毁金阁，此事后来成为三岛由纪夫小说《金阁寺》的题材。现在的建筑是1955年重建的，1980年代又重新贴金。

summary.en: A quarrel over a knife at Shinori, where a Japanese smith killed an Ainu customer, set off a rising under the chief Koshamain against the Japanese (Wajin) trading forts of southern Ezo. Most of the twelve forts fell before Takeda Nobuhiro, founder of the later Matsumae house, killed Koshamain.
summary.zh: 在志苔，一名和人铁匠因一把小刀的纠纷杀死了阿伊努顾客，由此引发首领胡奢魔犬领导的起义，矛头指向虾夷地南部的和人据点“道南十二馆”。十二馆大多陷落，后来松前氏的始祖武田信广射杀胡奢魔犬，起义才平息。

sources.title: Shinra no kiroku (Matsumae family chronicle, 1646)
Brett L. Walker, The Conquest of Ainu Lands: Ecology and Culture in Japanese Expansion, 1590–1800 (University of California Press, 2001)
Wikipedia: Koshamain's War

note: Known almost entirely from the later Matsumae family chronicle; the war is often dated 1457 with the 1456 knife incident as its trigger.

story.en:
The Matsumae family chronicle tells the story as its founding legend. In 1456 an Ainu youth came to a blacksmith at Shinori, on the coast near present-day Hakodate, to have a makiri knife made. They argued over the quality and price, and the smith stabbed him to death.

The Ainu of the region rose the next year under Koshamain. They attacked the Wajin forts (tate) strung along the Oshima peninsula, held by warrior families who traded fish, furs and hawk feathers for rice, iron and lacquerware; according to the chronicle ten of the twelve fell. The tide turned when Takeda Nobuhiro, a retainer of the Kakizaki house, killed Koshamain and his son with arrows.

Nobuhiro married into the Kakizaki and his descendants, later called Matsumae, became masters of the Ainu trade. Historians read the war as the first large clash in four centuries of conflict over who would control Ezo and its trade.
story.zh:
松前家的家史把这段故事当作家族的开基传说。1456年，一名阿伊努青年到今函馆附近海岸的志苔，请一名铁匠打制一把“马基里”小刀。双方为刀的质量和价格争吵起来，铁匠将他刺死。

次年，当地阿伊努人在胡奢魔犬率领下起事，攻击渡岛半岛沿岸的和人据点“馆”。据守这些馆的武士家族以大米、铁器和漆器，换取阿伊努人的鱼、毛皮和鹰羽。据家史记载，十二馆中有十座陷落。武田信广的出现扭转了局势：这位蛎崎氏的家臣用箭射杀了胡奢魔犬父子。

信广入赘蛎崎家，其后代改姓松前，成为阿伊努贸易的主宰者。史学家把这场战争视为此后四百年间围绕虾夷地及其贸易控制权的冲突中，第一次大规模的交锋。

name.en: Portuguese reach Tanegashima and firearms arrive
name.zh: 葡萄牙人漂至种子岛，铁炮传入

summary.en: Portuguese traders aboard a Chinese junk landed on Tanegashima, where the island's lord bought two of their matchlock guns and had his smiths copy them. Within decades "tanegashima" guns were made in quantity at Sakai and Kunitomo, transforming Sengoku warfare; European trade and Jesuit missions followed.
summary.zh: 搭乘中国帆船的葡萄牙商人在种子岛登陆，岛主种子岛时尧购得两支火绳枪，并令工匠仿制。数十年间，被称为“种子岛”的铁炮在堺和国友大量生产，改变了战国时代的战争；欧洲贸易和耶稣会传教随之而来。

sources.title: Teppōki (Chronicle of the Gun, 1606), by the monk Nanpo Bunshi
Olof G. Lidin, Tanegashima: The Arrival of Europe in Japan (NIAS Press, 2002)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Nanban art
Wikipedia: Tanegashima (gun)

note: The Japanese Teppōki gives 1543; the Portuguese writer António Galvão implies 1542.

story.en:
According to the Teppōki, a chronicle written for the Tanegashima family in 1606, a large ship with a hundred strangers aboard drifted to the island's southern cape in the autumn of 1543. A Chinese scholar on board, Wufeng, wrote in the sand to explain that these were traders from the southwestern barbarians. Two of them carried iron tubes that spat fire and could knock a bird from the sky.

The sixteen-year-old lord Tanegashima Tokitaka bought both guns for a large sum and set his swordsmiths to copy them; the hardest problem, closing the breech, was reportedly solved with a screw plug learned from a later visitor. Within a generation, workshops at Sakai, Negoro and Kunitomo were turning out thousands of matchlocks.

The Portuguese came back for trade, bringing silk from Macao and taking Japanese silver, and in 1549 Francis Xavier landed at Kagoshima to begin the Christian mission. For about a century, the Nanban ("southern barbarian") contacts reshaped Japanese warfare, art and religion.
story.zh:
据1606年为种子岛家族撰写的《铁炮记》记载，1543年秋，一艘载着百余名陌生人的大船漂到种子岛南端的海岬。船上一位名叫五峰的中国儒生在沙地上笔谈，说明这些人是西南蛮族的商人。其中两人携带着能喷火的铁管，可以把飞鸟打下来。

年仅十六岁的岛主种子岛时尧以重金买下这两支枪，并命刀匠仿制。据说最难的枪尾封闭问题，是后来向另一位来访者学会螺栓塞之后才解决的。不到一代人的时间，堺、根来和国友的作坊已能成千地制造火绳枪。

葡萄牙人随后回来经商，从澳门运来生丝，换走日本白银；1549年，方济各·沙勿略在鹿儿岛登陆，开始了天主教传教。在大约一个世纪里，与“南蛮”的接触重塑了日本的战争、艺术和宗教。

summary.en: Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu relieved Nagashino Castle and, behind wooden palisades, used massed arquebusiers to shatter the cavalry charges of Takeda Katsuyori. The Takeda never recovered, and the battle became the symbol of firearms changing Japanese warfare.
summary.zh: 织田信长与德川家康驰援长筱城，在木栅之后以大量火绳枪兵击溃武田胜赖的骑兵冲锋。武田氏从此一蹶不振，此役也成为火器改变日本战争的象征。

sources.title: Ōta Gyūichi, Shinchō kōki (Chronicle of Lord Nobunaga)
Stephen Turnbull, Nagashino 1575 (Osprey, 2000)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Nagashino
Wikipedia: Battle of Nagashino

note: The famous rotating three-rank volley comes from later accounts; modern historians doubt it, while accepting that massed guns behind palisades decided the battle.

story.en:
Takeda Katsuyori, son of the great Shingen, besieged the small Tokugawa castle of Nagashino in 1575 with about 15,000 men. One defender, Torii Sune'emon, slipped out to ask for help and, captured on his way back, shouted to the garrison that relief was coming before he was killed.

Nobunaga and Ieyasu arrived with perhaps 38,000 men and built a long fence of wooden stakes along the Rengo stream at Shitarabara, with gaps for counter-attacks. On 29 June Katsuyori's commanders, against the advice of veterans, charged across the wet ground. Nobunaga's chronicler says he had about a thousand arquebusiers; whatever their drill, the volleys tore apart the attack. By early afternoon many of the famous Takeda generals were dead.

Nagashino did not end mounted warfare, but it showed that disciplined infantry with guns could defeat the most admired army in Japan. Katsuyori held on for seven more years before the Takeda house was destroyed in 1582.
story.zh:
1575年，武田信玄之子武田胜赖率约一万五千人包围德川家的小城长筱城。守军鸟居强右卫门潜出城外求援，归途中被俘，他在临死前向城中高喊援军将至。

织田信长与德川家康带着约三万八千人赶到，在设乐原的连吾川畔筑起长长的木栅，并留出缺口以便反击。6月29日，武田军将领不顾老将劝阻，冲过泥泞的河滩。据信长的传记作者记载，信长有约一千名铁炮手；无论他们采用何种射击方式，齐射都撕碎了武田军的冲锋。到午后，武田家的许多名将已经战死。

长筱之战并没有终结骑兵作战，但它证明了训练有素、装备火器的步兵能够击败日本最受推崇的军队。胜赖又支撑了七年，1582年武田家灭亡。

summary.en: Oda Nobunaga, on the verge of unifying Japan, was attacked at the Honnō-ji temple in Kyoto by his general Akechi Mitsuhide and died in the burning building. Toyotomi Hideyoshi rushed back from the west and defeated Mitsuhide at Yamazaki eleven days later, inheriting Nobunaga's project.
summary.zh: 即将统一日本的织田信长在京都本能寺遭其部将明智光秀袭击，葬身火海。羽柴（丰臣）秀吉从西线火速回师，十一天后在山崎之战击败光秀，继承了信长的统一大业。

label.en: Hideyoshi at Takamatsu Castle makes peace with the Mōri
label.zh: 秀吉在高松城与毛利议和

sources.title: Ōta Gyūichi, Shinchō kōki (Chronicle of Lord Nobunaga)
Luís Fróis, Historia de Japam
Jeroen Lamers, Japonius Tyrannus: The Japanese Warlord Oda Nobunaga Reconsidered (Hotei, 2000)
Wikipedia: Honnō-ji Incident

note: Mitsuhide's motive is unknown; grudge, ambition and conspiracy theories all have advocates.

story.en:
In June 1582 Nobunaga was the master of central Japan. He had crushed the Takeda that spring and was sending troops to help Hideyoshi against the Mōri in the west. He stopped in Kyoto with only a few dozen attendants, lodging at the Honnō-ji temple, and spent the evening of 20 June at a tea gathering.

Akechi Mitsuhide, ordered west with some 13,000 men, turned his army toward the capital instead; tradition has him declare, "The enemy is at the Honnō-ji." At dawn his troops surrounded the temple. The chronicler Ōta Gyūichi heard from survivors that Nobunaga fought with a bow and spear until wounded, then withdrew into the burning halls and was never seen again. His heir Nobutada died the same day.

Hideyoshi heard the news at the siege of Takamatsu, concealed it while he made peace with the Mōri, and marched his army some 200 kilometres in about a week. At Yamazaki on 2 July he routed Mitsuhide, who was killed by peasants as he fled. Mitsuhide's rule had lasted barely two weeks; Hideyoshi's would unite Japan.
story.zh:
1582年6月，织田信长已是日本中部的霸主。那年春天他消灭了武田氏，正准备派兵到西线支援羽柴秀吉对毛利氏作战。他只带着数十名随从在京都停留，下榻本能寺，6月20日晚还举办了一场茶会。

奉命率约一万三千人西征的明智光秀，却把大军转向京都；相传他宣称“敌在本能寺”。黎明时分，明智军包围了寺院。据太田牛一从幸存者处听到的说法，信长先用弓、后用长枪奋战，负伤后退入燃烧的殿宇，从此再未现身。他的继承人织田信忠也在同一天战死。

秀吉在高松城围城时得到消息，他秘不发丧，先与毛利氏议和，随后率军在大约一周内急行约200公里。7月2日，他在山崎大败光秀，光秀逃亡途中被农民所杀。光秀的统治只维持了两周左右，而秀吉最终统一了日本。

name.en: Shō Hashi unifies Okinawa: the Ryukyu Kingdom
name.zh: 尚巴志统一冲绳，琉球王国建立

summary.en: Shō Hashi, lord of Sashiki, made his father king of Chūzan in 1406, conquered the northern kingdom of Hokuzan and in 1429 the southern kingdom of Nanzan, uniting Okinawa under a court at Shuri that traded across East and Southeast Asia as a tributary of Ming China.
summary.zh: 佐敷按司尚巴志于1406年拥立其父为中山王，随后攻灭北山，1429年又灭南山，统一冲绳本岛。以首里为王都的琉球王国作为明朝的朝贡国，开展遍及东亚和东南亚的贸易。

sources.title: Chūzan seikan (Mirror of Chūzan, 1650), by Haneji Chōshū
George H. Kerr, Okinawa: The History of an Island People (Tuttle, 1958; rev. 2000)
Gregory Smits, Visions of Ryukyu: Identity and Ideology in Early-Modern Thought and Politics (University of Hawaii Press, 1999)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Gusuku Sites and Related Properties of the Kingdom of Ryukyu
Wikipedia: Shō Hashi

note: No Wikidata item for the unification itself. The dates 1416 (Hokuzan) and 1429 (Nanzan) come from 17th–18th-century Ryukyuan histories; Ming records show the last Hokuzan and Nanzan tribute missions in 1415 and 1429.

story.en:
In the 14th century Okinawa was divided among three rival kingdoms, Hokuzan in the north, Chūzan in the middle and Nanzan in the south, each sending tribute to the Ming court and each ruled from a stone gusuku castle. Shō Hashi was a minor lord of Sashiki on the southeast coast. In 1406 he overthrew King Bunei of Chūzan at Urasoe and placed his own father, Shishō, on the throne.

The Ryukyuan histories say Hashi then marched north and took the great castle of Nakijin from Hokuzan, and in 1429 captured Shimajiri Ōzato, the seat of Nanzan. He made Shuri, on a hill above the port of Naha, his capital, and the Ming emperor confirmed his family with the surname Shō.

The kingdom that followed was small but cosmopolitan. Its ships carried Chinese silk and porcelain, Japanese swords and Southeast Asian spices between Fujian, Kyushu, Korea, Siam and Malacca. A bronze bell cast for Shuri Castle in 1458 boasted that Ryukyu was a "bridge between nations".
story.zh:
14世纪的冲绳分裂为三个相互竞争的王国：北部的北山、中部的中山和南部的南山。三国各自向明朝朝贡，各自以石砌的“御城”（古斯库）为统治中心。尚巴志原是东南海岸佐敷的一名小按司。1406年，他在浦添推翻中山王武宁，拥立父亲思绍为王。

据琉球史书记载，尚巴志随后北伐，攻取北山的今归仁城，1429年又攻下南山的都城岛尻大里。他以那霸港上方山丘上的首里为王都，明朝皇帝赐其家族姓“尚”。

此后的琉球王国虽小，却十分开放。它的船只往来于福建、九州、朝鲜、暹罗和马六甲之间，运载中国的丝绸和瓷器、日本的刀剑以及东南亚的香料。1458年为首里城铸造的铜钟上自豪地宣称，琉球是“万国之津梁”。

name.zh: 萨摩入侵琉球（庆长琉球之役）

summary.en: With the shogun's permission, the Shimazu lords of Satsuma sent about 3,000 men who took Shuri in a few weeks. King Shō Nei was carried to Kagoshima and Edo; the Amami islands were annexed and Ryukyu became a vassal of Satsuma while still sending tribute to China.
summary.zh: 在德川幕府许可下，萨摩藩岛津氏派出约三千人，数周内攻占首里。国王尚宁被押往鹿儿岛和江户；奄美诸岛被割让，琉球成为萨摩的附庸，同时继续向中国朝贡。

label.en: Landing at Unten; Nakijin castle falls
label.zh: 在运天登陆，今归仁城陷落

sources.title: George H. Kerr, Okinawa: The History of an Island People (Tuttle, 1958; rev. 2000)
Gregory Smits, Visions of Ryukyu: Identity and Ideology in Early-Modern Thought and Politics (University of Hawaii Press, 1999)
Robert K. Sakai, "The Satsuma–Ryukyu Trade and the Tokugawa Seclusion Policy", Journal of Asian Studies 23:3 (1964)
Wikipedia: Invasion of Ryukyu

story.en:
Ryukyu had angered the new Tokugawa regime by refusing to help with Hideyoshi's Korean war and to send thanks for the return of shipwrecked sailors. In 1609 Shimazu Tadatsune of Satsuma obtained the shogun's leave to punish it. About 3,000 samurai, many of them veterans of Korea, sailed south in some hundred ships with matchlocks; the Ryukyuans had little experience of war.

The islands of Amami fell one by one. The army landed at Unten, burned Nakijin, and marched on Shuri, which surrendered in early April after brief resistance. King Shō Nei was taken to Kagoshima and on to Sunpu and Edo to meet Ieyasu and the shogun Hidetada, and returned in 1611 only after swearing an oath of loyalty to the Shimazu.

Satsuma took the Amami islands, imposed taxes and placed officials in Naha, but kept the conquest discreet. Ryukyu went on sending tribute to the Ming and later the Qing, and Chinese envoys were not told of the Japanese overlords: a double subordination that lasted until 1879.
story.zh:
琉球曾拒绝为丰臣秀吉的朝鲜战争提供援助，也没有为德川政权送还漂流船员一事遣使致谢，因而得罪了新成立的幕府。1609年，萨摩藩主岛津忠恒获得将军许可出兵问罪。约三千名武士乘坐上百艘船、携带火绳枪南下，其中许多人参加过朝鲜之战；而琉球人几乎没有战争经验。

奄美诸岛相继陷落。萨摩军在运天登陆，焚毁今归仁城，进逼首里。经过短暂抵抗，首里于4月初投降。国王尚宁被押到鹿儿岛，又被带往骏府和江户拜见德川家康和将军秀忠，直到1611年向岛津氏宣誓效忠后才获准回国。

萨摩夺取了奄美诸岛，向琉球征收贡赋，并在那霸派驻官员，但对这场征服秘而不宣。琉球继续向明朝及后来的清朝朝贡，中国使节也不被告知日本才是真正的宗主。这种“两属”状态一直持续到1879年。

name.en: Dejima: the Dutch window on Japan
name.zh: 出岛：荷兰人的“日本之窗”

summary.en: Nagasaki merchants built the small fan-shaped island of Dejima in 1634–1636 to confine Portuguese traders. After the Portuguese were expelled in 1639, the Dutch East India Company was moved there from Hirado in 1641, and for two centuries it was the only Western trading post allowed in Japan.
summary.zh: 1634—1636年，长崎商人修筑了扇形小岛出岛，用以圈禁葡萄牙商人。1639年葡萄牙人被驱逐后，荷兰东印度公司于1641年从平户迁至此地。此后两百年间，这里是日本唯一允许存在的西方商馆。

sources.title: Grant K. Goodman, Japan and the Dutch, 1600–1853 (Curzon, 2000)
Engelbert Kaempfer, The History of Japan (1727)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Dejima
Wikipedia: Dejima

story.en:
Dejima was a prison as much as a port. A single guarded bridge linked it to Nagasaki; the Dutch could not leave without permission, and Japanese could enter only on business. A dozen or so Company employees lived there at a time, trading Indian textiles, sugar and books for Japanese copper, silver and lacquer.

Once a year the head of the factory travelled to Edo to thank the shogun. The physician Engelbert Kaempfer, who made the trip twice in 1691–92, described being made to dance, sing and act out a drunken man for the shogun Tsunayoshi's entertainment, and his posthumous History of Japan shaped Europe's picture of the country for a century.

The traffic in ideas mattered more than the trade. Japanese interpreters and doctors learned Dutch and built rangaku, "Dutch learning": in 1774 Sugita Genpaku and colleagues published a translation of a Dutch anatomy book after checking it against an executed criminal's body. Philipp Franz von Siebold taught medicine near Nagasaki in the 1820s. When Perry arrived, Japan already had scholars who could read Western science.
story.zh:
出岛与其说是港口，不如说是一座监狱。只有一座有人看守的小桥把它与长崎相连；荷兰人未经许可不得离开，日本人也只有因公才能进入。岛上通常只住着十几名公司职员，用印度布料、砂糖和书籍交换日本的铜、白银和漆器。

商馆馆长每年要前往江户觐见将军致谢。医生恩格尔贝特·坎普弗尔在1691—1692年两次随行，他记述自己被要求为将军德川纲吉跳舞、唱歌，还要表演醉汉。他身后出版的《日本史》在一个世纪里塑造了欧洲人心目中的日本形象。

比贸易更重要的是思想的流通。日本的通词和医生学习荷兰语，形成了“兰学”。1774年，杉田玄白等人在对照一具受刑犯人的尸体验证之后，出版了荷兰解剖学书的译本《解体新书》。1820年代，西博尔德在长崎附近教授医学。当佩里到来时，日本已经有能够阅读西方科学著作的学者。

summary.en: The Ainu chief Shakushain of Shibuchari led a pan-Ainu rising against the Matsumae domain's trade monopoly, killing Japanese traders and sailors along the coasts. Matsumae guns stopped the advance at Kunnui; Shakushain was murdered at a peace banquet, and Matsumae control over Ainu trade grew tighter.
summary.zh: 静内（シブチャリ）的阿伊努首领沙牟奢允发动跨地域的阿伊努起义，反抗松前藩的贸易垄断，沿海的和人商人和船员多被杀死。松前军以火枪在国缝阻止了阿伊努军的推进；沙牟奢允在议和宴会上被杀，此后松前藩对阿伊努贸易的控制更加严密。

label.en: Shakushain killed at Pipok peace talks
label.zh: 沙牟奢允在新冠议和时被杀

sources.title: Brett L. Walker, The Conquest of Ainu Lands: Ecology and Culture in Japanese Expansion, 1590–1800 (University of California Press, 2001)
David L. Howell, "Ainu Ethnicity and the Boundaries of the Early Modern Japanese State", Past & Present 142 (1994)
Ezo hōki (Matsumae account of the war, c. 1670)
Wikipedia: Shakushain's revolt

note: Japanese casualty figures (about 270 traders and sailors) come from Matsumae sources; Ainu losses are unknown.

story.en:
By the 1660s the Ainu of Hokkaido were trapped in an unequal trade. The Matsumae domain controlled all exchange with Japan and had cut the amount of rice it gave for each bale of dried salmon, while Japanese gold-miners and falconers pushed into Ainu rivers. Rival Ainu groups were fighting over hunting grounds; when Shakushain of the Shibuchari river killed his rival Onibishi in 1668 and an envoy seeking Matsumae help died on the way home, perhaps of smallpox, rumour said the Japanese had poisoned him.

In the summer of 1669 Shakushain called on the Ainu to strike. Along the Pacific and Japan Sea coasts they killed Japanese traders and crews of trading ships. His warriors marched toward Matsumae itself, but at Kunnui on the Oshima peninsula they met musket fire and fell back.

That autumn the Matsumae commander invited Shakushain to make peace at Pipok. During the drinking that followed, Shakushain and his companions were killed. Resistance went on in places until 1672. Afterwards the Ainu had to swear loyalty to Matsumae, and Japanese merchants took over the fisheries.
story.zh:
到1660年代，北海道的阿伊努人深陷不平等的贸易之中。松前藩垄断了与本州的全部交易，并削减了每包干鲑鱼可换得的大米数量，同时和人的淘金者和鹰匠不断深入阿伊努人的河流地带。阿伊努各部为争夺猎场彼此相争。1668年，静内河流域的沙牟奢允杀死对手鬼菱；一名前往松前求援的使者在归途中死去，可能死于天花，但谣言说是被和人毒死的。

1669年夏，沙牟奢允号召阿伊努人起事。在太平洋和日本海沿岸，他们杀死了和人商人和贸易船船员。他的战士向松前进军，却在渡岛半岛的国缝遭遇火枪射击而退却。

当年秋天，松前藩将领邀沙牟奢允到新冠（ピポク）议和。在随后的酒宴上，沙牟奢允及其同伴被杀。部分地区的抵抗持续到1672年。此后阿伊努人被迫宣誓效忠松前藩，和人商人则逐步接管了渔场。

name.zh: 赤穗四十七义士复仇（赤穗事件）

summary.en: After Lord Asano Naganori of Akō was forced to commit seppuku in 1701 for drawing his sword on the official Kira Yoshinaka in Edo Castle, forty-seven of his masterless samurai, led by Ōishi Kuranosuke, killed Kira at his Edo mansion. They were ordered to commit seppuku, and their story became the drama Chūshingura.
summary.zh: 1701年，赤穗藩主浅野长矩在江户城内拔刀砍伤幕府高家吉良义央，被命切腹。1703年初，其旧臣大石内藏助率四十七名浪士夜袭江户吉良宅邸，将吉良斩杀。浪士们随后奉命切腹，他们的故事成为戏剧《忠臣藏》。

sources.title: Henry D. Smith II, "The Trouble with Terasaka: The Forty-Seventh Rōnin and the Chūshingura Imagination", Japan Review 16 (2004)
Donald Keene (trans.), Chūshingura: The Treasury of Loyal Retainers (Columbia University Press, 1971)
Wikipedia: Forty-seven rōnin

story.en:
On 21 April 1701, in a corridor of Edo Castle, Asano Naganori, lord of the small domain of Akō, drew his short sword and wounded Kira Yoshinaka, the master of ceremonies who had been instructing him for an imperial reception. Drawing a weapon in the castle was a capital offence. Asano was ordered to cut his belly that same day, his domain was confiscated, and Kira went unpunished.

Asano's chief retainer, Ōishi Kuranosuke, first petitioned for the house to be restored; when that failed, he and forty-six others planned revenge while living as ronin, some of them pretending to have abandoned honour. On a snowy night at the end of January 1703 they broke into Kira's mansion, found him hiding in a charcoal shed, and carried his head to Asano's grave at the Sengaku-ji temple.

The shogunate debated for weeks before ordering them to commit seppuku, an honourable death rather than execution. Within decades the puppet and kabuki play Chūshingura (1748) made them the model of loyalty; they still lie at Sengaku-ji beside their lord.
story.zh:
1701年4月21日，在江户城的走廊里，小藩赤穗的藩主浅野长矩拔出短刀砍伤了吉良义央。吉良是负责礼仪的高家，正在指导浅野接待天皇敕使。在城中拔刀是死罪，浅野当天即被命令切腹，领地被没收，而吉良却未受惩罚。

浅野的首席家老大石内藏助起初请求恢复浅野家，失败后，他与另外四十六人以浪人身份谋划复仇，其中有些人还装作放弃了武士的名誉。1703年1月末一个下雪的夜晚，他们攻入吉良宅邸，在炭屋里找到藏身的吉良，并把他的首级带到泉岳寺浅野的墓前。

幕府争论了数周，最终命令他们切腹，这是体面的死法，而非斩首。数十年后，人形净琉璃和歌舞伎剧目《假名手本忠臣藏》（1748年）使他们成为忠义的典范。至今他们仍与主君一同长眠于泉岳寺。

summary.en: Cold summers from 1782, worsened by the eruption of Mount Asama in 1783, destroyed harvests across northeastern Japan. Hundreds of thousands died of hunger and disease; rice riots hit Edo and Osaka in 1787, toppling the policies of Tanuma Okitsugu and ushering in Matsudaira Sadanobu's Kansei reforms.
summary.zh: 自1782年起连年冷夏，1783年浅间山喷发更使灾情加剧，日本东北地区颗粒无收。数十万人死于饥饿与疾病；1787年江户和大阪爆发“打毁”骚乱，田沼意次的政策随之破产，松平定信开始推行宽政改革。

sources.title: Conrad Totman, Early Modern Japan (University of California Press, 1993), ch. 13
Anne Walthall, Social Protest and Popular Culture in Eighteenth-Century Japan (University of Arizona Press, 1986)
Wikipedia: Tenmei famine

note: Death tolls are estimates: shogunal population surveys fell by roughly 900,000 between 1780 and 1786.

story.en:
The trouble began with weather. From 1782 the summers in northeastern Japan were cold and wet; then in August 1783 Mount Asama in central Honshu erupted, burying villages under pumice and mudflows and veiling the sky with ash. In the domains of Tsugaru, Nanbu and Sendai the rice crop failed almost completely.

Many domains had sold their rice reserves to Osaka merchants for cash, and could not feed their people. Contemporary accounts from Tsugaru describe villagers eating roots, straw and dogs, and abandoned bodies along the roads. Epidemics followed hunger. The shogunate's population surveys suggest that Japan lost about 900,000 people between 1780 and 1786.

In 1787 the anger reached the cities. Crowds in Edo and Osaka smashed rice dealers' shops in the uchikowashi riots. The senior councillor Tanuma Okitsugu, already blamed for corruption, had fallen the year before; his successor Matsudaira Sadanobu ordered granaries in every domain, frugality and moral discipline in the Kansei reforms.
story.zh:
灾难始于天气。自1782年起，日本东北地区的夏天寒冷潮湿；1783年8月，本州中部的浅间山又发生喷发，浮石和泥流吞没村庄，火山灰遮天蔽日。津轻、南部、仙台等藩的稻米几乎绝收。

许多藩此前已把储备米卖给大阪商人换取现金，此时无力赈济百姓。当时津轻的记载描述，村民靠草根、稻草甚至狗充饥，路旁遗尸无人收殓。饥荒之后又是瘟疫。幕府的人口调查显示，1780至1786年间日本人口减少约九十万。

1787年，愤怒蔓延到城市。江户和大阪的民众捣毁米商的店铺，史称“打毁”。早已背负贪腐骂名的老中田沼意次已于前一年下台；继任的松平定信推行宽政改革，命令各藩设置义仓，提倡节俭与道德约束。

name.zh: 葛饰北斋《神奈川冲浪里》

summary.en: Published in Edo around 1831 as part of Katsushika Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the print of fishermen's boats beneath a towering wave used imported Prussian blue and became the best-known image of Japanese art worldwide.
summary.zh: 约1831年，葛饰北斋在江户出版组画《富岳三十六景》，其中一幅描绘渔船在巨浪下挣扎、远处可见富士山。此画使用了进口的普鲁士蓝颜料，成为全世界最知名的日本艺术形象。

sources.title: Timothy Clark, Hokusai: Beyond the Great Wave (British Museum / Thames & Hudson, 2017)
Metropolitan Museum of Art: Under the Wave off Kanagawa (JP1847)
Wikipedia: The Great Wave off Kanagawa

note: The series was issued from about 1830 to 1832; the exact year of the Great Wave is not recorded.

story.en:
Hokusai was about seventy, poor and recovering from a stroke, when the publisher Nishimuraya Yohachi began issuing his landscapes of Mount Fuji around 1830. Landscape was then a minor genre beside prints of actors and courtesans; the series made it a major one.

In the Great Wave the mountain is tiny, framed by the trough of a wave whose crest breaks into claw-like spray over three fast cargo boats rowing fish to the Edo market. The deep blue was Prussian blue, a synthetic pigment newly cheap through the Dutch and Chinese trade, and the publisher advertised it as a selling point. Thousands of impressions were pulled from the woodblocks until they wore out.

After Japan opened in the 1850s the print reached Europe, where Monet, Van Gogh and Debussy admired it; the first edition of Debussy's La Mer (1905) bore a detail on its cover. Hokusai himself, who signed late works "the old man mad about painting", hoped to reach true mastery at a hundred and ten.
story.zh:
大约1830年，出版商西村屋与八开始发行葛饰北斋的富士山风景画时，北斋已年近七十，生活贫困，刚从中风中恢复。当时风景画在以演员和名妓为题材的版画旁边只是小类，这套组画使它跃升为主流。

在《神奈川冲浪里》中，富士山显得很小，被巨浪的波谷框住；浪尖碎成爪状的浪花，压在三条正把鲜鱼运往江户市场的快船上。画中的深蓝色是普鲁士蓝，这种合成颜料经荷兰和中国贸易而变得便宜，出版商还把它当作卖点来宣传。木版不断刷印，直到磨损，印量达数千张。

1850年代日本开国后，这幅画传到欧洲，受到莫奈、梵高和德彪西的推崇；德彪西《大海》1905年初版乐谱的封面就采用了画中的局部。晚年署名“画狂老人”的北斋自己，则期望活到一百一十岁时才能达到真正的境界。

summary.en: Forces of Satsuma, Chōshū and allied domains fighting in the name of the young Emperor Meiji defeated the former shogun's army at Toba–Fushimi, took Edo without a battle, crushed the northern alliance at Aizu and ended the last resistance at Hakodate's Goryōkaku fortress in 1869.
summary.zh: 萨摩、长州等藩以年轻的明治天皇名义作战，在鸟羽·伏见击败前将军的军队，兵不血刃地接收江户，在会津击溃奥羽越列藩同盟，1869年在函馆五棱郭结束了最后的抵抗。

sources.title: Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)
Mark Ravina, The Last Samurai: The Life and Battles of Saigō Takamori (Wiley, 2004)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Boshin Civil War
Wikipedia: Boshin War

story.en:
Tokugawa Yoshinobu had handed his powers back to the emperor in November 1867, hoping to lead the new order as the greatest lord. Satsuma and Chōshū instead seized the palace in January 1868, proclaimed imperial rule and stripped him of his lands. When Yoshinobu's army marched on Kyoto, it met the smaller, better-armed southern forces at Toba and Fushimi; the appearance of the imperial brocade banner over the enemy lines made the shogun's men rebels, and Yoshinobu fled to Edo by ship.

Edo, a city of a million, was spared. Saigō Takamori and the shogunate's Katsu Kaishū negotiated the surrender of Edo Castle in May. But the northeastern domains formed an alliance, and Aizu resisted to the end; in the most remembered episode, teenage boys of the Byakkotai ("White Tiger Force") killed themselves on a hill when they mistook smoke over the town for the castle burning.

The last holdouts, under the naval officer Enomoto Takeaki, sailed to Hokkaido and declared a republic at Hakodate. It surrendered in June 1869, and the new government stood unchallenged.
story.zh:
1867年11月，德川庆喜将政权奉还天皇，希望以最大诸侯的身份主导新秩序。然而萨摩和长州在1868年1月控制皇宫，宣布“王政复古”，并剥夺他的领地。庆喜的军队向京都进发，在鸟羽和伏见遭遇人数较少但装备更好的南方诸藩军队。敌阵上竖起的锦之御旗，使幕府军沦为“贼军”，庆喜乘船逃回江户。

拥有百万人口的江户免于战火。西乡隆盛与幕府的胜海舟谈判，于5月实现江户城无血开城。但东北诸藩结成同盟，会津藩抵抗到最后；最令人难忘的一幕是：白虎队的少年们在山上望见城下浓烟，误以为城已陷落，集体自尽。

最后的抵抗者在海军军官榎本武扬率领下驶往北海道，在函馆宣布成立共和政权。1869年6月他们投降，新政府从此再无对手。

name.en: Ezo becomes Hokkaido: the Kaitakushi colonisation office
name.zh: 虾夷地改称北海道，设开拓使

summary.en: The Meiji government renamed Ezo "Hokkaido" in 1869 and created the Kaitakushi (Development Commission), which founded Sapporo, brought in American advisers and soldier-settlers, and opened Ainu lands to Japanese farming, fishing and mining.
summary.zh: 1869年，明治政府将虾夷地改称“北海道”，设立开拓使。开拓使建设札幌，聘请美国顾问，招募屯田兵，把阿伊努人的土地开放给和人农耕、捕鱼和采矿。

sources.title: Michele M. Mason, Dominant Narratives of Colonial Hokkaido and Imperial Japan (Palgrave Macmillan, 2012)
Richard Siddle, Race, Resistance and the Ainu of Japan (Routledge, 1996)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Hokkaido
Wikipedia: Hokkaido Development Commission

story.en:
The explorer Matsuura Takeshirō, who had travelled Ezo with Ainu guides in the 1840s and 1850s, proposed the new name; it was adopted in August 1869 as Hokkaido, the "northern sea circuit", modelled on the ancient circuits of the home islands. The government feared Russian expansion from Sakhalin and saw the island as empty land to be filled.

The Kaitakushi, led for most of its life by the Satsuma general Kuroda Kiyotaka, built Sapporo on a grid in 1871 and hired Americans, among them the former US agriculture commissioner Horace Capron and William S. Clark, who founded the Sapporo Agricultural College in 1876 and is remembered for "Boys, be ambitious". From 1875 tondenhei soldier-farmers settled the interior.

For the Ainu, colonisation meant the loss of land, rivers and deer. Salmon fishing and deer hunting were restricted, families were moved, and the 1899 Hokkaido Former Natives Protection Act pushed assimilation. Japan formally recognised the Ainu as an indigenous people only in 2008 and in law in 2019.
story.zh:
探险家松浦武四郎曾在1840至1850年代由阿伊努向导陪同遍游虾夷地，新名称正是他提出的。1869年8月，政府仿照古代的“五畿七道”，正式定名为“北海道”。政府担心俄国从库页岛南下，把这座岛视为有待填满的“空地”。

开拓使在其存续期间大多由萨摩出身的将领黑田清隆主持。1871年，开拓使按棋盘格规划建设札幌，并聘请美国人担任顾问，其中包括前美国农业部长霍勒斯·开普伦，以及1876年创办札幌农学校、以“少年们，要胸怀大志”一语闻名的威廉·克拉克。自1875年起，屯田兵在内陆开垦定居。

对阿伊努人而言，殖民意味着失去土地、河流和鹿群。捕捞鲑鱼和猎鹿受到限制，许多家庭被迫迁移，1899年的《北海道旧土人保护法》更推行同化政策。直到2008年日本国会才承认阿伊努人为原住民族，2019年才写入法律。

summary.en: About fifty senior officials led by Iwakura Tomomi, including Ōkubo Toshimichi, Kido Takayoshi and Itō Hirobumi, toured the United States and Europe for nearly two years to seek treaty revision and study Western institutions; their findings shaped Meiji reforms. Five girls, among them six-year-old Tsuda Umeko, went to study in America.
summary.zh: 以岩仓具视为首的约五十名高官，包括大久保利通、木户孝允和伊藤博文，历时近两年考察美国和欧洲，寻求修改条约并学习西方制度，其见闻深刻影响了明治改革。同行的还有五名赴美留学的女孩，其中包括年仅六岁的津田梅子。

sources.title: Kume Kunitake, Tokumei zenken taishi Bei-Ō kairan jikki (True Account of the Ambassador's Journey, 1878)
Ian Nish (ed.), The Iwakura Mission in America and Europe: A New Assessment (Japan Library, 1998)
Wikipedia: Iwakura Mission

story.en:
Less than four years after the Restoration, half of Japan's new leadership left the country. The Iwakura Mission sailed from Yokohama in December 1871 hoping to revise the unequal treaties. In Washington it learned that the Americans would not negotiate without full credentials, and Ōkubo and Itō had to sail home and back to fetch them, only to give up treaty revision in the end.

The mission became a study tour instead. Its members visited parliaments, schools, prisons, shipyards and the textile mills of Manchester and Glasgow; in Berlin Bismarck told them that international law served the strong and that a small nation had to build its own power. The historian Kume Kunitake recorded everything in a five-volume account published in 1878.

The travellers came home convinced that Japan was decades behind and needed industry, education and a strong state before foreign adventures. In 1873 they blocked Saigō Takamori's plan to send an expedition to Korea, a split that led to the Satsuma Rebellion four years later.
story.zh:
明治维新不到四年，新政府领导层的一半人就出国了。岩仓使节团于1871年12月从横滨起航，希望修改不平等条约。到了华盛顿，他们得知美方要求出示全权委任状才肯谈判，大久保利通和伊藤博文只得专程回国取来，最后却还是放弃了修约。

于是使节团变成了一次考察之旅。成员们参观议会、学校、监狱、造船厂以及曼彻斯特和格拉斯哥的纺织厂；在柏林，俾斯麦告诉他们，国际法为强者服务，小国必须建设自己的实力。史学家久米邦武把所见所闻全部记录下来，于1878年出版了五卷本的《特命全权大使美欧回览实记》。

归国的使节们深信日本落后西方数十年，必须先发展产业、教育和强大的国家，而不是对外冒险。1873年，他们阻止了西乡隆盛派使赴朝鲜的计划，这一分裂导致了四年后的西南战争。

summary.en: Disaffected Satsuma samurai led by Saigō Takamori rose against the Meiji government, besieged Kumamoto Castle and were driven back by a conscript army. Saigō died at Shiroyama in Kagoshima in September 1877, ending armed samurai resistance.
summary.zh: 心怀不满的萨摩士族在西乡隆盛率领下起兵反抗明治政府，围攻熊本城，后被征兵制新军击退。1877年9月西乡在鹿儿岛城山战死，士族的武装反抗就此终结。

sources.title: Mark Ravina, The Last Samurai: The Life and Battles of Saigō Takamori (Wiley, 2004)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Satsuma Rebellion
Wikipedia: Satsuma Rebellion

note: Wikidata's start year for this item is erroneous (2005); the rebellion ran from February to September 1877.

story.en:
Saigō Takamori had helped bring down the shogunate, but by 1873 he had left the government in anger after his plan to go to Korea, and perhaps provoke a war, was blocked. In Kagoshima he ran private schools for thousands of young samurai who had lost their stipends and, in 1876, the right to wear swords. When the government tried to remove arms from the Kagoshima arsenal in early 1877, his students seized it, and Saigō agreed to lead them north.

The rebels expected Kumamoto Castle to open its gates. Instead its conscript garrison held out for nearly two months, and at Tabaruzaka the two sides fought for seventeen days in the rain. Peasant soldiers with rifles defeated the samurai, and the government also used telegraphs, steamships and newly recruited police swordsmen.

Pursued through Kyushu, Saigō broke out at Enodake and returned to Kagoshima with a few hundred men. On 24 September, wounded at Shiroyama, he died, traditionally by asking a comrade to behead him. Pardoned in 1889, he became a national hero; his statue with his dog stands in Ueno Park.
story.zh:
西乡隆盛曾协助推翻幕府，但1873年他提出亲自出使朝鲜（或许意在挑起战争）的计划被否决，愤而辞官。在鹿儿岛，他开办私学，收容了数千名失去俸禄、并在1876年被禁止佩刀的青年士族。1877年初，政府打算运走鹿儿岛弹药库中的武器，私学校学生抢先占领了弹药库，西乡同意率领他们北上。

叛军原以为熊本城会开门迎接。然而由征召农民组成的守军坚守了近两个月；在田原坂，双方冒雨激战十七天。手持步枪的平民士兵击败了武士，政府还动用了电报、轮船和新招募的警视厅拔刀队。

西乡在九州各地被追击，后从可爱岳突围，带着几百人返回鹿儿岛。9月24日，他在城山负伤，据传请同伴为其介错而死。1889年他获得追赦，成为国民英雄；他牵着爱犬的铜像至今矗立在上野公园。

name.en: Ryūkyū Disposition: Japan annexes the kingdom
name.zh: 琉球处分：日本吞并琉球王国

summary.en: Japan made the Ryukyu Kingdom a "domain" in 1872, forbade its tribute to Qing China in 1875, and in 1879 sent police and troops to Shuri, deposed King Shō Tai and created Okinawa Prefecture. The Qing protested but never accepted a settlement.
summary.zh: 日本于1872年将琉球王国改为“琉球藩”，1875年禁止其向清朝朝贡，1879年派警察和军队进入首里，废黜国王尚泰，设立冲绳县。清朝提出抗议，但始终未能达成解决方案。

sources.title: George H. Kerr, Okinawa: The History of an Island People (Tuttle, 1958; rev. 2000)
Gregory Smits, Maritime Ryukyu, 1050–1650 (University of Hawaii Press, 2019)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ryukyu Islands: History
Wikipedia: Ryūkyū Disposition

story.en:
The new Meiji state wanted clear borders, and Ryukyu, tributary to China and secretly subordinate to Satsuma, did not fit. After sailors from Miyako were killed by Paiwan villagers on Taiwan in 1871, Tokyo claimed the right to protect them as Japanese subjects, sent a punitive expedition to Taiwan in 1874, and won a Qing payment that seemed to concede the point.

King Shō Tai's court stalled, petitioned and sent secret envoys to Beijing. In March 1879 the official Matsuda Michiyuki arrived at Shuri with about 160 police and 400 soldiers and read the order abolishing the domain. The king left the castle and was taken to Tokyo, where he lived as a peer until his death in 1901; Okinawa Prefecture was proclaimed on 4 April.

The former US president Ulysses Grant, then touring Asia, tried to mediate, and a treaty dividing the islands was drafted in 1880 but never signed. Ryukyuan aristocrats who fled to Fuzhou kept petitioning for restoration into the 1890s. Japan's victory over China in 1895 ended the question.
story.zh:
新成立的明治国家需要清晰的国界，而既向中国朝贡、又暗中从属于萨摩的琉球显得格格不入。1871年，宫古岛船员在台湾被排湾族村民杀害，东京宣称有权以日本臣民的身份保护他们，1874年出兵台湾，并从清朝获得一笔抚恤银，这似乎等于承认了日本的主张。

国王尚泰的朝廷一再拖延、请愿，并秘密遣使前往北京。1879年3月，官员松田道之带着约160名警察和400名士兵来到首里，宣读废藩命令。国王离开首里城，被带往东京，此后以华族身份生活，直到1901年去世；4月4日，冲绳县正式设立。

正在亚洲游历的美国前总统格兰特曾试图调停，1880年中日拟订了分割琉球群岛的条约，但最终没有签署。逃往福州的琉球士族直到1890年代仍在请愿复国。1895年日本在甲午战争中战胜清朝，这一问题也就随之终结。

summary.en: Drafted by Itō Hirobumi after studying Prussian and Austrian models, the constitution was granted by Emperor Meiji on 11 February 1889. It created an elected House of Representatives and a peers' house, but left sovereignty and command of the armed forces with the emperor. It was Asia's first modern constitution to take lasting effect.
summary.zh: 伊藤博文考察普鲁士和奥地利宪政后起草的宪法，于1889年2月11日由明治天皇钦定颁布。宪法设立民选的众议院和贵族院，但主权和统帅权仍归天皇。这是亚洲第一部长期实施的近代宪法。

sources.title: George Akita, Foundations of Constitutional Government in Modern Japan, 1868–1900 (Harvard University Press, 1967)
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)
National Diet Library: Birth of the Constitution of Japan, "The Constitution of the Empire of Japan"
Wikipedia: Meiji Constitution

story.en:
Popular movements had been demanding a parliament since the 1870s, and in 1881 the government promised one within ten years. Itō Hirobumi spent 1882 and 1883 in Europe, listening to the jurist Rudolf von Gneist in Berlin and Lorenz von Stein in Vienna, and came home convinced that Prussia's strong monarchy, not Britain's parliamentary rule, suited Japan. He drafted the text in secret with a few advisers, among them the German Hermann Roesler.

On 11 February 1889, the traditional founding day of the empire, Emperor Meiji handed the document to the prime minister in a new Western-style palace hall. That same morning the education minister Mori Arinori was stabbed by a nationalist who believed he had insulted the Ise shrine. The constitution was presented as a gift from a sacred and inviolable emperor.

The first Diet met in November 1890, elected by about one per cent of the population, men paying substantial tax. Its control of the budget forced governments to bargain with parties; but the emperor's direct command of the army and navy later let the military escape civilian control.
story.zh:
自1870年代起，民权运动一直要求开设国会，1881年政府承诺在十年内召开议会。伊藤博文于1882至1883年赴欧洲，在柏林听法学家格奈斯特讲学，在维也纳求教于施泰因，回国后确信适合日本的是普鲁士式的强大君权，而非英国式的议会政治。他与包括德国人罗斯勒在内的少数顾问秘密起草了宪法。

1889年2月11日，即传说中的建国纪念日，明治天皇在新落成的西式宫殿大厅里把宪法授予首相。同一天早上，文部大臣森有礼被一名民族主义者刺杀，凶手认为他亵渎了伊势神宫。宪法被表述为“神圣不可侵犯”的天皇赐予臣民的礼物。

第一届帝国议会于1890年11月召开，选民仅占人口约百分之一，均为缴纳较高税额的男子。议会对预算的控制权迫使政府与政党讨价还价；但天皇直接统帅陆海军的规定，后来使军部得以摆脱文官控制。

summary.en: Between the Hibiya riots of 1905 and the assassination of Prime Minister Inukai in 1932, mass protests, party cabinets and a lively press pushed Japan toward parliamentary rule. Hara Takashi formed the first full party cabinet in 1918 and men over 25 won the vote in 1925, the same year as the repressive Peace Preservation Law.
summary.zh: 从1905年日比谷骚乱到1932年首相犬养毅遇刺，群众抗议、政党内阁和活跃的报刊推动日本走向议会政治。1918年原敬组成第一个真正的政党内阁，1925年二十五岁以上男子获得选举权，同年却也通过了压制性的《治安维持法》。

sources.title: Andrew Gordon, Labor and Imperial Democracy in Prewar Japan (University of California Press, 1991)
Sharon A. Minichiello (ed.), Japan's Competing Modernities: Issues in Culture and Democracy, 1900–1930 (University of Hawaii Press, 1998)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Japan: The Taishō period
Wikipedia: Taishō democracy

note: Historians date the period variously, from 1905 or 1912 to 1925 or 1932.

story.en:
The era began in the streets. In September 1905 crowds furious at the meagre Treaty of Portsmouth burned police boxes around Hibiya Park in Tokyo; in 1913 demonstrators surrounded the Diet and brought down the Katsura cabinet; in 1918 rice riots spread to hundreds of towns. Each time, the oligarchs found they could no longer govern without the parties.

The political scientist Yoshino Sakuzō argued that government should serve the people's welfare, even under an emperor, and called it minpon-shugi. The journalist Hiratsuka Raichō launched the feminist magazine Seitō in 1911 with the line "In the beginning, woman was the sun". Labour unions, tenant farmers' associations and the Buraku liberation movement organised.

The gains were real but fragile. Hara Takashi, the first commoner to lead a party cabinet, was stabbed to death in 1921. Universal male suffrage in 1925 came with a Peace Preservation Law used against socialists, and after naval officers shot Prime Minister Inukai Tsuyoshi on 15 May 1932, no party politician led a government again until after the war.
story.zh:
这个时代始于街头。1905年9月，对《朴次茅斯条约》所得太少而愤怒的人群在东京日比谷公园一带焚烧派出所；1913年，示威者包围议会，迫使桂太郎内阁倒台；1918年，米骚动蔓延到数百个城镇。每一次，元老们都发现，没有政党已经无法执政。

政治学家吉野作造主张，即使在天皇之下，政治也应以民众福祉为本，他称之为“民本主义”。1911年，平冢雷鸟创办女性杂志《青鞜》，发刊词写道：“原始，女性是太阳。”工会、佃农组织和部落解放运动也纷纷组织起来。

这些成果真实却脆弱。第一位出身平民的政党内阁首相原敬于1921年被刺身亡。1925年实现男子普选的同时，也通过了用来镇压社会主义者的《治安维持法》。1932年5月15日海军军官枪杀首相犬养毅之后，直到战后都再没有政党政治家组阁。

summary.en: Japan's attacks on Pearl Harbor, Malaya and the Philippines in December 1941 widened its war in China into a war with the United States, Britain and the Netherlands. After rapid conquests, Japan was pushed back from Midway and Guadalcanal across the Pacific until the atomic bombings and Soviet entry forced surrender in August 1945.
summary.zh: 1941年12月，日本袭击珍珠港、马来亚和菲律宾，把侵华战争扩大为与美国、英国、荷兰的战争。日本在迅速扩张之后，自中途岛和瓜达尔卡纳尔岛起被逐步逼退，直到原子弹轰炸和苏联参战迫使其于1945年8月投降。

sources.title: John W. Dower, War Without Mercy: Race and Power in the Pacific War (Pantheon, 1986)
Ronald H. Spector, Eagle Against the Sun: The American War with Japan (Free Press, 1985)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: World War II: The Pacific War
Wikipedia: Pacific War

story.en:
Japan had been at war in China since 1937. When it moved into southern French Indochina in July 1941, the United States, Britain and the Netherlands froze its assets and cut off oil. The leadership chose war over withdrawal: on 7 December (8 December in Asia) carrier aircraft struck the US fleet at Pearl Harbor while armies landed in Malaya, Hong Kong and the Philippines.

For six months the advance seemed unstoppable. Singapore fell in February 1942 with some 80,000 British and imperial troops captured, and Japan proclaimed a "Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere". But at Midway in June it lost four fleet carriers in a day, and the six-month struggle for Guadalcanal bled its navy and air arm. American submarines strangled shipping; island garrisons fought almost to the last man at Tarawa, Saipan, Iwo Jima and Okinawa.

From late 1944 American bombers burned Japanese cities; a single raid on Tokyo on 9–10 March 1945 killed about 100,000 people. Some three million Japanese died in the war, and many millions more across Asia under occupation, forced labour and fighting. Emperor Hirohito announced surrender on 15 August 1945.
story.zh:
日本自1937年起已在中国进行全面战争。1941年7月日军进驻法属印度支那南部后，美国、英国和荷兰冻结日本资产并切断石油供应。日本领导层选择开战而不撤军：12月7日（亚洲时间8日），航母舰载机袭击珍珠港的美国舰队，同时陆军在马来亚、香港和菲律宾登陆。

此后半年，日军的推进似乎势不可挡。1942年2月新加坡陷落，约八万英国及英联邦官兵被俘，日本宣布建立“大东亚共荣圈”。但6月的中途岛海战中，日本一天之内损失四艘主力航母；长达半年的瓜达尔卡纳尔岛争夺战又耗尽了其海军和航空兵力。美国潜艇扼杀了日本的海上运输；塔拉瓦、塞班、硫磺岛和冲绳的守军几乎战至最后一人。

自1944年底起，美军轰炸机焚烧日本城市；1945年3月9日至10日对东京的一次空袭就造成约十万人死亡。约三百万日本人死于这场战争，而亚洲各地在占领、强迫劳动和战火中死去的人则多达数千万。1945年8月15日，昭和天皇宣布投降。

summary.en: From 1 April to late June 1945 US forces fought the Japanese 32nd Army for Okinawa in the largest amphibious assault of the Pacific War. Kamikaze attacks sank dozens of ships; more than 12,000 Americans, about 100,000 Japanese soldiers and a quarter or more of Okinawa's civilian population died.
summary.zh: 1945年4月1日至6月下旬，美军与日本第三十二军争夺冲绳，这是太平洋战争中规模最大的两栖作战。神风特攻击沉了数十艘舰船；一万二千多名美军、约十万日本军人以及冲绳四分之一以上的平民丧生。

sources.title: George Feifer, Tennozan: The Battle of Okinawa and the Atomic Bomb (Ticknor & Fields, 1992)
Okinawa Prefectural Peace Memorial Museum
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Okinawa
Wikipedia: Battle of Okinawa

note: Civilian deaths are estimated between about 94,000 and 150,000.

story.en:
The Americans landed on Okinawa's western beaches on Easter Sunday, 1 April 1945, almost unopposed. General Ushijima Mitsuru had pulled his army back into the limestone ridges and caves of the south, aiming not to win but to bleed the invaders and delay the attack on the home islands. For weeks the fighting on Kakazu Ridge, Sugar Loaf Hill and around Shuri, whose castle was destroyed, cost hundreds of lives a day, while waves of kamikaze planes struck the fleet offshore.

Okinawa's civilians were caught between the armies. Schoolgirls of the Himeyuri corps served as nurses in cave hospitals; families hid in caves where Japanese soldiers sometimes drove them out or killed them, and in places such as the Kerama Islands hundreds died in mass suicides after being told the Americans would torture them. Ushijima killed himself on about 22 June at Mabuni.

Okinawa remained under US rule until 1972 and still hosts most US bases in Japan. At Mabuni, the Cornerstone of Peace lists the names of more than 240,000 people of every nationality who died in the battle.
story.zh:
1945年4月1日复活节，美军在冲绳西海岸登陆，几乎未遇抵抗。牛岛满中将把部队撤到南部的石灰岩山脊和洞穴中，目的不是取胜，而是让进攻者流血，拖延对日本本土的进攻。此后数周，嘉数高地、“甜面包山”和首里一带的战斗每天夺去数百人的生命，首里城也被摧毁；与此同时，一波又一波的神风特攻机撞向海上的舰队。

冲绳平民被夹在两军之间。“姬百合学徒队”的女学生在洞穴医院中担任护士；躲在洞穴里的家庭有时被日军赶出或杀害；在庆良间群岛等地，民众被告知美军会施以酷刑，数百人在“集体自决”中死去。约6月22日，牛岛在摩文仁自杀。

冲绳此后一直处于美国统治之下，直到1972年，至今仍集中着驻日美军的大部分基地。在摩文仁，“和平之础”刻着在这场战役中死去的二十四万多名各国人士的名字。

summary.en: After the atomic bombings and the Soviet declaration of war, Emperor Hirohito broke the deadlock in his cabinet and accepted the Potsdam Declaration. His recorded broadcast on 15 August announced the surrender, and on 2 September Japanese representatives signed the instrument of surrender aboard USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay.
summary.zh: 在原子弹轰炸和苏联对日宣战之后，昭和天皇打破内阁僵局，接受《波茨坦公告》。8月15日播放的天皇录音宣布投降；9月2日，日本代表在东京湾的美国军舰“密苏里”号上签署投降书。

sources.title: Richard B. Frank, Downfall: The End of the Imperial Japanese Empire (Random House, 1999)
Tsuyoshi Hasegawa, Racing the Enemy: Stalin, Truman, and the Surrender of Japan (Harvard University Press, 2005)
US National Archives: Japanese Instrument of Surrender (1945)
Wikipedia: Surrender of Japan

story.en:
The Allies called on Japan to surrender unconditionally in the Potsdam Declaration of 26 July 1945. The government chose to "ignore" it. After Hiroshima on 6 August, the Soviet invasion of Manchuria on 9 August and the bombing of Nagasaki the same day, the Supreme War Council was still split three against three. Near midnight Prime Minister Suzuki Kantarō asked the emperor to decide, and Hirohito said the war must end.

On the night of 14 August he recorded a speech. Young army officers stormed the palace looking for the recording to stop the broadcast, but failed. At noon on 15 August millions heard their emperor's voice for the first time, in formal court language many could barely follow, telling them to "endure the unendurable". War Minister Anami Korechika had killed himself that morning.

On 2 September Foreign Minister Shigemitsu Mamoru and General Umezu Yoshijirō signed the instrument of surrender on the deck of USS Missouri, and General Douglas MacArthur signed as Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers. Fighting in Manchuria, Sakhalin and the Kurils went on for days after the broadcast.
story.zh:
1945年7月26日，盟国在《波茨坦公告》中要求日本无条件投降，日本政府决定对其“默杀”。8月6日广岛遭原子弹轰炸，8月9日苏联进攻中国东北，同日长崎遭到轰炸，最高战争指导会议却仍以三比三僵持不下。接近午夜时，首相铃木贯太郎请天皇裁决，昭和天皇表示必须结束战争。

8月14日夜，天皇录制了诏书。一批少壮陆军军官冲进皇宫，试图找到录音盘以阻止播出，但没有成功。8月15日正午，数百万日本人第一次听到天皇的声音，他以许多人难以听懂的宫廷文言，要求国民“忍所难忍”。陆军大臣阿南惟几已于当天早晨自杀。

9月2日，外务大臣重光葵和参谋总长梅津美治郎在“密苏里”号甲板上签署投降书，道格拉斯·麦克阿瑟以盟军最高司令官身份签字。天皇广播之后，中国东北、库页岛和千岛群岛的战斗仍持续了数日。

name.en: Postwar Constitution of Japan takes effect

summary.en: Drafted largely by the occupation's Government Section in February 1946 and passed by the Diet as an amendment of the Meiji Constitution, the new constitution made the emperor "the symbol of the State", vested sovereignty in the people, guaranteed rights including equality of the sexes, and in Article 9 renounced war. It has never been amended.
summary.zh: 新宪法主要由占领当局民政局于1946年2月起草，由帝国议会以修改明治宪法的形式通过。它规定天皇是“日本国的象征”，主权属于国民，保障包括男女平等在内的各项权利，并在第九条中宣布放弃战争。这部宪法至今从未修改。

sources.title: John W. Dower, Embracing Defeat: Japan in the Wake of World War II (Norton, 1999)
National Diet Library: Birth of the Constitution of Japan
Beate Sirota Gordon, The Only Woman in the Room: A Memoir (Kodansha, 1997)
Wikipedia: Constitution of Japan

story.en:
In early February 1946 a Japanese government committee produced a draft constitution that barely changed the Meiji text. MacArthur rejected it and ordered his Government Section to write a model in secret. About two dozen Americans, lawyers, soldiers and a few civilians, did it in nine days, working from three principles MacArthur had jotted down: the emperor at the head of the state but under the constitution, the renunciation of war, and the end of the peerage.

One of the drafters was Beate Sirota, a 22-year-old who had grown up in Tokyo and was one of very few in the room who spoke Japanese. She wrote the clauses on the equality of women in marriage and the family, which survive as Article 24. Japanese negotiators fought over the wording for a night and a day, then accepted the draft, which was revised and debated in the Diet through the summer.

Promulgated on 3 November 1946, it took effect on 3 May 1947, now Constitution Day. Article 9's renunciation of war and armed forces has been reinterpreted to allow the Self-Defense Forces, but proposals to amend it have so far failed.
story.zh:
1946年2月初，日本政府的一个委员会拟出一份宪法草案，与明治宪法几乎没有差别。麦克阿瑟否决了它，命令盟总民政局秘密起草一个范本。大约二十多名美国人，包括律师、军人和少数文职人员，在九天内完成了这项工作，依据的是麦克阿瑟随手写下的三项原则：天皇为国家元首但受宪法约束、放弃战争、废除华族制度。

起草者之一贝亚特·西罗塔年仅二十二岁，在东京长大，是房间里极少数懂日语的人。她撰写了婚姻和家庭中男女平等的条款，这些条款保留在今天的第二十四条中。日方谈判代表为措辞争执了一天一夜，最终接受草案；此后草案又在议会中经过整个夏天的修改和辩论。

宪法于1946年11月3日公布，1947年5月3日施行，这一天如今是宪法纪念日。第九条放弃战争和军队的规定经过重新解释，允许设立自卫队，但修改宪法的提议至今均未成功。

summary.en: Japan and 48 Allied nations signed a peace treaty that ended the occupation on 28 April 1952. Japan renounced Korea, Taiwan, the Kurils and southern Sakhalin, while Okinawa stayed under US administration. A US–Japan Security Treaty signed the same day kept American bases in Japan; the Soviet Union refused to sign and neither Chinese government was invited.
summary.zh: 日本与48个盟国签署和约，占领于1952年4月28日结束。日本放弃对朝鲜、台湾、千岛群岛和南库页岛的权利，冲绳则继续由美国管理。同日签署的《日美安全保障条约》使美军基地留驻日本；苏联拒绝签字，海峡两岸的中国政府均未受邀。

sources.title: John W. Dower, Embracing Defeat: Japan in the Wake of World War II (Norton, 1999)
Michael M. Yoshitsu, Japan and the San Francisco Peace Settlement (Columbia University Press, 1983)
United Nations Treaty Series vol. 136, no. 1832: Treaty of Peace with Japan
Wikipedia: Treaty of San Francisco

story.en:
By 1950 the Cold War and the Korean War had turned the occupation's purpose from remaking Japan to securing it as an ally. The American negotiator John Foster Dulles drafted a short, lenient treaty without heavy reparations, and Prime Minister Shigeru Yoshida accepted the price: American troops and bases would stay after independence.

The conference opened in the San Francisco Opera House in September 1951. The Soviet delegate Andrei Gromyko denounced the treaty and walked out with Poland and Czechoslovakia; neither Beijing nor Taipei was invited, and Korea, though a victim of Japanese rule, was excluded. Japan renounced its empire without the treaty saying who received Taiwan, the Kurils or small disputed islands, ambiguities behind several of today's territorial quarrels.

That afternoon, at an army base in the Presidio, Yoshida alone signed the Security Treaty with the United States. The two documents together, the peace and the alliance, became the frame of postwar Japan, often called the San Francisco system.
story.zh:
到1950年，冷战和朝鲜战争已把占领的目标从改造日本转为把日本巩固为盟友。美国谈判代表约翰·福斯特·杜勒斯起草了一份简短而宽大的和约，不要求巨额赔偿；首相吉田茂则接受了代价：独立后美军和基地将继续留驻日本。

和会于1951年9月在旧金山歌剧院开幕。苏联代表葛罗米柯谴责和约，并与波兰、捷克斯洛伐克一同退场；北京和台北都未受邀请，曾遭日本殖民统治的朝鲜半岛也被排除在外。日本放弃了帝国的领土，但和约并未写明台湾、千岛群岛以及若干小岛归属何方，这些含糊之处成为今天多起领土争端的根源。

当天下午，吉田茂独自在普雷西迪奥的一处陆军基地签署了《日美安全保障条约》。和约与同盟这两份文件共同构成了战后日本的基本框架，常被称为“旧金山体制”。

summary.en: From the mid-1950s to the oil shock of 1973 Japan's economy grew by around 10 per cent a year, driven by high investment, exports, cheap energy and Prime Minister Ikeda Hayato's Income Doubling Plan. By 1968 Japan had the second-largest economy in the capitalist world, at the cost of severe industrial pollution.
summary.zh: 从1950年代中期到1973年石油危机，日本经济年均增长约百分之十，动力来自高投资、出口、廉价能源以及池田勇人首相的“国民收入倍增计划”。到1968年，日本已成为资本主义世界第二大经济体，但也付出了严重工业污染的代价。

sources.title: Chalmers Johnson, MITI and the Japanese Miracle (Stanford University Press, 1982)
Andrew Gordon, A Modern History of Japan: From Tokugawa Times to the Present (Oxford University Press, 2003)
Wikipedia: Japanese economic miracle

story.en:
In 1956 the government's economic white paper declared that "the postwar era is over": Japan had recovered its prewar output, helped by American procurement for the Korean War. What came next astonished the world. Companies poured savings into new steel mills, shipyards and petrochemical plants on reclaimed coastlines; the Ministry of International Trade and Industry steered credit and technology licences; and workers left the farms for the factories of the Pacific belt.

In 1960, after huge protests over the renewal of the US security treaty, Prime Minister Ikeda Hayato changed the subject with a plan to double national income in ten years. It was achieved in seven. Families bought the "three sacred treasures" of television, washing machine and refrigerator, and later the "3 Cs" of car, colour television and air conditioner. The 1964 Tokyo Olympics and the first Shinkansen showed the new Japan to the world.

Growth had victims. Mercury poisoning at Minamata, cadmium poisoning in Toyama and asthma in Yokkaichi forced new pollution laws in 1970. The oil shock of 1973 ended the age of double-digit growth.
story.zh:
1956年，日本政府的《经济白皮书》宣布“已经不再是战后”：在朝鲜战争美军特需的帮助下，日本的产量已恢复到战前水平。接下来的发展令世界震惊。企业把储蓄投向填海造地建成的新钢铁厂、造船厂和石化工厂；通商产业省引导信贷和技术引进；工人则离开农村，涌入太平洋沿岸工业带的工厂。

1960年，围绕修订日美安保条约爆发了大规模抗议，此后首相池田勇人提出十年内国民收入翻一番的计划，转移了社会焦点。这一目标七年就实现了。家家户户买进电视机、洗衣机、电冰箱这“三种神器”，后来又追求汽车、彩电、空调这“3C”。1964年东京奥运会和首条新干线向世界展示了一个新日本。

增长也有受害者。水俣的汞中毒、富山的镉中毒和四日市的哮喘，迫使国会在1970年通过一系列公害法律。1973年的石油危机结束了两位数增长的时代。

summary.en: After 27 years of US administration, Okinawa returned to Japanese sovereignty on 15 May 1972 under an agreement between Prime Minister Satō Eisaku and President Nixon. The large American bases stayed, and Okinawa still hosts about 70 per cent of the land used exclusively by US forces in Japan.
summary.zh: 在美国管理27年之后，根据佐藤荣作首相与尼克松总统达成的协议，冲绳于1972年5月15日回归日本。庞大的美军基地被保留下来，至今冲绳仍集中着驻日美军专用设施用地的约百分之七十。

sources.title: Robert D. Eldridge, The Origins of the Bilateral Okinawa Problem (Garland, 2001)
Okinawa Prefectural Government: US Military Base Issues in Okinawa
Wikipedia: Okinawa Reversion Agreement

summary.en: At 5:46 a.m. on 17 January 1995 a magnitude 6.9 earthquake beneath Awaji Island and Kobe killed 6,434 people, toppled sections of the elevated Hanshin Expressway and destroyed over 100,000 buildings. The slow official response and the flood of volunteers changed Japanese disaster policy and civil society.
summary.zh: 1995年1月17日清晨5时46分，淡路岛和神户地下发生6.9级地震，造成6434人死亡，阪神高速公路高架桥部分倒塌，十余万栋建筑被毁。政府应对迟缓与志愿者的大量涌现，改变了日本的防灾政策和公民社会。

sources.title: Fire and Disaster Management Agency of Japan: final damage report on the Southern Hyōgo Prefecture earthquake (2006)
Kobe City: The Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake: Statistics and Restoration Progress
Wikipedia: Great Hanshin earthquake

summary.en: The tsunami that followed the Tōhoku earthquake flooded the Fukushima Daiichi plant, knocking out power and cooling. Three reactors melted down and hydrogen explosions wrecked their buildings. Rated level 7, the accident forced more than 150,000 people to evacuate and led to the shutdown of every reactor in Japan.
summary.zh: 东日本大地震引发的海啸淹没了福岛第一核电站，造成全厂断电、冷却失灵。三座反应堆堆芯熔毁，氢气爆炸摧毁了反应堆厂房。事故被定为国际核事件分级最高的7级，超过十五万人被迫疏散，日本所有核电站随后一度全部停运。

sources.title: IAEA, The Fukushima Daiichi Accident: Report by the Director General (2015)
National Diet of Japan Fukushima Nuclear Accident Independent Investigation Commission, Official Report (2012)
Wikipedia: Fukushima nuclear accident

story.en:
The earthquake on 11 March 2011 shut down Fukushima Daiichi's three operating reactors as designed. About fifty minutes later a tsunami some 14 metres high swept over the seawall, drowning the emergency diesel generators and electrical switchboards in the turbine basements. Without power the cooling pumps stopped, and in the dark control rooms operators read gauges by torchlight while improvising with fire engines and car batteries.

Over the next four days the fuel in Units 1, 2 and 3 melted; hydrogen built up and exploded in the buildings of Units 1, 3 and 4, scattering radioactive material across the farmland to the northwest. The government widened the evacuation zone step by step, and more than 150,000 people left their homes; many towns were still closed years later. The Diet's independent commission called the disaster "profoundly man-made", blaming regulators and the operator TEPCO for ignoring tsunami warnings.

All of Japan's reactors were shut for safety checks, and only some have restarted. The release of treated water from the site began in 2023, and removing the melted fuel is expected to take decades.
story.zh:
2011年3月11日的地震发生时，福岛第一核电站正在运行的三座反应堆按设计自动停堆。大约五十分钟后，约14米高的海啸越过防波堤，淹没了位于汽轮机厂房地下的应急柴油发电机和配电盘。失去电源后冷却泵停止运转；在漆黑的控制室里，操作员打着手电读取仪表，用消防车和汽车电瓶临时应急。

此后四天内，1、2、3号机组的燃料熔毁；氢气积聚，在1、3、4号机组厂房内发生爆炸，放射性物质飘落到西北方向的农田。政府一步步扩大疏散范围，超过十五万人离开家园，许多城镇多年后仍无法返回。国会独立调查委员会称这场灾难“显然是人祸”，指责监管机构和运营商东京电力公司无视海啸警告。

日本所有核电站都停运接受安全检查，此后只有部分重新启动。2023年开始向海洋排放处理水，而取出熔毁燃料预计需要数十年。

summary.en: The Silla minister Kim Dae-seong began rebuilding Bulguksa, "the temple of the Buddha land", near Gyeongju in 751, together with the Seokguram grotto above it. Its stone terraces, bridges and the pagodas Dabotap and Seokgatap are masterpieces of Unified Silla, and a sutra found in Seokgatap in 1966 is among the oldest surviving woodblock prints.
summary.zh: 新罗宰相金大城于751年开始在庆州附近重建佛国寺，同时营造其上方的石窟庵。寺中的石筑台基、石桥以及多宝塔和释迦塔是统一新罗艺术的杰作；1966年在释迦塔中发现的经卷，是现存最古老的雕版印刷品之一。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Seokguram Grotto and Bulguksa Temple
Iryeon, Samguk yusa (Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms, c. 1281), "Kim Dae-seong"
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Bulguksa
Wikipedia: Bulguksa

note: The Samguk yusa dates the rebuilding to 751 and says the state completed it after Kim Dae-seong died in 774; an earlier temple on the site is traditionally dated to 528.

story.en:
The Samguk yusa tells Kim Dae-seong's story as a parable of karma. Born poor, he gave his family's only field to a monk and died young; he was reborn into the house of a chief minister, and as an adult he built Bulguksa for the parents of his present life and the Seokguram grotto for the parents of his former one.

Whatever its origins, Bulguksa is a carefully planned vision of paradise. Visitors climb from the world of suffering to the Buddha's realm over stone stairways named the Blue Cloud and White Cloud bridges. In the courtyard of the main hall stand two pagodas: the ornate Dabotap, and the austere three-storey Seokgatap.

In 1966, while repairing Seokgatap after a theft attempt, workers found a printed scroll of the Mugujeonggwang Great Dharani Sutra sealed inside. It must have been printed before the pagoda was finished around 751, making it among the oldest woodblock prints known. Most of the temple's wooden halls burned during the Japanese invasion of 1593 and were rebuilt; the stonework is original.
story.zh:
《三国遗事》把金大城的故事讲成一则因果报应的寓言。他出身贫寒，把家中唯一的田地布施给僧人，后来早逝；转世投生到宰相家中，长大后为今生的父母修建佛国寺，又为前世的父母营造石窟庵。

无论缘起如何，佛国寺都是一个精心规划的极乐世界。参拜者沿着名为青云桥、白云桥的石阶，从苦难的尘世登上佛国。大雄殿前的庭院里矗立着两座石塔：华丽的多宝塔和简朴庄重的三层释迦塔。

1966年，在修复曾遭盗贼破坏的释迦塔时，工人在塔内发现了一卷封存的《无垢净光大陀罗尼经》印本。它必定印制于约751年石塔完工之前，因此是已知最古老的雕版印刷品之一。寺中的木构殿堂大多在1593年壬辰战争中被焚毁后重建，石构部分则是原物。

name.en: Jang Bogo founds the Cheonghaejin garrison

summary.en: Back from service in Tang China, Jang Bogo persuaded King Heungdeok to let him base 10,000 men on Wando island to stop pirates seizing Koreans for the slave trade. From Cheonghaejin he built a trading network linking Silla, the Korean communities of Shandong and Japan.
summary.zh: 在唐朝从军归来的张保皋说服新罗兴德王，允许他率一万人驻守莞岛，以阻止海盗掳掠新罗人贩卖为奴。他以清海镇为据点，建立起连接新罗、山东新罗人社区和日本的贸易网络。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Edwin O. Reischauer, Ennin's Travels in T'ang China (Ronald Press, 1955)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Cheonghaejin
Wikipedia: Cheonghaejin

story.en:
Jang Bogo was an islander of humble birth who went to Tang China as a young man and rose to junior command in the Wuning army in Xuzhou. In China he saw Koreans sold as slaves, carried off by pirates from Silla's coasts. Returning home, he told King Heungdeok in 828 that he could end the trade if given a base; the Samguk sagi says the king gave him 10,000 men and the title of commissioner of Cheonghae.

From his fortress on Wando, at the southwestern tip of the peninsula, Jang's fleet cleared the sea lanes and his agents ran a commerce in ceramics, silk and other goods between Shandong, Silla and Hakata. The Japanese monk Ennin, who travelled in China from 838 to 847, stayed at the Buddhist temple Jang had founded among the Silla community at Mount Chi in Shandong and relied on his men to get home.

Jang's power drew him into Silla's succession struggles; he helped put King Sinmu on the throne in 839. When the court refused to marry the next king to his daughter, an assassin, Yeom Jang, killed him, and in 851 the garrison was broken up and its people moved inland.
story.zh:
张保皋出身海岛，门第低微。他年轻时前往唐朝，在徐州武宁军中升至小将。在中国，他看到被海盗从新罗沿海掳来的同胞被卖为奴隶。828年回国后，他对兴德王说，只要给他一个据点，就能杜绝这种买卖。据《三国史记》记载，国王拨给他一万人，并授予他清海镇大使之职。

从半岛西南端莞岛上的城寨出发，张保皋的船队肃清了航道，他的部下经营着山东、新罗与博多之间的陶瓷、丝绸等货物贸易。838年至847年在中国游历的日本僧人圆仁，曾寄住在张保皋于山东赤山新罗人社区创建的法华院，回国时也依靠了他部下的帮助。

张保皋的权势把他卷入新罗的王位之争，839年他协助神武王登上王位。后来朝廷拒绝让下一任国王娶他的女儿，刺客阎长将他杀害。851年清海镇被撤废，居民被迁往内地。

summary.en: The Khitan Liao empire invaded Goryeo three times. In 993 the diplomat Seo Hui talked the invaders into withdrawing and won the lands south of the Yalu; in 1010–11 the Liao burned Kaesong; in 1018–19 General Gang Gam-chan destroyed the third invasion at Gwiju, and Goryeo kept its independence.
summary.zh: 契丹辽朝三次入侵高丽。993年外交家徐熙说服入侵者退兵，并取得鸭绿江以南的土地；1010至1011年辽军焚毁开京；1018至1019年姜邯赞在龟州歼灭第三次入侵的辽军，高丽得以保全独立。

label.en: Seo Hui negotiates with Xiao Sunning (993)

sources.title: Goryeosa (History of Goryeo, 1451)
Liao shi (History of Liao, 1344)
Michael C. Rogers, "The Chinese World Order in Its Transmutation: The Case of Chin and Koryŏ", in Morris Rossabi (ed.), China Among Equals (1983)
Wikipedia: Goryeo–Khitan War

note: Peace and Goryeo's acceptance of the Liao calendar followed in 1020–22 (Wikidata ends the war in 1022). Troop numbers in the Goryeosa are probably exaggerated.

story.en:
When a Khitan army under Xiao Sunning crossed the Yalu in 993 and demanded that Goryeo surrender, the court considered giving up its northern lands. The minister Seo Hui went to the Khitan camp instead. He argued that Goryeo was the heir of Goguryeo and could not open relations with the Liao while the Jurchen blocked the road between them; the Khitan withdrew, and Goryeo gained six garrisons south of the river.

The peace did not last. In 1010 the Liao emperor Shengzong himself invaded, and early in 1011 his troops burned Kaesong while the young King Hyeonjong fled south to Naju. In 1018 the general Xiao Paiya came again with about 100,000 men. The 71-year-old commander Gang Gam-chan, the Goryeosa says, dammed a stream near Heunghwajin with cowhides, released the water as the Khitan crossed, and harried them all the way toward Kaesong. In March 1019 he caught the retreating army at Gwiju and annihilated it; only a few thousand returned.

Goryeo afterward accepted the Liao calendar but kept its independence, and built a thousand-li wall across the north.
story.zh:
993年，萧逊宁率契丹大军越过鸭绿江，要求高丽投降，朝廷一度考虑割让北方土地。大臣徐熙却亲自前往契丹军营。他辩称高丽是高句丽的继承者，而女真阻隔两国道路，高丽无法与辽通好。契丹退兵，高丽还取得了鸭绿江以南的江东六州。

和平没有持续多久。1010年辽圣宗亲征，1011年初辽军焚毁开京，年轻的显宗南逃罗州。1018年，萧排押率约十万人再度来犯。据《高丽史》记载，七十一岁的统帅姜邯赞在兴化镇附近用牛皮堰塞溪流，待契丹军渡河时放水冲击，并一路追击至开京附近。1019年3月，他在龟州截住撤退的辽军，几乎全歼，生还者仅数千人。

此后高丽虽奉辽正朔，却保持了独立，并在北方修筑了千里长城。

name.en: Goryeo military coup and the Choe house
name.zh: 高丽武臣政变与崔氏政权

summary.en: Humiliated by civil officials, the general Jeong Jung-bu and his officers massacred courtiers during a royal outing at Bohyeonwon in 1170 and deposed King Uijong. A century of military rule followed, dominated from 1196 by four generations of the Choe family, until the court made peace with the Mongols in 1270.
summary.zh: 长期受文臣羞辱的将军郑仲夫等人，于1170年趁国王出游普贤院之机屠杀文臣，废黜毅宗。此后高丽进入长达百年的武臣统治时期，1196年起由崔氏家族四代把持，直到1270年朝廷与蒙古议和为止。

sources.title: Goryeosa (History of Goryeo, 1451)
Edward J. Shultz, Generals and Scholars: Military Rule in Medieval Korea (University of Hawaii Press, 2000)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Musin jeongbyeon (Military coup of 1170)
Wikipedia: Goryeo military regime

story.en:
Goryeo was a state of scholar-officials, and its generals ranked below them. The Goryeosa records the insults that piled up: a civil official set fire to the beard of the general Jeong Jung-bu at a court festival, and at another outing a young courtier slapped an elderly general in front of the king. In the autumn of 1170, during King Uijong's excursion to the Bohyeonwon pavilion, Jeong and his officers fell upon the civil officials and killed them; the king was exiled and later murdered.

The generals then fought one another for decades until Choe Chung-heon seized power in 1196. He and his descendants ruled through a private headquarters and bodyguards while keeping kings as figureheads. Choe's own slave Manjeok plotted a rising in 1198, reportedly asking, "Are generals and ministers born to their rank?"

The Choe house moved the court to Ganghwa Island to resist the Mongols, and it was under their rule that the Tripitaka Koreana was carved. After the last Choe dictator was killed in 1258, the court moved toward peace and returned to Kaesong in 1270.
story.zh:
高丽是一个由文臣主导的国家，武将的地位低于文臣。《高丽史》记载了日积月累的屈辱：一次宫廷节庆上，一名文臣烧了将军郑仲夫的胡须；另一次出游时，一名年轻文臣当着国王的面掌掴一位老将。1170年秋，毅宗出游普贤院，郑仲夫等武将突然袭击随行文臣，将其杀戮；毅宗被流放，后来遇害。

此后武将们互相争斗数十年，直到1196年崔忠献夺取大权。他和他的子孙通过私设的教定都监和家兵统治国家，国王只是傀儡。1198年，崔忠献的家奴万积密谋起事，据说他曾问：“王侯将相，宁有种乎？”

崔氏政权为抵抗蒙古把朝廷迁到江华岛，《高丽大藏经》正是在其统治下刻成的。1258年最后一位崔氏执政者被杀后，朝廷转向议和，并于1270年还都开京。

summary.en: When the Goryeo court made peace with the Mongols and returned to Kaesong in 1270, the Sambyeolcho elite troops refused to submit. Under Bae Jung-son they set up a rival king on Jindo island, then held out on Jeju until a Goryeo–Mongol force destroyed them in 1273.
summary.zh: 1270年高丽朝廷与蒙古议和并还都开京，精锐部队三别抄拒绝投降。他们在裴仲孙率领下于珍岛另立国王，后又退守济州岛，1273年被高丽与蒙古联军消灭。

label.zh: 济州缸坡头里最后抵抗

sources.title: Goryeosa (History of Goryeo, 1451)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Sambyeolcho
Wikipedia: Sambyeolcho Rebellion

summary.en: Ordered by King U and Choe Yeong to attack Ming Liaodong, General Yi Seong-gye halted on Wihwado island in the Yalu, turned his army around and seized Kaesong. The coup put power in his hands and led four years later to the founding of Joseon.
summary.zh: 奉禑王和崔莹之命进攻明朝辽东的李成桂，在鸭绿江中的威化岛停兵，回师攻占开京。这次政变使大权落入他手中，四年后他建立了朝鲜王朝。

sources.title: Goryeosa (History of Goryeo, 1451)
Joseon wangjo sillok (Veritable Records of the Joseon Dynasty)
John B. Duncan, The Origins of the Chosŏn Dynasty (University of Washington Press, 2000)
Wikipedia: Wihwado Retreat

story.en:
