In 1388 the Ming announced that it would take over the lands north of Cheollyeong in northeastern Korea, once ruled by the Mongols. The general Choe Yeong persuaded King U to answer with an invasion of Liaodong. Yi Seong-gye, the most successful commander of his generation, objected with four reasons that the Joseon records preserve: a small country should not attack a great one, summer was no time for war, the south would be left open to Japanese pirates, and in the monsoon bows would loosen and soldiers fall sick.

Overruled, he marched to the Yalu. Rain had swollen the river, and the army was stuck on the island of Wihwado as men deserted. Yi asked permission to withdraw; when it was refused, he turned the army around. Within weeks he had taken Kaesong, exiled Choe Yeong, and deposed King U.

Yi and his allies, Neo-Confucian reformers such as Jeong Do-jeon, then redistributed land and pushed aside the Goryeo aristocracy. In 1392 he took the throne himself.
story.zh:
1388年，明朝宣布要接管曾由蒙古统治的朝鲜东北铁岭以北之地。将军崔莹说服禑王以进攻辽东作为回应。李成桂是当时战功最显赫的将领，他提出了被朝鲜史书保存下来的“四不可”：以小逆大不可，夏月发兵不可，举国远征则倭寇乘虚而入不可，时值雨季弓弩胶解、士卒染疫不可。

他的意见被驳回，只得率军开到鸭绿江。雨水使江水暴涨，大军被困在威化岛上，士兵不断逃亡。李成桂请求撤兵未获准许，于是回师南下。数周之内，他攻占开京，流放崔莹，废黜禑王。

此后李成桂与郑道传等性理学改革派重新分配土地，排挤高丽旧贵族。1392年，他自己登上了王位。

name.en: Gyeongbokgung built in the new capital Hanyang

summary.en: After moving the capital from Kaesong to Hanyang in 1394, King Taejo completed the main palace in 1395; the minister Jeong Do-jeon named it Gyeongbokgung, "palace greatly blessed by heaven". Burned during the Japanese invasion of 1592, it lay in ruins until the regent Heungseon Daewongun rebuilt it in 1867.
summary.zh: 太祖李成桂于1394年把都城从开京迁到汉阳，1395年建成正宫，大臣郑道传为其命名为“景福宫”，意为“承天之大福”。1592年壬辰战争中宫殿被焚，此后长期荒废，直到1867年兴宣大院君将其重建。

sources.title: Joseon wangjo sillok (Veritable Records of the Joseon Dynasty)
Cultural Heritage Administration of Korea: Gyeongbokgung Palace
Wikipedia: Gyeongbokgung

summary.en: Under King Sejong, Joseon introduced a standard bronze rain gauge in 1441 and in 1442 ordered every county to measure rainfall with it and report to the capital, creating one of the earliest national rainfall records.
summary.zh: 世宗时期，朝鲜于1441年制成标准的铜制测雨器，1442年下令各郡县用它测量降雨并上报中央，形成了世界上最早的全国性降雨记录之一。

sources.title: Sejong sillok, entries for Sejong 23 (1441) and 24 (1442)
Joseph Needham et al., The Hall of Heavenly Records: Korean Astronomical Instruments and Clocks, 1380–1780 (Cambridge University Press, 1986)
Wikipedia: Cheugugi

note: The Sillok credits the crown prince (the future King Munjong) with the idea; popular tradition credits Jang Yeong-sil.

summary.en: After the Imjin War, Joseon and the Tokugawa shogunate restored relations through the Tsushima domain. Twelve Korean embassies of several hundred people each travelled to Edo between 1607 and 1811, drawing crowds and exchanging poetry, calligraphy and painting along the way.
summary.zh: 壬辰战争之后，朝鲜与德川幕府经对马藩恢复邦交。1607年至1811年间，朝鲜共派出十二次通信使，每次数百人前往江户，沿途观者如堵，双方以诗文、书法和绘画相互交流。

label.en: Audience with the shogun in Edo

sources.title: Ronald P. Toby, State and Diplomacy in Early Modern Japan (Princeton University Press, 1984)
UNESCO Memory of the World: Documents on Joseon Tongsinsa (2017)
Wikipedia: Joseon missions to Japan

story.en:
Less than a decade after Hideyoshi's armies left Korea, a Joseon embassy arrived in Edo. Its official purpose in 1607 was to answer a letter from the shogun and bring home Korean captives; the Tsushima domain, which lived on trade with Korea, had forged parts of the correspondence to make both sides appear to have taken the first step.

Over the next two centuries eleven more embassies made the months-long journey. With 300 to 500 members, musicians, painters, physicians and scholars among them, each was a moving festival. Domains along the route spent fortunes on banquets; crowds lined the Tōkaidō; Japanese scholars queued at the inns to exchange poems written in classical Chinese with the Korean secretaries. The Tsushima official Amenomori Hōshū, who spoke Korean, urged "sincere good faith" as the basis of diplomacy.

The last embassy, in 1811, went no further than Tsushima to save money. In 2017 records of the missions held in Korea and Japan were jointly inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World register.
story.zh:
丰臣秀吉的军队撤出朝鲜还不到十年，一个朝鲜使团就来到了江户。1607年使团的正式任务是回复将军的国书并带回被掳的朝鲜人；依靠对朝贸易为生的对马藩，曾篡改部分国书，好让双方都觉得是对方先迈出了第一步。

此后两百年间，又有十一个使团进行了历时数月的旅行。每个使团有三百到五百人，包括乐师、画员、医员和学者，堪称一场流动的盛会。沿途各藩不惜重金设宴款待，东海道两旁挤满围观人群；日本学者在驿馆前排队，与朝鲜书记官以汉诗唱和。通晓朝鲜语的对马藩儒者雨森芳洲主张以“诚信”作为外交之本。

为节省开支，最后一次通信使于1811年只到对马为止。2017年，韩日两国收藏的通信使记录共同列入联合国教科文组织《世界记忆名录》。

summary.en: A Later Jin army under Amin crossed the Yalu, defeated Joseon forces in the northwest and pushed toward Pyongyang; King Injo fled to Ganghwa Island. The peace made there bound Joseon to the Jurchen state as a "younger brother" while it kept its ties to the Ming.
summary.zh: 后金贝勒阿敏率军渡过鸭绿江，击败朝鲜西北的守军，逼近平壤，仁祖逃往江华岛。双方在江华岛议和，朝鲜与后金结为“兄弟之国”，但仍维持与明朝的关系。

sources.title: Joseon wangjo sillok (Veritable Records of the Joseon Dynasty)
JaHyun Kim Haboush, "Constructing the Center: The Ritual Controversy and the Search for a New Identity in Seventeenth-Century Korea", in Culture and the State in Late Chosŏn Korea (Harvard, 1999)
Wikipedia: Later Jin invasion of Joseon

name.en: Second Manchu invasion and the surrender at Samjeondo
name.zh: 丙子胡乱与三田渡之降

summary.en: After Joseon refused to recognise Hong Taiji as emperor, a Qing army crossed the frozen Yalu in December 1636. King Injo held out in Namhansanseong fortress for 47 days, then surrendered at Samjeondo, bowing nine times to Hong Taiji. Joseon became a Qing tributary and two princes were taken to Shenyang as hostages.
summary.zh: 朝鲜拒绝承认皇太极称帝后，清军于1636年12月踏冰渡过鸭绿江。仁祖在南汉山城坚守四十七天，随后在三田渡出降，向皇太极行三跪九叩之礼。朝鲜成为清朝的藩属，两位王子被押往沈阳为人质。

label.en: Qing army crosses the frozen Yalu

sources.title: Joseon wangjo sillok (Veritable Records of the Joseon Dynasty)
Na Man-gap, Byeongja rok (Record of the Byeongja Year)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Namhansanseong
Wikipedia: Qing invasion of Joseon

story.en:
In 1636 Hong Taiji renamed his state Qing and declared himself emperor. Joseon's envoys at his enthronement refused to bow, and in Seoul officials loyal to the Ming demanded war. In late December a Qing army of over 100,000 crossed the frozen Yalu and rode so fast that King Injo could not reach the island refuge of Ganghwa; he took shelter in the mountain fortress of Namhansanseong south of the capital with about 13,000 troops and little food.

Inside the walls, the court argued through the bitter winter. Kim Sang-heon insisted on resistance to the death; Choe Myeong-gil drafted the letters of surrender, which Kim tore up. Relief armies were beaten one by one, and when Ganghwa fell with the queen and princes in January, resistance became pointless.

On 24 February 1637 (30th of the first lunar month) Injo came down from the fortress in plain clothes and, at the ferry of Samjeondo on the Han, knelt three times and bowed his head to the ground nine times before Hong Taiji. Crown Prince Sohyeon and his brother went to Shenyang as hostages, and great numbers of Koreans were carried off as captives.
story.zh:
1636年，皇太极改国号为清，自称皇帝。在他的登基典礼上，朝鲜使臣拒绝下拜；在汉城，忠于明朝的官员纷纷主战。12月下旬，十余万清军踏冰渡过鸭绿江，行军极快，仁祖来不及逃往江华岛，只得率约一万三千名士兵躲进京城以南的南汉山城，城中存粮无几。

严冬中，朝廷在城内争论不休。金尚宪坚持死战到底；崔鸣吉起草降书，金尚宪将其撕毁。各路援军相继被击败，1637年1月江华岛连同王妃和王子一起陷落，抵抗已经没有意义。

1637年2月24日（正月三十日），仁祖身穿素服走出山城，在汉江边的三田渡向皇太极行三跪九叩之礼。昭显世子及其弟被押往沈阳为人质，大批朝鲜人被掳往北方。

summary.en: King Jeongjo built a new walled city at Suwon near the tomb of his father, Crown Prince Sado. Designed with help from the Silhak scholar Jeong Yak-yong, who devised a crane and pulleys, it was finished in under three years with paid labour and documented in a detailed illustrated report.
summary.zh: 正祖在其父思悼世子陵墓附近的水原修建新城。实学家丁若镛参与设计并发明了起重机和滑轮，城墙以雇佣劳力在不到三年内完工，工程过程被详细记录在附有插图的报告书中。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Hwaseong Fortress
Hwaseong seongyeok uigwe (Records of the Construction of Hwaseong Fortress, 1801)
Wikipedia: Hwaseong Fortress

story.en:
Jeongjo's father, Crown Prince Sado, had died in 1762 locked in a rice chest on the orders of his own father, King Yeongjo. When Jeongjo became king in 1776 he declared, "I am the son of Crown Prince Sado," and in 1789 moved his father's tomb to a hill near Suwon, relocating the town to a new site. The new city he planned there was both an act of filial piety and a base for royal power outside the factional capital.

Jeong Yak-yong, then a young official, drew on Chinese and Western books to plan its walls and engines. His geojunggi crane and pulley wheels let workers lift huge stones; the 5.7 km wall combined stone and brick, with gates, observation towers, gun bastions and a beacon tower. Labourers were paid wages rather than conscripted, and the work, begun in early 1794, was done by the autumn of 1796.

The court published the Hwaseong seongyeok uigwe, recording costs, tools, workers' names and drawings. After heavy damage in the Korean War, it allowed the fortress to be rebuilt accurately, and UNESCO inscribed it in 1997.
story.zh:
正祖的父亲思悼世子于1762年被其父英祖下令关进米柜而死。1776年正祖即位时宣布：“寡人乃思悼世子之子。”1789年，他将父亲的陵墓迁到水原附近的山上，并把水原城邑迁往新址。他在那里规划的新城，既是孝道的表达，也是在党争激烈的京城之外建立王权据点。

当时还是年轻官员的丁若镛参考中国和西方书籍，规划城墙和工程器械。他发明的举重机和滑轮使工人能够吊起巨石；全长5.7公里的城墙兼用石材和砖块，设有城门、敌台、炮楼和烽墩。劳工领取工钱而非被强征，工程于1794年初动工，1796年秋完成。

朝廷刊行了《华城城役仪轨》，记录了经费、工具、工匠姓名和图样。华城在朝鲜战争中严重受损，正是依靠这部仪轨才得以准确复原，1997年被列入世界遗产名录。

summary.en: Young reformers led by Kim Ok-gyun, hoping to copy the Meiji reforms, killed conservative ministers at the opening banquet of Seoul's new post office and seized the king with the help of Japanese legation guards. Qing troops under Yuan Shikai crushed the coup within three days.
summary.zh: 以金玉均为首、希望效法明治维新的青年开化派，在汉城新邮政局开局宴会上刺杀守旧派大臣，并在日本公使馆卫兵协助下挟持国王。三天之内，袁世凯率领的清军便镇压了政变。

sources.title: Bruce Cumings, Korea's Place in the Sun: A Modern History (Norton, 1997)
Kim Ok-gyun, Gapsin illok (Diary of 1884)
Wikipedia: Gapsin Coup

name.zh: 乙未事变（明成皇后遇害）

summary.en: Before dawn on 8 October 1895, Japanese soldiers and armed civilians organised by the Japanese minister Miura Gorō broke into Gyeongbokgung and murdered Queen Min (Empress Myeongseong), who had turned to Russia against Japan, and burned her body. The killing provoked "righteous army" uprisings and drove King Gojong to take refuge in the Russian legation.
summary.zh: 1895年10月8日黎明前，日本公使三浦梧楼策划的日本士兵和武装浪人闯入景福宫，杀害了联俄抗日的闵妃（明成皇后），并焚烧其遗体。此事激起各地义兵起义，并迫使高宗避入俄国公使馆。

sources.title: Peter Duus, The Abacus and the Sword: The Japanese Penetration of Korea, 1895–1910 (University of California Press, 1995)
Bruce Cumings, Korea's Place in the Sun: A Modern History (Norton, 1997)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Eulmi sabyeon
Wikipedia: Eulmi Incident

story.en:
After Japan defeated China in 1895, Queen Min, the most capable politician at the Joseon court, turned to Russia to balance Japanese power. Miura Gorō, a retired general newly appointed as Japan's minister in Seoul, decided to remove her. He recruited the queen's old enemy, the regent Heungseon Daewongun, as a figurehead, and assembled legation guards, Japanese police and sōshi, political toughs.

Before dawn on 8 October they entered Gyeongbokgung, overpowered the palace guard and burst into the queen's quarters in the Geoncheonggung compound. They killed her and several court ladies, then carried her body to a nearby grove and burned it. The American military adviser William Dye and the Russian architect Seredin-Sabatin witnessed parts of the attack, so the crime could not be hidden.

Japan recalled Miura and tried him and dozens of others in Hiroshima, but all were released for lack of evidence. In Korea the murder, followed by an order to cut off topknots, set off the first righteous army uprisings. In February 1896 King Gojong slipped out of the palace in a woman's palanquin and lived for a year in the Russian legation.
story.zh:
1895年日本在甲午战争中战胜中国后，朝鲜宫廷中最有手腕的政治家闵妃转而依靠俄国来牵制日本。刚被任命为驻汉城公使的退役将军三浦梧楼决定除掉她。他拉拢闵妃的宿敌兴宣大院君作为幌子，召集了公使馆卫兵、日本警察和被称为“壮士”的浪人。

10月8日黎明前，他们进入景福宫，制服宫廷卫队，冲进乾清宫内闵妃的寝殿，杀死了她和几名宫女，随后把她的遗体抬到附近的树林里焚烧。美国军事顾问戴伊和俄国建筑师萨巴丁目睹了部分经过，罪行因而无法掩盖。

日本召回三浦，并在广岛审判了他和数十名同伙，最终全部以证据不足为由释放。在朝鲜，这起谋杀加上随后的断发令，引发了最早的义兵起义。1896年2月，高宗乘坐宫女的轿子溜出王宫，在俄国公使馆住了一年。

name.en: An Jung-geun assassinates Itō Hirobumi at Harbin
name.zh: 安重根在哈尔滨刺杀伊藤博文

summary.en: The Korean independence fighter An Jung-geun shot Itō Hirobumi, the former Resident-General of Korea, on the platform of Harbin station. Tried by a Japanese court at Lüshun, An was executed in March 1910, leaving an unfinished essay on peace in East Asia; Japan annexed Korea five months later.
summary.zh: 朝鲜独立运动者安重根在哈尔滨火车站月台上枪杀前韩国统监伊藤博文。安重根在旅顺受日本法庭审判，1910年3月被处决，留下一篇未完成的《东洋和平论》；五个月后日本吞并朝鲜。

sources.title: Franklin Rausch, "The Harbin Assassination and the Unfinished Essay: An Jung-geun's Vision of Peace in East Asia", Korean Studies 36 (2012)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): An Jung-geun
Wikipedia: Assassination of Itō Hirobumi

story.en:
Itō Hirobumi had forced the 1905 protectorate treaty on Korea and served as its first Resident-General. In October 1909 he travelled to Harbin, in Russian-controlled Manchuria, to meet the Russian finance minister Kokovtsov. An Jung-geun, a 30-year-old Catholic from Hwanghae province who had fought with a righteous army in the Russian Far East, was waiting. Earlier that year he and eleven comrades had each cut off the top joint of a finger as a pledge.

At about 9.30 a.m. on 26 October, as Itō walked along the platform reviewing the honour guard, An stepped forward and fired three shots into him, then shot three other Japanese officials. He shouted "Korea, hurrah!" in Russian before being seized. Itō died within half an hour.

At his trial in Lüshun, An listed fifteen crimes he blamed on Itō, beginning with the murder of Queen Min. He spent his last weeks writing calligraphy, which his Japanese guards prized, and a treatise proposing a peaceful partnership of Korea, China and Japan. He was hanged on 26 March 1910; his remains have never been found.
story.zh:
伊藤博文曾强迫朝鲜签订1905年的保护条约，并担任首任韩国统监。1909年10月，他前往俄国控制下的中国东北城市哈尔滨，与俄国财政大臣科科夫佐夫会面。三十岁的安重根早已在此等候。他是黄海道出身的天主教徒，曾在俄国远东参加义兵作战；这一年早些时候，他和十一名同志各自断指为誓。

10月26日上午约9时30分，伊藤在月台上检阅仪仗队时，安重根上前向他连开三枪，又击中三名日本官员。被擒之前，他用俄语高呼“大韩万岁”。伊藤在半小时内死去。

在旅顺受审时，安重根列举了伊藤的十五条罪状，第一条就是杀害明成皇后。他在生命的最后几周写下许多书法作品，连看守他的日本人都视若珍宝；他还撰写文章，主张朝鲜、中国、日本和平合作。1910年3月26日，他被处以绞刑，遗骸至今下落不明。

name.en: Korean Provisional Government founded in Shanghai
name.zh: 大韩民国临时政府在上海成立

summary.en: Inspired by the March First Movement, Korean exiles proclaimed a Republic of Korea in the French Concession of Shanghai in April 1919, with Syngman Rhee as its first head. Driven inland by the Japanese war in China, the government moved through several cities to Chongqing, where it formed the Korean Liberation Army in 1940.
summary.zh: 受三一运动鼓舞，朝鲜流亡者于1919年4月在上海法租界宣布成立大韩民国，以李承晚为首任领导人。随着日本侵华战争的推进，临时政府辗转多地迁往重庆，并于1940年组建韩国光复军。

sources.title: Chong-sik Lee, The Politics of Korean Nationalism (University of California Press, 1963)
Encyclopedia of Korean Culture (Academy of Korean Studies): Daehan minguk imsi jeongbu
Wikipedia: Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea

note: Wikidata places this item at Seoul; the government sat in Shanghai and later in Chinese inland cities.

story.en:
Within weeks of the March First demonstrations, several rival governments-in-exile had been announced, in Seoul, in Vladivostok and in Shanghai. Delegates meeting in the French Concession of Shanghai on 10–11 April 1919 adopted a charter declaring Korea a democratic republic, and by September the groups had merged, with Syngman Rhee, then in the United States, as president.

The government was poor, divided between nationalists and communists and between advocates of diplomacy and armed struggle; Rhee himself was impeached in 1925. Its most dramatic act came in 1932, when Kim Gu's Korean Patriotic Organization sent Yun Bong-gil to throw a bomb at a Japanese victory celebration in Hongkou Park, killing General Shirakawa Yoshinori. Chiang Kai-shek's government began to support the exiles, and the Japanese hunted them from city to city.

In Chongqing in 1940 the government formed the Korean Liberation Army, but Japan surrendered before it could take part in an invasion of Korea, and its leaders returned home in late 1945 only as private individuals. South Korea's constitution still names it as the origin of the Republic.
story.zh:
三一示威爆发后的几周内，汉城、海参崴和上海相继宣布成立了几个互相竞争的流亡政府。1919年4月10日至11日，代表们在上海法租界开会，通过临时宪章，宣布朝鲜为民主共和国；到9月，各方合并，由当时身在美国的李承晚出任总统。

临时政府经费匮乏，内部在民族主义者与共产主义者之间、在外交路线与武装斗争之间争执不断；1925年李承晚本人也遭弹劾。最轰动的一次行动发生在1932年：金九领导的韩人爱国团派尹奉吉在虹口公园日军庆祝会上投掷炸弹，炸死白川义则大将。蒋介石政府开始支持流亡者，日本人则在一座又一座城市里追捕他们。

1940年，临时政府在重庆组建韩国光复军，但日本在其参与进攻朝鲜之前就投降了，其领导人1945年底只能以个人身份回国。韩国现行宪法仍把它列为大韩民国的法统源头。

name.en: Liberation and division of Korea at the 38th parallel
name.zh: 朝鲜光复与三八线分割

summary.en: As Japan surrendered in August 1945, two US officers proposed the 38th parallel as the line between Soviet and American occupation zones, and Moscow accepted. Plans for a joint trusteeship failed, and in 1948 separate states were founded: the Republic of Korea in Seoul on 15 August and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea in Pyongyang on 9 September.
summary.zh: 1945年8月日本投降之际，两名美国军官提议以北纬38度线划分苏美占领区，莫斯科予以接受。共同托管的计划破产后，1948年南北分别建国：8月15日大韩民国在汉城成立，9月9日朝鲜民主主义人民共和国在平壤成立。

sources.title: Bruce Cumings, Korea's Place in the Sun: A Modern History (Norton, 1997)
Bruce Cumings, The Origins of the Korean War, vol. 1 (Princeton University Press, 1981)
Dean Rusk, As I Saw It (Norton, 1990)
Wikipedia: Division of Korea

note: Wikidata dates the division from 1946; the occupation line was drawn in August 1945 and the two states founded in 1948.

story.en:
On the night of 10–11 August 1945, with the Soviet army already fighting in Manchuria, two young colonels in Washington, Dean Rusk and Charles Bonesteel, were given about half an hour to propose where American forces should accept the Japanese surrender in Korea. Looking at a National Geographic map, they chose the 38th parallel because it left Seoul in the American zone. To their surprise, Stalin agreed.

On 15 August, celebrated ever since as Liberation Day, Koreans poured into the streets. Soviet troops arrived in the north that month; Americans landed at Incheon only on 8 September. The two occupations went opposite ways: in the north the Soviets backed Kim Il-sung and a sweeping land reform, while in the south the US military government kept many colonial officials and police and clashed with left-wing people's committees.

The Moscow conference of December 1945 proposed a five-year trusteeship, which most Koreans rejected, and the US–Soviet joint commission broke down. Kim Gu crossed to Pyongyang in April 1948 to plead for unity, in vain. UN-supervised elections were held in the south alone in May 1948; by September there were two Korean states, each claiming the whole peninsula.
story.zh:
1945年8月10日至11日夜，苏军已在中国东北作战，华盛顿的两名年轻上校迪安·腊斯克和查尔斯·博恩斯蒂尔，被要求在大约半小时内提出美军在朝鲜受降的范围。他们看着一张《国家地理》地图，选定了北纬38度线，因为这条线可以把汉城划入美军区域。出乎他们意料，斯大林同意了。

8月15日，朝鲜人涌上街头庆祝，这一天此后一直作为光复节纪念。苏军当月就进入北方；美军直到9月8日才在仁川登陆。两个占领区走上了相反的道路：苏联在北方扶植金日成并推行彻底的土地改革；美军政厅在南方则留用了许多殖民时期的官员和警察，并与左翼的人民委员会发生冲突。

1945年12月的莫斯科会议提出五年托管方案，遭到大多数朝鲜人的反对；美苏联合委员会也宣告破裂。1948年4月，金九越过三八线前往平壤呼吁统一，但徒劳无功。1948年5月，联合国监督下的选举只在南方举行；到9月，半岛上已经出现两个都宣称代表全朝鲜的国家。

summary.en: On 3 April 1948 left-wing guerrillas on Jeju attacked police stations in protest against police brutality and the separate southern election. The counter-insurgency by police, army and right-wing youth groups burned hundreds of villages; by 1954 between 14,000 and 30,000 islanders had been killed. South Korea's government apologised in 2003.
summary.zh: 1948年4月3日，济州岛左翼游击队袭击警察局，抗议警察暴行和南方单独选举。警察、军队和右翼青年团的镇压行动焚毁数百个村庄；到1954年，约有一万四千至三万名岛民遇难。2003年韩国政府正式道歉。

sources.title: National Committee for Investigation of the Truth about the Jeju April Third Incident, The Jeju 4·3 Incident Investigation Report (2003)
Hun Joon Kim, The Massacres at Mt. Halla: Sixty Years of Truth Seeking in South Korea (Cornell University Press, 2014)
Wikipedia: Jeju uprising

note: The main killing took place in 1948–49; the area around Mount Halla was reopened only in 1954. Death toll estimates vary widely.

story.en:
Tension on Jeju began on 1 March 1947, when police fired into a crowd marking the anniversary of the March First Movement and killed six people. A general strike followed, and the US military government sent mainland police and members of the Northwest Youth League, refugees from the north with a hatred of communists, who beat and tortured islanders.

Before dawn on 3 April 1948, a few hundred guerrillas of the South Korean Workers' Party attacked police stations and the homes of right-wing figures. From late 1948, after the Republic was founded, the government declared martial law and ordered a scorched-earth campaign: villages in the mountain zone were burned and anyone found there could be shot as a rebel. Whole communities, including women, children and the old, were massacred, and others died in prisons on the mainland or in the summary executions of 1950.

For decades the killings could not be discussed. A government investigation in 2003 put the dead at between 25,000 and 30,000 by its estimate, and President Roh Moo-hyun apologised. The Jeju 4·3 Peace Park now records the names of the victims.
story.zh:
济州的紧张局势始于1947年3月1日：警察向纪念三一运动的人群开枪，打死六人。随后全岛总罢工，美军政厅从本土调来警察和“西北青年会”成员。后者是从北方逃来、仇视共产主义的难民，他们殴打、拷问岛民。

1948年4月3日黎明前，数百名南朝鲜劳动党游击队员袭击了警察局和右翼人士的住宅。1948年底，大韩民国成立后，政府宣布戒严，下令实行焦土作战：山区村庄被焚毁，凡在那里被发现的人都可能被当作叛乱者射杀。整个村落连同妇女、儿童和老人遭到屠杀，还有人死于本土的监狱或1950年的即决处刑。

几十年里，这段屠杀无人敢提。2003年政府调查报告估计死亡人数为两万五千至三万，卢武铉总统正式道歉。如今济州四·三和平公园镌刻着遇难者的名字。

summary.en: Protests against the rigged presidential election of March 1960 exploded after the body of a student killed by a tear-gas shell was found in Masan harbour. On 19 April police fired on crowds in Seoul, killing scores; after university professors joined the marches, President Syngman Rhee resigned on 26 April and went into exile.
summary.zh: 1960年3月总统选举舞弊引发抗议；一名被催泪弹打死的学生的遗体在马山港被发现后，抗议全面爆发。4月19日警察在汉城向人群开枪，造成数十人死亡；大学教授加入游行后，总统李承晚于4月26日辞职并流亡海外。

sources.title: Quee-Young Kim, The Fall of Syngman Rhee (Institute of East Asian Studies, Berkeley, 1983)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: April Revolution

story.en:
Syngman Rhee was 84 in 1960 and seeking a fourth term. His opponent died before the vote, so the real contest was for vice-president, and the ruling Liberal Party stuffed ballot boxes, voted in groups and intimidated voters on 15 March to win it. Students in the southern port of Masan protested that day and police fired on them.

On 11 April a fisherman found the body of Kim Ju-yul, a 17-year-old who had vanished during the protest, floating in Masan harbour with a tear-gas grenade lodged in his eye. Photographs of the corpse spread across the country. On 19 April more than 100,000 students and citizens marched on the presidential residence in Seoul; police opened fire, and across the country about 180 people were killed that week.

On 25 April some 250 university professors marched with a banner demanding that those responsible take responsibility. The army refused to fire on the crowds, the United States withdrew its support, and Rhee resigned the next day. He flew to Honolulu, where he died in 1965. The short-lived Second Republic that followed was overthrown by Park Chung-hee's coup in May 1961.
story.zh:
1960年，八十四岁的李承晚谋求第四个任期。他的竞选对手在投票前去世，真正的争夺集中在副总统一职上。3月15日，执政的自由党以塞票、编组投票和恐吓选民等手段赢得选举。当天南部港口马山的学生起来抗议，警察向他们开枪。

4月11日，一名渔民在马山港发现了抗议中失踪的十七岁学生金朱烈的遗体，一枚催泪弹嵌在他的眼睛里。遗体照片传遍全国。4月19日，十万多名学生和市民向汉城的总统官邸进发；警察开枪，那一周全国约有一百八十人死亡。

4月25日，约二百五十名大学教授打着要求追究责任的横幅上街游行。军队拒绝向人群开枪，美国撤回支持，李承晚于次日辞职。他飞往檀香山，1965年死于当地。随后短暂的第二共和国，在1961年5月被朴正熙的政变推翻。

summary.en: Major General Park Chung-hee and about 3,600 troops crossed the Han River bridges before dawn and seized Seoul, overthrowing the elected Second Republic. A military junta ruled until Park won the presidential election of 1963; he governed until his assassination in 1979.
summary.zh: 朴正熙少将率约三千六百名士兵于黎明前越过汉江大桥，占领汉城，推翻民选的第二共和国。军政府统治至1963年朴正熙当选总统，此后他一直执政到1979年遇刺。

sources.title: Byung-Kook Kim and Ezra F. Vogel (eds.), The Park Chung Hee Era: The Transformation of South Korea (Harvard University Press, 2011)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: May 16 coup

summary.en: When General Chun Doo-hwan extended martial law in May 1980, students in Gwangju protested and paratroopers responded with clubs, bayonets and gunfire. Citizens armed themselves and drove the army out, governing the city for five days until troops retook it on 27 May. Hundreds were killed; the uprising became the moral foundation of Korea's democracy movement.
summary.zh: 1980年5月全斗焕将军扩大戒严，光州学生起来抗议，空降部队以棍棒、刺刀和枪弹镇压。市民武装起来将军队逐出城外，自治五天，直到5月27日军队重新攻占城市。数百人遇难，这场起义成为韩国民主运动的道德基石。

sources.title: Lee Jae-eui, Kwangju Diary: Beyond Death, Beyond the Darkness of the Age (UCLA, 1999)
UNESCO Memory of the World: Human Rights Documentary Heritage 1980 Archives for the May 18th Democratic Uprising (2011)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kwangju uprising
Wikipedia: Gwangju Uprising

note: Official figures list about 165 civilians killed in May 1980 with dozens missing; other estimates are considerably higher.

story.en:
Park Chung-hee's assassination in October 1979 raised hopes of democracy, but General Chun Doo-hwan seized control of the army in December and, on 17 May 1980, extended martial law nationwide, closed the universities and arrested the opposition leader Kim Dae-jung, a native of the southwest.

Next morning students protested at the gates of Chonnam National University in Gwangju. Special forces paratroopers beat them and then bystanders with clubs and bayonets in the streets. As the violence grew, citizens joined in their thousands; taxi and bus drivers led a vehicle protest, and on 21 May troops fired on the crowd in front of the provincial office. People seized weapons from police stations, and by evening the army had withdrawn from the city.

For five days Gwangju governed itself through citizens' committees, with no looting reported, while the army sealed the city and the government's media called it a riot by communists. Before dawn on 27 May troops stormed the provincial office, killing its last defenders. Chun became president that summer. Sixteen years later he and his successor Roh Tae-woo were convicted of mutiny and treason, partly for Gwangju.
story.zh:
1979年10月朴正熙遇刺，民主化的希望随之升起。但全斗焕将军于12月掌握了军权，1980年5月17日又把戒严扩大到全国，关闭大学，并逮捕了出身西南地区的在野领袖金大中。

第二天上午，学生们在光州全南大学校门前抗议。特战司令部的空降兵用棍棒和刺刀殴打他们，随后又在街头殴打路人。暴力不断升级，成千上万的市民加入进来；出租车和公共汽车司机组织了车辆示威。5月21日，军队在道厅前向人群开枪。市民从派出所夺取武器，到傍晚军队已撤出市区。

此后五天，光州由市民委员会自治，没有发生抢劫，而军队封锁了城市，官方媒体称之为共产分子煽动的暴乱。5月27日黎明前，军队攻入道厅，杀害了最后的守卫者。全斗焕于当年夏天就任总统。十六年后，他和继任者卢泰愚以军事叛乱和内乱等罪名被判有罪，光州镇压正是罪状之一。

summary.en: After the death of a student under police torture and President Chun Doo-hwan's refusal to allow direct presidential elections, millions joined nationwide protests from 10 June 1987. On 29 June the ruling party candidate Roh Tae-woo accepted direct elections and civil liberties, opening the way to the constitution of the Sixth Republic.
summary.zh: 一名学生在警察酷刑下死亡，加之全斗焕总统拒绝实行总统直选，自1987年6月10日起数百万人参加了全国性抗议。6月29日，执政党候选人卢泰愚宣布接受总统直选并保障公民自由，为第六共和国宪法开辟了道路。

sources.title: Sunhyuk Kim, The Politics of Democratization in Korea: The Role of Civil Society (University of Pittsburgh Press, 2000)
Don Oberdorfer, The Two Koreas: A Contemporary History (Addison-Wesley, 1997)
Wikipedia: June Democratic Struggle

story.en:
In January 1987 police announced that Park Jong-chul, a Seoul National University student, had died during interrogation after an investigator "banged the desk and he collapsed". Doctors and a Catholic priests' group soon showed that he had been tortured with water. In April President Chun Doo-hwan declared that the constitution, which had the president chosen by an electoral college, would not be changed before he handed power to his chosen successor, Roh Tae-woo.

On 9 June Lee Han-yeol, a Yonsei University student, was struck in the head by a tear-gas canister; a photograph of him bleeding in a friend's arms became the movement's image. The next day rallies began in cities across the country. This time office workers in ties joined the students, applauding from windows and marching at lunchtime, and for nearly three weeks the protests grew.

With the 1988 Seoul Olympics approaching and the United States urging restraint, the regime gave way. On 29 June Roh announced direct presidential elections, an amnesty for Kim Dae-jung and press freedom. A new constitution was approved in October, and Roh won the December election when the opposition split.
story.zh:
1987年1月，警方宣布首尔大学学生朴钟哲在审讯中死亡，称审讯人员“一拍桌子，他就倒下了”。医生和天主教正义实现司祭团很快证明他是被水刑折磨致死的。4月，全斗焕总统宣布，在把权力交给他选定的继承人卢泰愚之前，不修改由选举人团选举总统的宪法。

6月9日，延世大学学生李韩烈头部被催泪弹击中；他满身是血倒在同学怀里的照片，成为这场运动的象征。第二天，全国各城市开始举行集会。这一次，系着领带的上班族也加入了学生的行列，他们在窗口鼓掌，在午休时间上街游行。近三周里，抗议规模不断扩大。

1988年汉城奥运会临近，美国也敦促克制，政权终于让步。6月29日，卢泰愚宣布实行总统直选、赦免金大中并保障新闻自由。10月新宪法经公民投票通过；12月的选举中，由于在野阵营分裂，卢泰愚当选总统。

summary.en: South Korean President Kim Dae-jung flew to Pyongyang and met Kim Jong-il, the first meeting of the two Koreas' leaders since the division. Their 15 June declaration led to family reunions, the Kaesong industrial zone and Kim Dae-jung's Nobel Peace Prize, though secret payments to the North later tarnished it.
summary.zh: 韩国总统金大中飞抵平壤与金正日会晤，这是南北分裂以来双方最高领导人的首次会面。双方发表的《六一五共同宣言》促成了离散家属团聚、开城工业园区，金大中也因此获得诺贝尔和平奖，但事后曝光的对朝秘密汇款使其蒙上阴影。

sources.title: Don Oberdorfer, The Two Koreas: A Contemporary History (Addison-Wesley, 1997)
Norwegian Nobel Committee: The Nobel Peace Prize 2000, Kim Dae-jung
Wikipedia: 2000 inter-Korean summit

story.en:
Kim Dae-jung had spent decades in prison, exile and house arrest, and had once been sentenced to death. As president from 1998 he pursued what he called the Sunshine Policy, arguing that engagement rather than pressure would change North Korea.

On 13 June 2000 his plane landed at Pyongyang's Sunan airport, and to everyone's surprise Kim Jong-il was waiting on the tarmac to greet him. Television across the South showed the two men holding hands and toasting each other, scenes almost unimaginable a few years earlier. Their joint declaration of 15 June promised reunions of separated families, economic cooperation and steps toward reunification "by the Korean people themselves".

In August, for the first time in decades, a hundred families from each side met their relatives in Seoul and Pyongyang. Kim Dae-jung received the Nobel Peace Prize that December. In 2003 investigators found that the Hyundai group had transferred hundreds of millions of dollars to the North with government help before the summit, and later nuclear tests strained the détente.
story.zh:
金大中曾在监狱、流亡和软禁中度过数十年，还一度被判处死刑。1998年就任总统后，他推行所谓的“阳光政策”，主张以接触而非施压来改变朝鲜。

2000年6月13日，他的专机降落在平壤顺安机场，出乎所有人意料，金正日亲自在停机坪上迎接。韩国各地的电视转播了两人手拉着手、互相举杯的画面，这在几年前几乎是无法想象的。6月15日发表的共同宣言承诺实现离散家属团聚、开展经济合作，并由“民族自主”推进统一。

8月，南北双方各一百个家庭在汉城和平壤与亲人重逢，这是几十年来的第一次。同年12月，金大中获得诺贝尔和平奖。2003年的调查发现，峰会之前现代集团曾在政府协助下向朝鲜汇款数亿美元；此后朝鲜的核试验也使缓和局面趋于紧张。
